docs.title: SafeRS Native Public API
docs.text:
This site documents the public scripting / plugin API, exposed in two mirror forms:

  • C++ — srs::api::*, for plugins compiled against OSRSClient.lib. Headers live in OSRSClient/PluginAPI/API/. Plugins implement IScript (OSRSClient/PluginAPI/IScript.h) and call API methods, passing the ScriptContext& they receive in onLoad / pulse / onTick / onDraw.
  • Lua — srs.*, for .lua scripts loaded by the in-process Lua VM. Bindings live in OSRSClient/ScriptEngine/ScriptAPI.cpp. The host builds the ScriptContext internally; scripts just call srs.<module>.<method>(args).

The two forms are at feature parity — every method documented here is callable from both C++ and Lua. Differences in shape (where unavoidable, e.g. Lua lacks pointer semantics) are called out per-method.

Threading and spoofing contract

All action-firing methods (interact, attack, click, cast, …) route through Interact on the engine main thread with always-on input spoofing. There is no escape hatch — calling DoAction from the render thread crashes, and the spoofer is fail-closed (if it can't inject, the action drops).

docs.title: C++ — IScript
docs.text:
class IScript {
public:
    virtual const char* name() const = 0;
    virtual bool onLoad(const ScriptContext& ctx) = 0;
    virtual void onUnload() = 0;

    virtual void pulse  (const ScriptContext& ctx) {}  // per frame (~60Hz)
    virtual void onTick (const ScriptContext& ctx) {}  // per game tick (~600ms)
    virtual void onDraw (const ScriptContext& ctx) {}  // per frame, inside ImGui frame

    virtual void onSettingsChanged(const nlohmann::json& settings) {}
    virtual nlohmann::json schema() const { return {}; }
};

Plugins export CreateScript / DestroyScript functions and ship as DLLs in the plugins/ directory.

To defer a one-shot to the next game tick from inside pulse, call ctx.tickScheduler->onNext(fn) — see nextTick / onNext below.

docs.title: Lua — callback registration
docs.text:
script.pulse(function() ... end)     -- per frame
script.onTick(function() ... end)    -- per game tick
script.nextTick(function() ... end)  -- one-shot, fires on the next tick only
script.draw(function() ... end)      -- per frame, inside ImGui frame

script.draw is the only callback where srs.draw.* calls are valid — the host guarantees a live ImGui frame for it. pulse, onTick, and nextTick do not.

docs.title: Metadata and settings
docs.text: The launcher's sidebar treats C++ plugins and Lua scripts uniformly — both can declare display metadata (name, author, version, description) and a settings schema that the launcher renders as an editable form.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Without a metadata declaration, a Lua script shows up in the sidebar under its filename stem with v * * "lua" and empty version / size. To override, call script.declareInfo once at the top level:

script.declareInfo {
    name        = "Power Miner",        -- overrides filename stem
    author      = "you",
    version     = "1.0.0",
    description = "Mines essence at Power-mine, drops at threshold.",
}

All fields are optional. C++ plugins set the equivalent fields via REGISTER_CORE_PLUGIN(...) (or external-plugin metadata) and the IScript::name() virtual.

docs.title: Settings schema
docs.text:
Both IScript::schema() and script.declareSettings accept the same shape — a list of groups, each with a list of rows. The launcher renders each row as a typed input (check, select, number, slider) and ships the user's edits back to the plugin / script.

script.declareSettings {
    groups = {
        { id = "general", title = "general", open = true, rows = {
            { id = "mode",      label = "Protect mode",   kind = "select",
              value = "Auto", options = { "Auto", "Magic", "Range", "Melee" } },
            { id = "lookahead", label = "Tick lookahead", kind = "number",
              value = 1, min = 0, max = 3 },
            { id = "smite",     label = "Use Smite",      kind = "check",
              value = false },
        }},
        { id = "display", title = "display", open = true, rows = {
            { id = "opacity",   label = "Overlay opacity", kind = "slider",
              value = 80, min = 0, max = 100 },
        }},
    },
}

The C++ equivalent returns the same JSON shape from IScript::schema():

nlohmann::json schema() const override {
    return nlohmann::json::parse(R"json({
        "groups": [
            { "id": "general", "title": "general", "open": true, "rows": [
                { "id": "mode", "label": "Protect mode", "kind": "select",
                  "value": "Auto",
                  "options": ["Auto", "Magic", "Range", "Melee"] }
            ]}
        ]
    })json");
}
kind Renders as Extra fields check checkbox value: bool select dropdown value, options: [...] number numeric input value, min, max slider slider value, min, max

Without a declareSettings / schema() call, the sidebar shows just the master enable toggle and no rows.

docs.title: Reading values
docs.text:
User edits are flattened by the launcher to "<groupId>.<rowId>" keys before crossing the IPC boundary, so a script reads its own setting under that combined key:

script.onSettingsChanged(function(s)
    print("protect mode:", s["general.mode"])
    print("smite on:",     s["general.smite"])
end)

-- Snapshot read at call time:
local s = script.settings()
if s["general.smite"] then ... end

The C++ onSettingsChanged(const nlohmann::json&) receives the same flat-keyed object. The launcher pushes the current values to the plugin / script on enable, on every edit, and after a hot reload — handlers should be idempotent.

Identity

A script's settings are persisted by the launcher under the script's id, derived from the filename stem. Renaming the .lua file orphans its saved values. Pick a name you're willing to keep, and avoid renaming group / row ids in the schema between releases for the same reason.

docs.title: pulse vs onTick
docs.text:
Callback Cadence Use for pulse every rendered frame (~60 Hz) cheap state checks, per-frame visual work onTick every game tick (~600 ms) action firing, state-machine transitions

Move action logic to onTick and use pulse only for checks.

docs.title: nextTick / onNext
docs.text:
nextTick (Lua) / tickScheduler->onNext (C++) bridge fast pulse detection to server-aligned firing: evaluate a condition inside pulse (~60Hz so you don't miss a short-lived window), and when it fires, queue a closure to run on the very next game tick, then drop it.

Each call queues exactly one callback. The host drains the queue once per tick after the regular onTick fan, so steady-state tick handlers always run first. A re-queue from inside a deferred callback lands on the next tick, not this one.

Property Behavior Cadence one-shot — fires on the next tick rollover, then dropped Order after onTick, before the BreakManager scheduler Pause / disable owning plugin/script disabled or paused before drain → callback is silently dropped (same gating as pulse / onTick) Re-entrancy onNext called from inside a deferred fn schedules for the NEXT tick ImGui frame not guaranteed — call srs.draw.* only from script.draw / onDraw

When to use each:

  • Always firing every tick? Use onTick.
  • Need fast detection (a projectile, a hitsplat, a tick-aligned animation start) but the action itself must land aligned to the server? Detect in pulse, defer with nextTick / onNext.
  • Per-frame visual work? Use pulse (state) + draw / onDraw (paint).

docs.title: Lua example
docs.text:
-- Detect the "tick-eat" window in pulse (need ≥60Hz to catch it),
-- then fire the eat exactly once on the next tick.
local pending = false
script.pulse(function()
    if not pending and srs.player.hpPercent() < 35 then
        pending = true
        script.nextTick(function()
            srs.inventory.interact("Shark", "Eat")
            pending = false
        end)
    end
end)

docs.title: C++ example
docs.text:
void pulse(const ScriptContext& ctx) override {
    using namespace srs::api;
    if (!m_pending && Player::hpPercent(ctx) < 35) {
        m_pending = true;
        ctx.tickScheduler->onNext([this, &ctx]{
            Inventory::interact(ctx, "Shark", "Eat");
            m_pending = false;
        });
    }
}

The m_pending flag prevents queueing the same action 36× across the ~600 ms tick window before nextTick actually fires. Without it, every pulse between detection and the next tick would push another copy of the closure onto the queue.

Lifetime of captured pointers

ScriptContext references stay valid for the lifetime of the enabled plugin/script. Capturing ctx by reference in a closure is safe because the deferred callback is dropped if the owning plugin/script is disabled before the drain runs. Do not capture raw pointers into game-state nodes that may rotate between ticks (e.g. an NpcInstance* from EntityQuery) — re-resolve from ctx inside the closure body.

docs.title: Example — minimal Lua script
docs.text:
-- Drop every shrimp the moment it lands in the backpack.
script.onTick(function()
    if srs.inventory.contains("Shrimps") then
        srs.inventory.dropAll("Shrimps")
    end
end)

script.draw(function()
    if srs.draw.beginAnchoredOverlay(
            "##fish-hud", 162, 32,
            srs.Corner.TopRight, -4, 4) then
        srs.draw.text("Caught: " .. srs.inventory.count("Shrimps"))
        srs.draw.endOverlay()
    end
end)

docs.title: Example — minimal C++ plugin
docs.text:
class FishingPlugin : public IScript {
public:
    const char* name() const override { return "Fishing"; }
    bool onLoad(const ScriptContext&) override { return true; }
    void onUnload() override {}

    void onTick(const ScriptContext& ctx) override {
        using namespace srs::api;
        if (Inventory::contains(ctx, "Shrimps")) {
            Inventory::dropAll(ctx, "Shrimps");
        }
    }

    void onDraw(const ScriptContext& ctx) override {
        using namespace srs::api;
        if (Drawing::beginAnchoredOverlay(ctx, "##fish-hud",
                                          162, 32,
                                          Drawing::Corner::TopRight,
                                          -4, 4)) {
            Drawing::text("Caught: " + std::to_string(
                Inventory::count(ctx, std::string("Shrimps"))));
            Drawing::endOverlay();
        }
    }
};

extern "C" __declspec(dllexport) IScript* CreateScript()  { return new FishingPlugin(); }
extern "C" __declspec(dllexport) void DestroyScript(IScript* s) { delete s; }

docs.title: Alternative Pathfinder — Devious-Client Port: Audit + Design Spec
docs.text: Date: 2026-07-02 Source audited: C:\Users\Mekkon\Downloads\devious-client-master — net.unethicalite.api.movement (RuneLite fork, "unethicalite"/devious-client) Goal: Add the devious pathfinder as a second, selectable path engine. Both engines stay available behind the existing executor until head-to-head testing picks a winner. Zero changes to any existing srs::api::Walk exported symbol or Lua binding.

docs.title: Part 1 — Audit of the devious-client pathfinder
1.1 Search core (Pathfinder.java)
docs.text:
Property Devious SafeRS StaticPathfinder (current) Algorithm Unweighted BFS (FIFO, no heuristic) Dual-queue A* (boundary + pending transport queue), Chebyshev heuristic w/ underground y-wrap Cost model Uniform 1/tile; transports free; gold tracked ad-hoc for charter ships 1/tile walk, duration ticks per transport, teleport seeding penalty Queue LinkedList.remove(0) — O(V²) worst case Proper priority queues Visited set HashSet<WorldPoint> (boxed objects, GC-heavy) Packed-int arena Cap 5,000,000 visited Progress-reset time budget (5000 ms) Failed-edge memory None Session blacklist (excludedEdges) Cross-plane goal Implicit (transports carry plane) Explicit goalPlane plumbing (WS-I1) Partial-path result None (null on failure) Best-progress partial + found=false

Verdict on the core: the devious search core is older and weaker than what we already ship. Our StaticPathfinder is a newer Skretzo/Microbot lineage port with a cost model, budget discipline, failure memory, and plane plumbing that devious lacks. Porting the BFS verbatim would be a downgrade. What devious does differently is everything around the search — but note the scoping below: several of those items are already on our own roadmap, so they are reference material for planned work, not engine differentiators.

docs.title: 1.2 What devious does differently — differentiators vs roadmap accelerants
docs.text:
True engine differentiators (what the A/B test actually decides):

  1. Live-overlay collision with doors-as-open (GlobalCollisionMap.withLocalCollisions() + RegionManager.getTileFlags(), RegionManager.java:313-412). Before searching, devious copies the global static map and overlays the live scene: spawned/despawned objects, wall flags, and — critically — any edge carrying a door with an "Open" action that is not a catalog transport gets its block flag subtracted (RegionManager.java:393-402). The planner paths straight through closed doors; the walker opens them on contact (Walker.handleTransports() diagonal + cardinal door checks, Walker.java:329-379). This is the inverse of our philosophy (static map + execution-time door probe, WS-D1) and directly attacks our known static-vs-live divergence class (project_collision_static_vs_live): cache-vs-live spawned locs and open door-edges without a transports.tsv row.

  2. Event-driven path invalidation (RegionManager subscriptions). Varbit/item-container/widget events set a REFRESH_PATH flag; transportsChanged()/teleportsChanged() diff the transport/teleport sets restricted to the current path and only recalc when something on the route actually changed. Cheaper and more precise than timer-based recalc.

  3. An independent transport dataset (transports.json, 5056 rows verified on disk: source, destination, action, objectId, requirements{quest/item/skill/var/world}; 71 quest, 86 item, 180 skill, 167 world, 243 var requirement uses). Clean JSON schema; maps 1:1 onto our PathfinderConfig account-snapshot evaluation. Running each engine on its own dataset lets the A/B surface data-quality gaps in either catalog.

Roadmap accelerants — NOT engine differentiators. These looked like devious advantages on first read, but they are already planned for our current implementation (June audit roadmap) and live in the shared executor, so whichever engine wins gets them; they must be excluded from the A/B comparison:

  1. Transport verb coverage via a handler model (TransportLoader.java, 921 lines). Every transport is {source, destination, radii, Runnable handler, Requirements}: object click, NPC interact, NPC-dialog chains, item-use-on-object, fairy-ring dialing, glider/spirit-tree/charter widgets. This is exactly our planned WS-H2 (per-type handler table, fairy rings → NPC boats → spirit trees). Devious's per-category interaction recipes are reference material for that work — executed our way (packets, not widget clicks) — not something the devious engine uniquely provides.

  2. POH teleport layer (TeleportLoader.java POH sections + poh/*.java). Mounted glory/digsite/xeric/mythical cape, jewellery box tiers, portal nexus (varbit-scanned 6672-10103 → HousePortal enum, 30 destinations), house portals. Already planned as Phase 4 POH integration in the June audit roadmap. Devious's varbit maps and destination tables shortcut the data-collection part of that phase; the seeding/execution lands in shared infrastructure both engines consume.

docs.title: 1.3 Collision data compatibility (important)
docs.text: Devious's /regions resource (657 KB gzip) is a sparse region map of BitSet4D[64][64][4][2] — 2 bits per tile: walk-north, walk-east, south/west derived from neighbors. This is the same encoding family as our FlagMap/SCM1 collision-map.bin (both descend from Skretzo's data). Consequence: the new engine can consume our existing StaticCollisionMap unchanged — no second collision dataset needed. Optionally, a one-off converter (devious /regions → SCM1) gives us a second dataset for divergence testing, but it is not on the critical path.

docs.title: 1.4 Flaws found in the devious source (do NOT port)
docs.text:
• LinkedList.remove(0) BFS queue — O(V²); replace with ring buffer.
  • HashSet<WorldPoint> visited — replace with packed-key bitset/arena.
  • Hardcoded NPC/item/widget IDs sprinkled through 900-line TransportLoader switch — brittle across game updates; we keep transports data-driven (TSV/JSON) instead.
  • Gold-cost tracking bolted onto the node struct just for charter ships — model as a currency requirement instead.
  • Reachable.isWalkable() re-floods per call (we already fixed this class with the per-tick cached flood, WS-B3).
  • Wilderness areas hardcoded as WorldAreas in MovementConstants.
  • LocalCollisionMap.blockDoors dead parameter; writeToFile() dead code.
  • Sleeps, widget click chains, camera fiddling in Walker/Movement — superseded by our packet verbs (feedback_packet_path_default, feedback_input_method_priority).
  • Threading trap: devious queries live client state mid-search (LocalCollisionMap → Reachable.getCollisionFlag). Our searches run on a detached worker thread that must never touch engine memory → the live overlay must be snapshotted on the render thread before dispatch (same pattern as refreshUsableTeleports / account snapshot, PathfinderConfig.h threading note).

docs.title: 1.5 Licensing
docs.text: BSD 2-Clause (RuneLite base license, inherited by the fork; no per-file headers in the movement package). Compatible with our closed-source distribution: retain the copyright notice + license text in a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry (same treatment as the Skretzo/Microbot-derived collision code). No copyleft obligations.

docs.title: 1.6 External dependencies of the ported code
docs.text:
All local — no remote/unethicalite server calls anywhere in the movement package (verified: RegionManager is config + event glue only). Client-state needs, with our equivalents:

Devious dependency SafeRS equivalent client.getCollisionMaps() GameSDK/CollisionMap (live snapshot) Vars.getBit/getVarp VarpSystem Quests.getState Quest varbit tables → CS2 QUEST_STATUS_GET=4029 (TTL-cached) Inventory/Equipment Account snapshot + BankCache Skills.getBoostedLevel Account snapshot TileObjects.* ObjectQuery Dialog.* Resume*Dialog wire packets (P2GR catalog) Widgets.* IfButton/IfSubOp packets Worlds.inMembersWorld GS+0x21A8 members byte Game.getWildyLevel coord-derived wilderness level (WS-E5)

docs.title: 2.1 Constraints (verified 2026-07-02)
docs.text:
• Frozen surface: srs::api::Walk exported symbols (Walk.h — to 4-arg + 5-arg overloads, state, arrivalDistance, findSafeTile, walkSmart, fastCanvas, cancel, isMoving, hasArrived) and Lua names (game.moveTo/minimapWalkTo/walkTo/walkFastCanvas/walkSmart/cancelWalk/isWalking/hasArrived/walkState). Evolution rule: add overloads / new symbols only (feedback_api_abi_overload_not_default).
  • PathExecutor internals are NOT ABI: ExternalPlugins/include/PluginAPI/IScript.h:31 holds PathExecutor* as an opaque forward declaration; PathExecutor.h does not ship in the SDK. Internal members/methods may be added freely.
  • The producer contract is PathResult (Pathfinder.h:60): path, rawPath, found, cost, nodesExplored, transports[] (PathTransportEdge). Any engine that emits a correct PathResult gets the entire existing executor for free: click dispatch, transport firing, stall recovery, failed-edge memory, run management, telemetry.
  • Worker-thread searches must not read engine memory. All live state is snapshotted on the render thread pre-dispatch.

docs.title: 2.2 Architecture: engine seam behind the existing executor
docs.text:
One executor, two path producers. We do not build a second walker — the 2,926-line PathExecutor state machine (stall recovery, transport firing, run energy, telemetry) is engine-agnostic already; only path production differs.

                       ┌─ PathEngine::Static (adapter → existing StaticPathfinder, UNTOUCHED)
walkTo(goal, opts) ────┤
                       └─ PathEngine::Devious (new: overlay snapshot + BFS + devious graph)
                                  │
                    both emit PathResult{path, transports[]}
                                  │
                       PathExecutor (existing tick loop, unchanged behavior)

docs.title: New interface (new file Pathfinding/IPathEngine.h)
docs.text:
struct PathRequest {
    int startX, startY, startPlane;
    int goalX, goalY, goalPlane;          // goalPlane -1 = start plane
    bool useTransports;
    int budgetMs;
    const std::atomic<bool>* cancelFlag;
    const std::unordered_set<int64_t>* excludedEdges;    // failed-edge memory
    const std::unordered_set<int64_t>* blockedWalkEdges; // quest-locked steps
};

class IPathEngine {
public:
    virtual ~IPathEngine() = default;
    virtual PathResult findPath(const PathRequest&) const = 0;
    virtual const char* name() const = 0;    // "static" / "devious" — telemetry key
    // Render-thread hook, called by dllmain's onGameTick BEFORE any dispatch
    // this tick. Engines snapshot live state here (scene overlay, teleport
    // usability). Static engine: no-op (uses existing refreshUsableTeleports).
    virtual void refreshSnapshot() {}
};
  • StaticPathEngine — ~30-line adapter that forwards PathRequest to the existing StaticPathfinder::findPath(...) signature. StaticPathfinder.h/.cpp are not modified.
  • DeviousPathEngine — the port (see 2.4).

docs.title: PathExecutor changes (internal, additive only)
docs.text:
• dispatchStaticPathfinder(...) (PathExecutor.cpp:383) generalizes to dispatchPathfinder(const IPathEngine& engine, ...) — same worker-thread + promise/future + cancel-flag + snapshot pattern, engine call swapped in at PathExecutor.cpp:414. Existing call sites (initial dispatch :255, recalc :373, lookahead :1381) route through the executor's current engine pointer.
  • New appended members: const IPathEngine* m_engineStatic; const IPathEngine* m_engineDevious; const IPathEngine* m_activeEngine; + setEngines(...) late-bind (same pattern as setObjectQuery).
  • New walkTo overload (internal class — overload only for symmetry, not ABI): walkTo(goalX, goalY, useTransports, mode, goalPlane, EngineSelect engine) where EngineSelect { Default, Static, Devious }. Default = the session-level engine set by config/debug panel. Existing 5-param walkTo keeps its exact signature and forwards with Default — all current callers compile and behave identically.
  • Recalc/stall/lookahead re-dispatches use the engine that produced the current path (stored per-walk), so a walk never silently switches engines mid-route.

Everything downstream is untouched: the transport-fire branch keys off PathTransportEdge.type exactly as today, failed-edge blacklist and telemetry work identically (the blacklist is keyed on packed tiles, engine-independent — a door that times out under one engine is correctly avoided by both).

docs.title: 2.3 New public API (additive — nothing existing changes)
docs.text:
C++ facade (new exported symbols on srs::api::Walk; existing symbols byte-identical):

// Walk.h additions
enum class PathEngine { Default = 0, Static = 1, Devious = 2 };

// Same contracts as to(), but pins the path engine for this walk.
static bool toWith(const ScriptContext& ctx, PathEngine engine,
                   int32_t worldX, int32_t worldY, bool useTransports = true);
static bool toWith(const ScriptContext& ctx, PathEngine engine,
                   int32_t worldX, int32_t worldY, bool useTransports, int32_t plane);

// Session default used by to()/walkSmart() when script doesn't pin one.
// Default on startup = Static (current behavior). Sticky until changed.
static void       setEngine(const ScriptContext& ctx, PathEngine engine);
static PathEngine engine(const ScriptContext& ctx);

// Which engine produced the CURRENT/most recent path (for A/B logging).
static PathEngine activePathEngine(const ScriptContext& ctx);

state(), hasArrived(), arrivalDistance(), cancel(), isMoving() are shared — one executor, one walk at a time — so scripts poll exactly as before regardless of engine.

Lua (new names only):

game.walkToAlt(x, y[, useTransports[, plane]])   -- pin Devious engine for this walk
game.setPathEngine("static"|"devious")            -- session default for game.moveTo/walkTo/…
game.pathEngine()                                  -- current session default
game.activePathEngine()                            -- engine of current path ("static"/"devious"/"none")

Host config: PathfinderConfig gains defaultEngine (init from launcher config / CFG_SAFERS_PATH_ENGINE, default Static), DebugPanel gets an engine dropdown + per-engine telemetry columns. Fail-safe: if DeviousPathEngine failed to init (bad data files), selection silently pins Static and logs once — scripts never break because the alt engine is missing.

docs.title: 2.4 DeviousPathEngine internals (the port, C++-idiomatic)
docs.text:
New directory OSRSClient/Pathfinding/Devious/:

File Ports Notes DeviousPathEngine.h/.cpp Pathfinder.java BFS with ring-buffer queue (not LinkedList) + packed-int visited arena; termination on goal-area contains; 5M-node cap replaced by the same progress-reset budget our static engine uses (so head-to-head timing is apples-to-apples). Emits PathResult incl. best-effort partial (parity with executor expectations). SceneOverlay.h/.cpp withLocalCollisions + RegionManager.getTileFlags Render-thread snapshot (in refreshSnapshot()): copy live 4×104×104 flags from GameSDK/CollisionMap, compute the doors-as-open subtraction (door-action wall/objects not in the transport catalog → clear directional block), diff vs static map, store as a compact override list {packedTile → flagDelta}. Worker thread reads static map + override list only. Cheap: same order of work as the existing per-tick collision copy (WS-B1). DeviousTransportGraph.h/.cpp TransportLoader (data part) Loads devious_transports.tsv (converted from transports.json, see 2.5). Indexed by packed origin, same shape as TransportRegistry. Requirements evaluated via the existing PathfinderConfig::isAllowed + account snapshot — no second evaluator. DeviousTeleportSeeder.h/.cpp TeleportLoader (data part) Builds the usable-teleport set on the render thread (jewellery, tabs, spells — categories the executor can fire today). Seeds them as start-adjacent edges exactly like our current spell seeding — reuses PathTransportEdge with type discriminant. PohModel.h/.cpp (shared, lives in Pathfinding/, not Devious/) poh/*.java HousePortal (30 dests), JewelryBox tiers, nexus varbit map — pure data + varbit reads. This is Phase-4-roadmap data both engines' teleport seeding consumes once POH verbs land; the port merely front-loads the data collection.

Explicitly not ported: Walker.java / Movement.java execution logic (our PathExecutor supersedes it), Reachable.java floods (WS-B3 flood already better), dialog/widget click chains (packet verbs instead), sleeps/randomized step-size (MovementProfile owns behavioral variance).

docs.title: 2.5 Data pipeline
docs.text:
• tools/devious_import/convert_transports.py — one-off + re-runnable converter: transports.json (5056 rows) → transports/devious_transports.tsv matching our existing TSV grammar (Origin/Destination/Duration/menuOption/Requirements columns), so Transport::fromTsvRow parses it with zero new parse code. Requirement mapping: questRequirements→Quests, skillRequirements→Skills, itemRequirements→Item IDs, varRequirements→Varbits/Varplayers, worldRequirements→isMembers.
  • Rows that duplicate existing transports.tsv entries are fine — the devious graph is loaded into its own DeviousTransportGraph, so the two engines' datasets stay independent (that independence is part of what we're A/B testing).
  • Optional (deferred): convert_regions.py — devious /regions GZIP → SCM1 for collision-dataset diffing. Not on critical path (encodings are equivalent; we reuse our bin).
  • THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry: BSD-2-Clause text + devious-client/RuneLite attribution.

docs.title: 2.6 Executor verb gaps shared by both engines
docs.text:
The devious graph will emit edge types our executor can't fire yet (fairy rings, NPC boats, gliders, spirit trees, POH objects). Two-stage policy, mirroring WS-G2:

  1. Capability gate at graph load (v1): DeviousTransportGraph only admits edge types with a registered executor handler — identical rule to today's static graph. Day one, the devious engine is at verb parity with static; the head-to-head measures search/overlay/data quality, not verb coverage.
  2. Handler table lands verbs for both engines at once (v2, = existing WS-H2 roadmap): per-TransportType handler registry in PathExecutor (fairy rings via IfButton dial packets, NPC boats via OPNPC1 + Resume*Dialog, POH via object clicks in the house instance). Each verb that lands widens both graphs' capability gates simultaneously — the port accelerates WS-H2 by providing devious's per-category interaction recipes as reference, executed our way (packets, not widget clicks).

docs.title: 2.7 Head-to-head test harness
docs.text:
1. Telemetry split by engine: PathTelemetry counters gain an engine dimension (two instances keyed by IPathEngine::name(); DebugPanel shows side-by-side). Compare: time-to-path, nodes explored, path cost vs actual ticks-to-arrive, recalcs per walk, transport timeouts, unreachables, arrival distance.
  2. Shadow mode (CFG_SAFERS_PATH_SHADOW=1): every dispatch runs both engines on identical PathRequest snapshots (two worker threads — cheap, searches are ms-class). The selected engine's result drives the walk; the shadow result is compared and logged (path cost Δ, length Δ, transports Δ, wall-time Δ, found/partial disagreement) to a CSV under logs/path_ab/. Zero behavioral risk — shadow output never steers.
  3. Route regression suite: Lua script scripts/tests/path_ab_routes.lua walking a fixed route book (bank-to-bank circuits, door-heavy interiors like POH/farmhouses, cross-plane dungeons, teleport-favored long hauls, instance areas) alternating engines, dumping per-route rows. Known weak classes from the June audit (door stalls, plane changes, teleport seeding) get dedicated routes.
  4. Decision gate: after N sessions of shadow CSVs + route-book runs, compare and either (a) promote devious ideas into static (most likely: SceneOverlay + event-driven invalidation are engine-independent modules and can be re-pointed at StaticPathfinder), (b) flip defaultEngine, or (c) delete the loser. The seam makes all three outcomes one-line config changes. Shared-infrastructure work (WS-H2 verbs, POH data) survives the decision either way — it is deliberately kept out of the engines so the A/B verdict never strands it.

docs.title: 2.8 Phasing & effort
docs.text: Phase Work Effort Exit criterion P0 — Seam IPathEngine, StaticPathEngine adapter, dispatchPathfinder generalization, engine members + EngineSelect, config default S (2-3 d) All existing walks byte-identical via adapter; zero API diff (dumpbin exports compare clean) P1 — Data transports.json converter, DeviousTransportGraph, license notice S-M (2-3 d) 5056 rows load; requirement parse coverage report P2 — Engine core BFS + visited arena + budget, SceneOverlay snapshot, teleport seeder (spells/items parity first) M (1-1.5 wk) Devious engine produces valid PathResult on route book; executor walks them P3 — API + harness Walk::toWith/setEngine exports, Lua bindings, per-engine telemetry, shadow mode, route suite M (3-5 d) Shadow CSVs flowing; A/B dashboard in DebugPanel P4 — Engine differentiators Doors-as-open overlay tuning, event-driven invalidation M (3-5 d) Devious engine wins/loses measurably on targeted route classes (door-heavy interiors) P5 — Shared roadmap (independent of A/B) WS-H2 handler table (fairy ring → NPC boats → spirit trees) + Phase-4 POH (PohModel data from the port) — widens both engines equally L (amortized) Per-verb live verification; excluded from A/B scoring

docs.title: 2.9 Risks
docs.text:
• Doors-as-open can strand walks if the walker meets a door it cannot open (quest-locked): mitigated by the existing failed-edge blacklist + blockedWalkEdges (the overlay consults the same session sets before clearing a door edge).
  • Two transport datasets drift — accepted for the A/B period; the decision gate ends it.
  • Shadow-mode thread pressure: two detached search threads per dispatch; bounded by existing cancel-flag discipline; disable shadow by default.
  • Game-update coupling: the port adds no new memory offsets (reuses CollisionMap/VarpSystem/ObjectQuery); update risk is unchanged.
  • PathExecutor churn: all changes additive/appended; header not shipped, so no plugin ABI exposure (verified IScript.h:31 opaque pointer).

docs.title: Appendix — devious file → design element map
docs.text: Devious source Disposition pathfinder/Pathfinder.java Port, re-implemented (ring buffer + arena) → DeviousPathEngine pathfinder/GlobalCollisionMap.java, BitSet4D.java Not ported — encoding equivalent to our SCM1; reuse StaticCollisionMap pathfinder/LocalCollisionMap.java, RegionManager.getTileFlags Port concept → SceneOverlay (render-thread snapshot) pathfinder/CollisionMap.java Interface only; superseded by StaticCollisionMap queries pathfinder/TransportLoader.java Data → converter + DeviousTransportGraph; handlers → WS-H2 reference recipes pathfinder/TeleportLoader.java Port (data+seeding) → DeviousTeleportSeeder pathfinder/model/Transport/Teleport/TransportDto Mapped onto existing Transport / PathTransportEdge pathfinder/model/requirement/* Mapped onto existing PathfinderConfig evaluation pathfinder/model/poh/* (HousePortal, JewelryBox, PortalNexus) Port → PohModel (shared — Phase-4 POH roadmap data, feeds both engines) pathfinder/model/{Fairy,Glider,Charter}*Location Data tables → TSV rows Walker.java, Movement.java, Reachable.java Not ported — PathExecutor/flood supersede; door-check logic informs SceneOverlay MovementConstants.java Wilderness areas → reuse WS-E5 coord-derived model

docs.title: Static collision divergence: Taverley/Falador border wall
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-11 · Status: root-caused + fixed (bin-level seal) · Area: ~(2924–2946, 3440–3452) plane 0

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: StaticPathfinder routed walks from ~(2930,3451) toward the Grand Exchange straight through the Falador north-west (Taverley border) wall with 0 transports. The live game blocks the crossing — there is no door/gate there — so PathExecutor could never traverse it (it survived only via the doorless-gap blacklist after 2 failed probes). The static map showed a one-tile stepped channel through the wall corner: (2941,3444) →E (2942,3444) →S (2942,3443) →E (2943,3443) →S (2943,3442), plus a fully open wall row at x=2924..2935, y=3450|3449 boundary.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The game cache ships an opened-up Taverley border, while the live server still enforces the old closed wall. Specifically, in every cache snapshot checked (OpenRS2 ids 2018 → 2593, i.e. 2025-01-08 → 2026-06-11, XTEA-decoded where needed):

  • The members gate (locs 1727/1728 "Gate", action Open) sits at (2935,3450)+(2935,3451), east edge — the old layout had it one tile east at x=2936 (matches Skretzo's restrictions.tsv "Talvery Gates" and Microbot's "gate at x=2936" comment).
  • The wall row west of the gate (x=2924..2934, y=3449..3451) contains no wall locs at all — open ground in the shipped map squares.
  • The wall corner at (2941..2944, 3442..3445) is built from loc 1911 (wall kit, no actions) and loc 7055 (fence, no actions) where the channel tiles hold only type-1 "wall corner diagonal" trim pieces. Type-1 corners are collision-inert for cardinal movement in the engine (corner flags gate diagonal steps only), and Skretzo's CollisionMapDumper.java does not emit anything for type 1.
  • No multi-state locs are involved: none of 1911/7055/980/1727/1728 has a varbit/varp transform (no opcode 77/92 in their defs). The leagues/broken-wall hypothesis is ruled out.
  • Tile settings (terrain file) carry blocked=1 only on the wall band tiles that are blocked in the static map; the channel tiles are settings=0.

The live game, however, still blocks the row and the corner channel (user verified live; Microbot's walker users hit the same and hand-patched it on 2026-06-02). Since the closed wall exists in no cache map square, the live server must be re-sealing it with server-spawned locs on zone load — geometry that is invisible to every cache-derived collision dump. The shipped map is presumably the future state of some pending content unlock.

docs.title: Answers to the original questions
docs.text:
1. Static dump (2935..2950, 3440..3450 p0): see tools/dump_collision_rect.py output; channel confirmed as the 3-tile pocket {(2942,3444),(2942,3443),(2943,3443)}.
  2. Is collision-map.bin stale? No. The deployed bin was byte-identical (SHA256 3946DE…) to a conversion of Microbot's current collision-map.zip (last regenerated 2026-05-12 from Skretzo's data). Skretzo's upstream zip (regenerated weekly by the ExtractCollisionMap GitHub Action; latest 2026-06-11) contains the identical flags in this region. The build pipeline pins nothing, but no available revision fixes this area.
  3. Multi-state loc? No (see above) — the divergence is cache-vs-live, not a state-resolution choice in the builder.
  4. Rebuild + diff: rebuilt from both current Microbot and current Skretzo zips; region 45_53/46_53 flags unchanged vs deployed. A rebuild alone cannot fix the divergence, hence the exclusion mechanism below.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Upstream (Microbot) band-aids this class of gap at search time via blocked_edges.tsv ("Static collision edge overrides for map data gaps"), which our pipeline fetched but never consumed (audit WS: 0 consumers). We now bake those edges into the bin at build time so every consumer of the static map (StaticPathfinder, PathSmoother, goal checks) sees sealed data:

  • tools/build_collision_map_bin.py — new repeatable --blocked-edges FILE.tsv option; clears the corresponding n/e flag bits (blocks are inherently bidirectional in the 2-bit encoding; diagonal edges rejected). Without the option the output is byte-identical to the old builder (regression-verified).
  • tools/collision_blocked_edges_local.tsv — SafeRS-tracked overrides and the only blocked-edges input to the build: upstream's Varrock-fence section (cherry-picked) + 5 edges sealing the corner pocket (not covered upstream). Gate edges stay open on purpose: doors are handled by the walker at execution time.

Correction (2026-06-11, same day): the first build also imported upstream Microbot's 14 "Taverley wall" row entries (x=2924–2938, y=3450→3449, comment "gate at x=2936"). An in-game object query then showed the live gate at (2935,3450)+(2935,3451) — the cache position, east edge — so the live wall follows the cache's N-S gate line and the ground west of it is open: those row entries are false walls (they shipped alongside Microbot's walker-BFS "false unreachable" bugfix and look like a workaround for that bug, not verified geometry). Removed; do not re-import upstream blocked_edges.tsv wholesale. The corner seal is unaffected: our live flood uses correct per-direction wall bits (CollisionMap.cpp canTraverse), so its "blocked" verdict at the channel reflects real engine flags, not corner-trim misreads. - tools/dump_collision_rect.py — diagnostic dumper (ASCII wall render + per-tile n/e/s/w flags) used throughout.

docs.title: Build workflow (after TSV refresh or upstream zip update)
docs.text:
python tools/build_collision_map_bin.py <collision-map.zip> x64/Release/collision-map.bin \
    --blocked-edges tools/collision_blocked_edges_local.tsv

(Deliberately does NOT pass the fetched upstream blocked_edges.tsv — see the correction above; upstream entries get cherry-picked into the local file after verification.)

Build log for the deployed bin: blocked edges: 12 applied, 6 already blocked, 0 in unmapped regions over Skretzo's 2026-06-11 zip (deployed SHA256 1067AFA6…, 2664 regions; the unpatched bin remains backed up as collision-map.bin.pre-seal.bak).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
BFS flood over the bin using canStep semantics from (2930,3451), with the gate door edges cut (incl. diagonal corner-cuts across them):

bin pocket entered east-side probes (2946,3443)/(2950,3445)/(3000,3450) unpatched yes (all 3 tiles) unreachable (pocket exits into the walled yard only) patched, gate cut no unreachable — reachable set shrinks by exactly the 3 pocket tiles patched, gate open no reachable via the gate + outside corridor only

So after the seal, the only static crossing of the wall complex is the members gate (a real, openable door), matching live geometry.

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
• Confirm the spawned-loc theory in game: with the client injected, query the live scene objects at (2942,3443)/(2930,3449) and diff against cache — spawned wall pieces should appear that exist in no map square. (DebugPanel object query is sufficient.)
  • Watch for the content flip: if Jagex unlocks the new layout, live will start matching the cache and these 19 edges become an unnecessary (but harmless — the row/corner then sit inside ordinary walls) detour-maker. Re-test with the executor if a Taverley-area game update lands.
  • Same failure class elsewhere: any cache-vs-live spawned-loc area will reproduce this. The playbook: dump_collision_rect.py the area, BFS-trace the leak (verify_seal.py pattern), decode the map square locs vs live, add edges to collision_blocked_edges_local.tsv, rebuild.

docs.title: Static collision divergence: Champions' Guild + Varrock Castle doors
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-13 · Status: root-caused + fixed (bin-level seal) · Areas: Champions' Guild ~(3188–3196, 3352–3364) p0; Varrock Castle keep ~(3203–3224, 3472–3500) p0

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text:
StaticPathfinder walk-only routes (useTransports=false) cut straight through the Champions' Guild and Varrock Castle, treating the door tiles as free passages. Live collision blocks the closed doors, so PathExecutor either tries to open them (dragging the player off-route into the building) or detects the door-less gap and flails against the live wall. Observed: a Varrock→Lumbridge walk clipped the guild and produced a 294-step blocked cascade, player stranded ~(3199,3355).

Unlike the Taverley wall, these are real, permanent buildings with real openable doors — not a spawned-loc cache/live divergence.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Open door edge + missing transport row. These doors are CLOSED-by-default in the live game but appear as walkable edges with no crossing transport in the static map, so A threads through them in both* walk-only and transport mode and the client never issues an "Open door" action.

How Skretzo/Microbot's data is supposed to model a door (two halves):

  1. a wall (or open edge) in the cache-derived collision-map.zip, and
  2. an Open;Door;<id> row in transports.tsv that provides the crossing when the pathfinder is allowed to open doors.

RuneLite's collision extractor (which generates Microbot's collision-map.zip) emits no movement-wall flag for an interactType==2 door loc — it leaves the edge OPEN and expects half #2 (the transport row) to carry the crossing. For the doors below, half #2 is missing: there is no transports.tsv row. Result: an always-open edge that nothing gates.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Cache decode (OpenRS2 2593, the live cache) of the door locs, cross-checked against the deployed bin (x64/Release/collision-map.bin, SHA 1067afa6…):

loc name / action tile(s) p0 edge in transports.tsv? edge in bin 1805 Door / Open (=closed) (3191,3363) S no OPEN 11773 Door / Open (=closed) (3195,3357),(3192,3354) +11 in castle W/N/… no OPEN 32464 Door / Open (=closed) (3222,3491),(3222,3479) S yes (lines 841-844) OPEN→ now sealed 11772 Door / Close (=open live) (3224,3493) N no already WALL 15514/15/16 "fai varrock gate" — — no do not exist in cache 2593

Discriminator — control doors that DO have a transport row are a mix of open and walled edges (9398,32464 OPEN; 12348,12349 WALL), all with a row. So "open door edge" is normal extractor output; the anomaly for 1805/11773 is the missing transport row, leaving the open edge ungated.

docs.title: Answers to the three questions
docs.text:
1. Static dump (tools/dump_collision_rect.py over both areas, p0): the building perimeters ARE walled, but the door tiles are open gaps. A canStep flood proves each interior is one connected component with the exterior (guild 44/44 interior tiles exterior-reachable; castle courtyard↔keep↔north all one 1415-tile component). So the buildings are NOT "fully walkable" — the walls are present; only the door edges leak.

  2. Source vs build-script vs door representation. Not the build script: tools/build_collision_map_bin.py only clears bits for explicit --blocked-edges and otherwise copies the zip byte-for-byte. Proof — the deployed bin differs from its pre-seal backup by exactly the 12 edges the local TSV targets (Taverley 5 + palace fence 7), nothing else; and a no---blocked-edges rebuild from the zip is byte-identical (SHA 5cc02d…) to the pre-seal backup. The divergence is in (a) the source collision-map.zip (open door edges, by extractor design) × (b) the door representation (transports.tsv lacks the matching rows). It is NOT a cache-vs-live spawned-loc case (the door locs are real cache geometry).

  3. Are the doors in transports.tsv? No — 1805, 11773, 15514/15516 appear in none of the 24 transport TSVs. 15514/15516 don't even exist as loc defs in cache 2593 (stale IDs); the castle's south courtyard entrance (x3212/3213, y3459) is a permanently open gateway with no gate loc and must stay walkable.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Restore the static map's half of the door model: bake the missing wall edges into the bin so walk-only routes around these closed doors (matching live). 16 edges added to tools/collision_blocked_edges_local.tsv, rebuilt into x64/Release/collision-map.bin (new SHA 33eedf58…; prior bin backed up as collision-map.bin.pre-buildings.bak).

python tools/build_collision_map_bin.py tools/collision-map.zip \
    x64/Release/collision-map.bin \
    --blocked-edges tools/collision_blocked_edges_local.tsv
# -> blocked edges: 28 applied, 6 already blocked, 0 in unmapped regions
  • Champions' Guild (3): 1805 (3191,3363 S) + 11773 (3195,3357 W), (3192,3354 N). Fully encloses the 42-tile interior.
  • Varrock Castle keep (13), plane 0: 11773 ×11 + 32464 ×2. Encloses the 216-tile side-room interior; the great hall stays open (it's a wide archway with no door loc — 174 tiles, correct vs live) and the grounds' south gateway stays open.

This is the Taverley pattern. Because the seal is baked into the bin (not loaded into TransportRegistry at runtime), it gates only the walking expansion — a future transports.tsv door row would still cross in transport mode (StaticPathfinder transport edges bypass canStep and consult only the runtime registry's blocked set, not the baked bits). So this fix does not foreclose the proper long-term model.

docs.title: Not sealed (deliberately)
docs.text:
• Castle south courtyard gateway (x3212/3213, y3459-3470): open in cache, no gate loc. If a closed gate appears live there, it's a spawned/scripted loc — handle via the live-flood blocked-edge bake (Taverley mechanism) after in-game confirmation, not from cache geometry. 15514/15516 are not it.
  • Great hall archway: legitimately open.
  • Upper floors (plane 1/2): 11773 has 11 plane-1 + 3 plane-2 placements (listed by the decode). Add analogously only if walk-only routing on the castle's upper floors is needed; out of scope here.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
BFS flood with canStep semantics (= what walk-only A* expands), via tools/diag_enclosure.py / tools/diag_door_edges.py / tools/diag_castle.py:

area before after (rebuilt bin) guild interior (44 walkable tiles) all exterior-reachable 42-tile sealed pocket, 0 gap edges castle keep side-rooms (390 region tiles) 388 exterior-reachable 216-tile sealed pocket, 0 gap edges (great hall 174 stays open) 16 door edges all OPEN / canStep=YES all WALL / canStep=no whole-bin diff vs pre-build backup — exactly 16 edges OPEN→WALL, nothing else no door tile became fully isBlocked — confirmed (each keeps ≥1 open edge)

A sealed interior pocket is disconnected from the exterior, so no walk-only path (any origin/dest) can route through it — strictly stronger than fixing one route.

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
• Reachability of building interiors: sealing makes walk-only correctly fail to path inside (vs flailing). To enter (e.g. King Roald), add the Open;Door rows to transports.tsv (1805, 11773, and the castle keep doors) AND fix the door-opening walker (it currently drags the player). Then walk-only routes around and transport-mode opens the door — the full model.
  • Confirm doors are closed live: cache "Open" action ⇒ default-closed, and the executor's live block cascade corroborates the guild. A DebugPanel object query on a sealed door tile would confirm each keep door is closed live.
  • Castle south gate: query the south gateway (x3212/3213, y3459-3470) live; if a closed gate spawns, add a Taverley-style live-flood edge.
  • Same failure class elsewhere: any building whose doors lack a transports.tsv row reproduces this. Playbook: dump_collision_rect.py the area → cache-decode the door locs (Open-action = closed) → check transports.tsv → seal the open closed-door edges in collision_blocked_edges_local.tsv → diag_enclosure.py to confirm.

docs.title: Mouse Profile Trainer — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-11 · Status: Proposed · Owner: SafeRSClient (trainer UI) + OSRSClient (runtime model)

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
A tool inside SafeRSClient that builds a per-user mouse movement profile from the user's own clicks. The user runs a short session clicking dots of varying size/position; we measure their real motor signature (velocity shape, submovements, lateral bend, launch/landing perturbation, tau braking, mid-drift, OU micro-tremor, LF macro tremor, per-call sigma scatter, overshoot), fit each measurement into a bounded distribution ({mu, sigma, lo, hi}), and save the result as JSON in the client directory. OSRSClient loads that JSON at runtime and samples fresh parameter values per path — so synthesized movement is modeled after the user but never pixel-identical (stable statistical signature, fresh noise per click — same philosophy as the existing MovementProfile comment block).

Reference: titanclient's "Mouse Path Testing" panel (screenshot 2026-06-11) — its tuning taxonomy (Duration/Fitts, Velocity profile, Submovements, Lateral bend twin-bumps, Launch/Landing perturbation 2D, Tau schedule, Mid-drift Cauchy, OU micro-tremor, LF macro tremor, Hyper per-call sigmas, Overshoot) is the model class we adopt, but we fit it from captured data instead of hand-tuned sliders.

docs.title: 2. Current state (what this builds on)
docs.text:
• OSRSClient/Input/MovementProfile.h — v1 params-only model: cubic-bezier bow (arcMag, bezierMid1/2), per-sample jitter, overshoot prob/dist, linear Fitts duration, event budget, bimodal dt buckets, click dwell/hold. Seeded per-account via FNV-1a of character name (MovementProfiles::fromSeed). Deliberate property: different accounts → decorrelated signatures. This property must survive (see §8).
  • Consumers: MouseController (per-frame WndProc curve: bezier + easeInOut + jitter + overshoot) and InputSpoofer (ring-writer: event budget + dt buckets). InputManager pushes MovementProfiles::active() before each move; dllmain calls resolveFor() per frame.
  • SafeRSClient = native C++ WebView2 host (main.cpp routes {type:...} JSON messages, nlohmann) + React/Vite UI (ui/src/Launcher.tsx, bridge in ui/src/nativeBridge.ts).
  • Config root: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SafeRS\ (AccountStore already uses ...\SafeRS\accounts).

docs.title: 3. Architecture
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────── SafeRSClient.exe ────────────────────────────┐
│  React UI (ui/src/MouseTrainer.tsx)            native host (main.cpp)    │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌──────────┐   JSON bridge   ┌──────────────┐  │
│  │ Capture  │ │  Review │ │ Simulate │ ◄──────────────► │ PathModel +  │  │
│  │ (dots)   │ │  (fit)  │ │ (A→B ×N) │  mouse_trainer_* │ Estimators   │  │
│  └──────────┘ └─────────┘ └──────────┘                  └──────┬───────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │ ────────┘
                       %LOCALAPPDATA%\SafeRS\mouse_profile.json ◄┘  (save)
                                      │ (load at injection / relog)
┌──────────────────────────── OSRSClient.dll ──────────────────────────────┐
│ MouseProfileStore ─► PathModel::generate(from,to,params,rng)             │
│        │                    │ timed polyline (x,y,t)                     │
│        ▼                    ▼                                            │
│ MovementProfiles      MouseController (WndProc frames) / InputSpoofer    │
│ (v1 fallback)         (ring events)  — emission machinery unchanged      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Single source of truth: the generator (and the estimators) are C++ in OSRSClient/Input/PathModel/, compiled into both OSRSClient.dll and SafeRSClient.exe (sibling submodules in the SafeRS superproject — SafeRSClient.vcxproj references ..\OSRSClient\Input\PathModel\*.cpp). The trainer UI never re-implements the model; Simulate calls the exact code that will run in-game, so preview == production. (Caveat: SafeRSClient then requires the sibling checkout to build — true for everyone using the superproject.)

New files:

OSRSClient/Input/PathModel/
  PathModel.h/.cpp        // generate(): params → timed polyline. Pure, seedable, no Win32.
  PathParams.h            // Band {mu,sigma,lo,hi} + per-family param structs + neutral defaults
  ProfileJson.h/.cpp      // (de)serialize, validate, clamp, version-migrate, crc
  Estimators.h/.cpp       // trial traces → fitted Bands (trainer-side; small, ship anyway)
  MouseProfileStore.h/.cpp// runtime: locate/load/cache JSON, fallback chain (OSRSClient only)
SafeRSClient/ui/src/MouseTrainer.tsx   // the three-tab tool
SafeRSClient/main.cpp                  // + mouse_trainer_* / mouse_profile_* message handlers

docs.title: 4. Capture session (the dot task)
docs.text:
Window: full-stage canvas view in the launcher (game stage hidden via existing set_stage_visible). Dark background, one dot at a time.

Trial schedule — Fitts coverage grid. Each trial is a (distance D, width W, direction θ) cell: W ∈ {12, 20, 32, 48, 72} px diameter (spans menu rows → inventory slots → big UI buttons), D ∈ {60, 150, 300, 500, 800} px (clamped to window), θ ∈ 8 compass directions. Stratified-random order filling the grid; dot spawns at the sampled D/θ relative to the current cursor position (clamped to bounds; actual D recorded). Defaults: Standard = 120 dots (~4–5 min), Quick = 60, Thorough = 200. Live coverage meter shows unfilled cells.

Per-trial flow: idle gap 300–700 ms (jittered) → dot appears (spawn timestamp) → user moves and clicks it → ripple feedback → next. The idle gaps and the pre-click hover are first-class data: cursor-at-rest windows are pure tremor signal (voluntary motion ≈ 0), which is exactly where OU micro-tremor and LF macro tremor are estimable without contamination.

Sampling: pointermove + getCoalescedEvents() (device-rate history, typically 125–1000 Hz in Chromium/WebView2) + pointerrawupdate where available; performance.now() timestamps; coordinates × devicePixelRatio → physical px (what the game's WndProc sees). Preflight screen ("swirl the mouse for 3 s") measures effective sample rate and DPR; warn below ~100 Hz effective. If real-world rates disappoint, fallback is native WM_INPUT capture in the host streamed over the bridge — deferred unless needed.

Trial rejection (logged, not silently dropped): pointer left canvas / visibilitychange; reaction < 80 ms (anticipation) or movement > 4 s (distraction); inter-sample gap > 50 ms mid-movement (hitch); first 8 trials (warm-up). Misclicks don't advance the dot but are recorded — miss rate feeds landing-sigma sanity and submovement stats.

Raw trial record (UI → host at session end, or incrementally):

{ "dpr": 1.25, "dot": {"x":812,"y":355,"r":16}, "spawnT": 91234.2, "clickT": 92110.7,
  "press": {"downT": 92110.7, "upT": 92187.3, "button": 0},
  "samples": [[t,x,y], ...] }            // physical px, ms, device-rate

docs.title: 5. Estimation (trial traces → model parameters)
docs.text:
Preprocess per trial: resample to uniform 4 ms (monotone cubic), Savitzky–Golay velocity/ acceleration, movement onset = speed > 5 % of trial peak sustained 3 samples; chord frame = (along s∈[0,1], perpendicular d). Then per family:

Family Estimator (per trial → pooled) Duration (Fitts) Regress MT = a + b·log₂(D/W+1) across trials → aMs, bMsPerBit; residual spread → duration sigma. R² is a quality gate. Velocity profile Normalized v(s): time-to-peak fraction (skew), peak/mean ratio, spectral-arc-length smoothness → shape params of the base minimum-jerk-with-skew profile. Submovements Parse velocity local minima after primary peak → count of corrective submovements, amplitude (frac of D), duration; logistic prob vs ID. Lateral bend Signed d(s) least-squares-fit to twin-bump basis (two raised-cosine bumps: amp₁,c₁,w₁, amp₂,c₂,w₂). Signed amps capture handedness/curl direction bias. Launch perturbation (2D) Heading error angle + magnitude over first ~60 ms vs chord; fitted decay constant. Bias ≠ 0 is a real human signature — keep it. Landing perturbation (2D) First-arrival endpoint offset in chord frame → along/across sigmas + bias, scaling vs W. Overshoot Chord-axis overrun > W/2 then reversal → P(overshoot Tau schedule Deceleration phase: τ(t) = gap/ġap; linear fit slope k (tau-coupling constant; k≈0.5 smooth stop, higher = harder braking) + engage fraction. Mid-drift (Cauchy) Residual after removing fitted bend, mid-window s∈[0.2,0.8]; increment distribution fitted by quantile-matched Cauchy scale (robust; tails are the point). OU micro-tremor From idle/hover windows: AR(1) on position residuals x[n+1]=αx[n]+ε → θ=−ln α/Δt, σ from ε. Movement-phase high-pass (>6 Hz) residual as cross-check. LF macro tremor Idle windows band-pass 0.5–3 Hz → amplitude + dominant freq. Hyper per-call sigmas Per-trial residual RMS relative to pooled RMS → lognormal σ of a per-path multiplier. This is the "variance of variance" — some trials careful, some sloppy. Click timing dwell (arrival→down), hold (down→up) distributions → replaces v1 clickDelay*/clickHold*. Reaction spawn→onset distribution (useful for humanized response delays beyond paths).

Anti-overfit shrinkage: ~120 trials is thin for ~40 scalars. Every fitted Band is blended toward the neutral default: mu' = w·mu_user + (1−w)·mu_neutral, w = n_accepted/(n_accepted+40) (same for sigma). Quick sessions lean neutral; thorough sessions are mostly user.

Normalization with retained variance (the core requirement): each scalar is stored as a Band {mu, sigma, lo, hi} where [lo,hi] is the hand-authored global human-plausible range (the analog of titanclient's "client rules"). Fitted mu is clamped into the band; sigma is floored (never 0 — a zero-variance profile is itself a bot tell) and capped. At generation time each path samples clamp(mu + sigma·m_hyper·N(0,1), lo, hi) per parameter — every path differs, but the distribution is the user's.

docs.title: 6. Generation model (PathModel v2)
docs.text:
generate(from, to, P, rng, bucketMs=0) → timed polyline. Layers, applied in order:

  1. Duration from Fitts Band (D, effective W of the target) → T.
  2. Base kinematic s(t): minimum-jerk position profile warped by velocity-shape params (time-to-peak skew, peak/mean flatness).
  3. Tau braking reshapes the final approach segment per k (blend-in at engage fraction).
  4. Lateral bend: d(s) = Σ twin bumps × D.
  5. Launch perturbation: initial heading/speed error decaying over fitted window.
  6. Mid-drift: Cauchy-stepped walk added in s∈[0.2,0.8], window-faded.
  7. OU micro-tremor (per-axis OU process at sample rate) + LF macro tremor (band-limited sway).
  8. Landing: endpoint drawn from 2D landing covariance; if outside target W or overshoot triggered → corrective submovement(s) (small Fitts moves with their own bend/noise) until inside; overshoot draws pass-distance then returns.
  9. Hyper multiplier m ~ LogNormal(0, σ_hyper) sampled once per call, scaling all noise families (3–11).
  10. Output: ≥ internal 8 ms granularity; optional resample to fixed bucketMs buckets (Simulate parity with titanclient-style invariants); last point == exact target; adjacent duplicates collapsed; clamped to bounds.

Determinism: rng is injected. Runtime uses fresh random_device per click (per existing v1 philosophy); Simulate exposes a lockable seed for reproducible overlays; golden tests use fixed seeds.

docs.title: 7. Profile JSON (v2 schema)
docs.text:
%LOCALAPPDATA%\SafeRS\mouse_profile.json (user default) · optional per-account override mouse_profile.<account-slug>.json (slug per AccountStore's slugify). Versioned, CRC'd, unknown fields ignored, every value re-clamped on load (hand-edited files can't go robotic).

{
  "schema": "safers.mouseProfile/2",
  "createdUtc": "2026-06-11T18:00:00Z",
  "trainer": { "trials": 120, "accepted": 104, "sampleHzMedian": 498, "dpr": 1.25,
               "qualityScore": 0.87, "appVersion": "..." },
  // every leaf below is a Band: {"mu":…,"sigma":…,"lo":…,"hi":…}
  "fitts":     { "aMs": B, "bMsPerBit": B, "durSigmaFrac": B },
  "velocity":  { "timeToPeakFrac": B, "peakOverMean": B, "smoothness": B },
  "submove":   { "extraCount": B, "ampFracOfD": B, "durMs": B, "probPerBit": B },
  "bend":      { "amp1FracOfD": B, "c1": B, "w1": B, "amp2FracOfD": B, "c2": B, "w2": B },
  "launch":    { "angleSigmaDeg": B, "angleBiasDeg": B, "magFrac": B, "decayFrac": B },
  "landing":   { "alongSigmaPx": B, "acrossSigmaPx": B, "alongBiasPx": B, "wScale": B },
  "tau":       { "k": B, "engageFrac": B },
  "midDrift":  { "cauchyScalePx": B },
  "ouTremor":  { "thetaHz": B, "sigmaPx": B },
  "lfTremor":  { "freqHz": B, "ampPx": B },
  "hyper":     { "sigmaLn": B },
  "overshoot": { "prob": B, "distFracOfD": B, "returnMsPerPx": B },
  "clicks":    { "dwellMs": B, "holdMs": B },
  "reaction":  { "ms": B },
  "accountDecorrelation": { "enabled": true, "muShiftFracOfSigma": 0.5, "sigmaScalePct": 15 },
  "legacyV1":  { /* mapped MovementProfile fields — lets v1 consumers run pre-switchover */ },
  "crc32": "…"
}

legacyV1 mapping ships in phase 1 so the existing MouseController/InputSpoofer immediately inherit user-fitted v1 values (arc ≈ bend amp, jitter ≈ tremor σ, durations from Fitts fit, dwell/hold, overshoot) even before the v2 generator switchover.

docs.title: 8. Runtime integration (OSRSClient) & per-account decorrelation
docs.text:
• MouseProfileStore::resolve() runs at injection and inside MovementProfiles::resolveFor (name-change path; add cheap mtime re-stat so re-saving from the trainer takes effect on relog, no client restart). Precedence: per-account JSON → user JSON → v1 fromSeed(name). Any parse/validation failure → log once, fall back; input must never hard-fail.
  • Keep cross-account decorrelation. A single shared user JSON would make all of a user's accounts emit one identical statistical fingerprint — exactly what v1's FNV-1a seeding was built to prevent (linkage risk). Default-on: account seed shifts each mu by up to ±0.5·sigma (within band) and scales sigma ±15 %. Same human style-envelope, different individual per account. Toggleable in the JSON for users who insist.
  • Consumers: MouseController::generateTrajectory swaps bezier/easeInOut/jitter for a PathModel polyline (per-frame update() interpolates it; WndProc emission + AFK-timer touch unchanged). InputSpoofer resamples the polyline into its event budget/dt-bucket ring format. Both behind a pathModelV2 kill-switch defaulting off until A/B'd.

docs.title: 9. Trainer UI (three tabs in the launcher)
docs.text:
Capture — preflight (sample-rate/DPR calibration) → dot session with progress bar, live coverage grid, accepted/rejected counters, abort/pause. Review — per-family cards: fitted mu ± sigma rendered inside the [lo, hi] band bar, shrinkage weight, quality gates (Fitts R² ≥ 0.5, accepted ≥ 50, sample rate ≥ 100 Hz…), warnings ("trackpad-like signature: tremor floor clamped"), then Save / Set active / Save as account override. Simulate — click two points on a canvas (or randomize), N = 1–200 paths (user-configurable), optional seed lock, bucket-ms control; renders overlaid polylines + a batch table (mean/σ/min/max of point count, duration, arc length, straightness, avg/peak speed, lateral dev, overshoot rate) + invariant checklist (exact target, bucket spacing, bounds, adjacent-distinct, monotonic t) — deliberately mirroring the titanclient panel — plus "vs. my real trials": overlays captured trials of similar D/W and shows per-metric percentile chips ("synth peak speed = p43 of yours").

Bridge messages (all host-side handlers in main.cpp, work off the UI thread): mouse_trainer_fit {trials[]} → mouse_trainer_fit_result {profile, diagnostics} · mouse_trainer_generate {profile?, from, to, n, seed?, bucketMs} → mouse_trainer_paths {paths[][], metrics, invariants} · mouse_profile_save / list / load / set_active → correspondingly-named replies. Raw session is also dumped to %LOCALAPPDATA%\SafeRS\profiles\sessions\<ts>.json.gz so fits can be re-run after estimator improvements without re-clicking.

docs.title: 10. Phasing
docs.text:
1. PathModel lib + schema + golden tests (no UI): generator, ProfileJson, neutral profile, invariant tests, legacyV1 mapping. Synthetic-profile sanity via existing DebugPanel. [DONE 2026-06-11] — OSRSClient/Input/PathModel/ (PathMath/PathParams/PathModel/ ProfileJson/Estimators/PathModelSelfTest), DebugPanel Path Lab tab, standalone runner OSRSClient/tools/pathmodel_tests/build_and_run.ps1 (39 tests green, incl. estimator round-trip). Gotcha: Profile::hyper had to be hyperVar — rpcndr.h #define hyper __int64 leaks through the DLL PCH.
  2. Trainer UI: capture + fit + save through the bridge; Review/Simulate tabs. [DONE 2026-06-11] — SafeRSClient/MouseTrainerHost.{h,cpp} (compiles the shared ..\OSRSClient\Input\PathModel\*.cpp + MovementProfileNeutral.cpp; verbs mouse_trainer_fit / mouse_trainer_generate / mouse_profile_{save,load} / mouse_trainer_session_save, atomic write to %LOCALAPPDATA%\SafeRS\mouse_profile.json), bridge wrappers in nativeBridge.ts, ui/src/MouseTrainer.tsx (Capture/Review/Simulate), dock entry. Both binaries build clean; UI renders + is interactive (verified in vite preview + by the user manually). Bug found & fixed during smoke test: the capture surface cached its getBoundingClientRect right after the phase flip to "running", but the status row grows taller in running mode and shifts the surface down after the cache — so every dot-click mis-tested against a stale vertical offset. Fix: read the rect live per pointer event (liveRect()), never cache. (Note: synthetic PointerEvents don't drive React's pointer handlers in the headless preview — only .click()/onClick does — so the dot-hit path must be verified with real mouse input, not the preview harness.)
  3. Runtime loader + MouseController v2 switchover behind kill-switch; A/B with spoof logs. [DONE 2026-06-11] — OSRSClient/Input/MouseProfileStore.{h,cpp} loads %LOCALAPPDATA%\SafeRS\mouse_profile.json via pathmodel::parse, caches + re-stats mtime in resolveFor (picks up trainer re-saves on next frame), applies name-seeded decorrelate, fail-soft on parse error. Runtime kill-switch enabled() (default off). MouseController::setProfileV2 + moveToV2/updateV2Locked: when the switch is on and a profile is loaded, moveTo synthesizes a full pathmodel::generate polyline and update interpolates it by timestamp — bypassing bezier/overshoot/jitter (all baked into the path). v1 path untouched when off. InputManager::clickAt pushes the v2 profile+predicate; dllmain resolves the store each frame after MovementProfiles::resolveFor. DebugPanel Input tab has the toggle + load/quality/seed status (the A/B control). Thread-safety: clickAt→moveTo runs on the Lua worker thread, update on the render thread; the v1 POD control points tolerate that race but the polyline std::vector can't, so all v2-playback fields are serialized by m_v2Mtx (publish under lock, flip m_moving after). Click delay/hold still come from v1 — wiring v2 dwell/hold is a phase-4 follow-up, as is per-target width (currently a fixed 8px radius) and the per-account override file.
  4. InputSpoofer switchover, per-account overrides UX, decorrelation polish. [DONE 2026-06-11] — (a) InputSpoofer::inject samples ring positions from the v2 polyline (MouseProfileStore) instead of bezier+decelEase when the kill-switch is on, and takes duration from the polyline (clamped to the ring's [60,320] window); the ring budget, bimodal dt timeline, secondary-ring mirror and click-staging are unchanged, and it fail-softs to v1 on an empty path. With the switch OFF (default) both paths are byte-for-byte the old v1 behavior. (b) v2 click dwell/hold: MouseController::v2ClickTiming hands InputManager the fitted dwell (arrival→down) and hold (down→up) for the click states; v1 bands otherwise. (c) per-target width: optional targetRadiusPx threaded through clickAt→moveTo→moveToV2 and SpoofRequest, and derived from the target's real on-screen bounds — Camera::footprintRadiusPx projects 1-tile neighbours → screen px-per-tile, scales by the footprint, takes the tighter dimension, clamps [4,60]; object/NPC/player (perform) and widget WndProc (clickReal*, from the rect) pass real radii, so near/large targets read as easier and far/small as precise. 8px default only where bounds are unknown (bare clickScreen, short widget-button DoActions where Fitts sits near the floor anyway). (d) per-account override: MouseProfileStore prefers mouse_profile.<charslug>.json (used as-is — already account-specific) over the shared mouse_profile.json (decorrelated by name); DebugPanel flags which is active. Launcher "save for this account" UX is the remaining bit (the load/precedence side is live). DLL builds clean, 42 lib tests green.

Status: all four phases shipped. The trainer captures→fits→saves a profile, and both in-game movement paths (WndProc curve + ring-writer) consume it behind the pathModelV2 kill-switch. Remaining polish: launcher "save override for account" UX and persisting the kill-switch in Config.

docs.title: 11. Risks / open questions
docs.text:
• WebView2 effective sample rate on low-end mice/VMs — preflight measures it; WM_INPUT native capture is the fallback. Pointer coords must be DPR-corrected or tremor σ is ~25 % off.
  • Trackpad/pen users produce non-mouse signatures (no 8–12 Hz tremor, speed caps) — detect via tremor spectrum and warn; clamps prevent degenerate profiles either way.
  • Profile sharing between users would clone fingerprints — discourage (per-account decorrelation already softens it; could salt exports later).
  • Staleness: human signatures drift; nudge re-capture after ~60 days (metadata has the date).
  • Open: should the trainer also fit wheel/scroll and key-timing profiles later? Same capture-fit-band machinery applies.

docs.title: Pathfinder Audit vs Microbot — 2026-06-10
docs.text: Verified against current working tree (uncommitted changes incl.) and E:\microbot-audit (clone of 2026-05-27). 41 gaps confirmed, 2 claims refuted. 55 agents, every gap adversarially verified with file:line evidence.

docs.title: Pathfinder Improvement Plan — SafeRS vs Microbot Audit Synthesis
docs.text: Priorities applied in order: SPEED (no idle time) > ACCURACY (exact tile) > COMPLETENESS (every accessible transport). Fixes are grouped into workstreams (WS) because several gaps share one mechanism; every confirmed gap id is mapped to exactly one workstream or the do-not-bother list.

docs.title: WS-A: Run-energy management — speed-no-run-energy-management
docs.text: The single largest speed lever in the audit (2x walk speed). - Mechanism: Wire the setRunToggle stub (GameSDK/GameData.cpp:214-223) as an IfButton wire packet on the run orb widget (lift widget id from RuneLite per feedback_runelite_data_source, mark kTODO until live-verified), dispatched via EngineDispatch — not Microbot's orb mouse-click. The existing varp-173 reader (getRunToggle, GameData.cpp:207-212) is already correct for state checks. Then add a manageRunEnergy() pass to PathExecutor::onGameTick (Pathfinding/PathExecutor.cpp, near the watchdog block ~:850): enable run when energy > 10 (reader works, GameData.cpp:191-212). - v1.1 — potions: dose stamina/energy/super-energy via Inventory::contains + Inventory::interact when path-remaining >= 20 tiles and energy below a persona threshold. Seed the threshold from the existing MovementProfile FNV-1a char-name infrastructure (project_movement_profile) instead of porting Microbot's mix64 — same behavioral spread (12-24 hardcore / 35-55 casual), zero new seeding code. Enforce the 10s min interval with game-tick counting, not wall-clock sleeps. - Also fix: the stub's false-success return true (GameData.cpp:223) so Player::toggleRunEnergy (PluginAPI/API/Player.cpp:93-97) stops lying to scripts. - Effort: S (toggle + run-on), M (potions). Impact: speed HIGH. Deps: none. Do first.

docs.title: WS-B: Live collision correctness + one-flood reachability — accuracy-stale-live-collision-snapshot, speed-reachability-full-astar-per-call, accuracy-scene-size-garbage-band, accuracy-interpolation-not-reachability-gated, accuracy-offpath-detection-chebyshev-not-reachability
docs.text:
• B1 — per-tick snapshot refresh (S): delete/condition the same-region fast path at GameSDK/CollisionMap.cpp:89-92. update() is already called every game tick (dllmain.cpp:741); re-copying 4×110×110×4 ≈ 193KB per 600ms is negligible. This single edit un-defeats every live gate the executor was designed around (PathExecutor.h:540-545) and is a hard prerequisite for door handling (WS-D). forceRefresh()/needsRefresh() (CollisionMap.h:26-27) become moot — remove or keep for event-driven use.
  • B2 — scene-width clamp (S, same file): use the engine width already read into sw at CollisionMap.cpp:96 — clamp rebuild loops (:119-121, :133) and isInScene (:215-227) to min(sw, 110), zero-fill the remainder. Kills the 6-tile garbage band and the latent SEH-absorbed OOB read.
  • B3 — per-tick reachability flood (S-M): replace per-call full A in isTileReachable (PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639) with one capped BFS flood from the player tile, computed lazily on first query per tick and cached (110×110 bitset + tick stamp). The capped-BFS pattern already exists at findClosestPathIndex (cpp:1405-1444) — generalize it. Re-point all five consumers (:131, :763, :1070, :1684, :1708-1713). Eliminates the 15-17 full-A render-thread bursts (frame hitches) that fire exactly when the walker is struggling. This is better than Microbot, which recomputes its flood per call site.
  • B4 — gate interpolation on the flood (S, after B3): interpolateClickableTarget's radius probes (cpp:1775-1786) and especially the unvalidated geometric fallback (cpp:1803-1806) must require flood-reachability, substituting the furthest-reachable raw tile (function exists, :1690-1716) or falling to the no-click policy (:1085-1087).
  • B5 — off-path = BFS-failure (S): when findClosestPathIndex falls back to chebyshev argmin (cpp:1442-1444), that is the wall-separated state — flag it and trigger the off-path recalc immediately instead of masking it under the 10-tile chebyshev check (cpp:964-997) and waiting 12s for the stall watchdog.
  • Effort: M total. Impact: accuracy HIGH, speed MED-HIGH. Deps: none; B3 before B4/B5 and before WS-D.

docs.title: WS-C: Failure memory + search dedupe — speed-no-failed-edge-memory, speed-no-pathfinder-reuse-or-cache
docs.text:
• C1 — failed-edge blacklist (S-M): per-session unordered_set<int64_t> keyed packedOrigin<<32 | packedDest. Insert on Interact::perform failure (PathExecutor.cpp:690-697) and on transport timeout (:541-552) after 2 attempts. Thread an exclusion-set pointer through StaticPathfinder::findPath (StaticPathfinder.h:48-53) and check it at transport expansion (StaticPathfinder.cpp:383) and teleport seeding (:250). This converts every "edge we can't actually use" bug — including the unbounded quest-locked-door 6s-timeout loop the verdict found — into a one-time 6s cost. It is the safety net that de-risks every completeness fix later: land it before new edge types become fireable.
  • C2 — telemetry counters (S): atomic counters for recalc-by-cause (off-path / stall / transport-timeout / path-end-gap / unreachable), surfaced in DebugPanel + [Perf] prints. Currently these loops are invisible until a user reports a stuck bot.
  • C3 — same-goal walkTo dedupe (S): in PathExecutor::walkTo (cpp:65-72), if the new goal == m_finalGoalX/Y (+ same useTransports) and state is WALKING/WAITING_FOR_PATH → return true as a no-op. Today a script loop re-calling faster than the 5000ms budget cancels and restarts the search forever and never obtains a path — this is a livelock fix, not an optimization.
  • Effort: S-M. Impact: speed HIGH. Deps: none.

docs.title: WS-D: Door/obstacle handling — accuracy-no-dynamic-door-handling, accuracy-transport-anchor-size-hardcoded
docs.text:
• D1 — door probe v1 (M): at the exact point the executor today deliberately refuses to click (PathExecutor.cpp:1085-1087), insert a blocker probe: the WS-B flood gives the reachable frontier; find the path tile pair (reachable→unreachable); query the wall/game object on that boundary (Scene tile Wall slot per re_scene_tile_offsets, or ObjectQuery by tile); read its actions from TypeStruct+0xf8 (re_typestruct_actions); if a door-like name advertises "Open" (or "Slash" for webs), fire OPLOC1 via Interact::perform and continue the same path — no recalc needed since the static map already marks the doorway walkable (the StaticPathfinder.cpp:545-547 comment becomes the happy path). Suppress re-probing an opened door for ~10s.
  • D2 — quest-locked blacklist (S, after D1): if the click yields a dialogue/game-message instead of a state change (chat hook exists, re_chat_message_hook), insert the spanning walking edge into the WS-C blacklist and recalc.
  • D3 — anchor snap (S): route the transport-object resolution at PathExecutor.cpp:630-681 through dedupeByAnchor (ObjectQuery.cpp:108-128) — or replicate its SW-anchor snap + LocType size backfill — instead of raw byId + hardcoded sizeX/sizeY=1 (:680-681). Per re_oploc_anchor_in_api/GameObject.cpp:80-82, non-anchor footprint tiles are silently dropped server-side.
  • Stage, don't port wholesale: single doors + gates + webs v1; double-door family grouping v2; skip the ~15-entry exception table and rockfall handler (see do-not-bother).
  • Effort: M (v1). Impact: accuracy HIGH and speed HIGH (kills the 12-48s stall-escalation class on the most common dynamic obstacle in the game). Deps: B1 (fresh collision — doors are invisible without it), B3 (cheap probes), C1 (blacklist).

docs.title: WS-E: Requirement evaluation + curated no-go data — completeness-requirements-unevaluated, completeness-var-operator-coverage, accuracy-blocked-edges-restrictions-unbound, completeness-wilderness-model-absent (v1)
docs.text:
