• E1 — typed parsing (S): parse skillsRaw/questsRaw/itemIdsRaw/currencyRaw/varplayersRaw into typed fields at TSV load (Transport.cpp:101-111 currently stores write-only strings). Parse the Consumable column while in there (one getCol).
  • E2 — account-state snapshot (M): extend the established refreshUsableTeleports pattern (dllmain.cpp:614-669, PathfinderConfig.h:71-78 threading note): each game tick, build a snapshot on the render thread — skill levels (boosted), inventory+equipment+bank item set, varps — push into PathfinderConfig under the existing mutex. isAllowed (PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57) evaluates skills/items/currency/varplayers against the snapshot on the worker. Quests: v1 via RuneLite-lifted quest varp/varbit tables (kTODO-marked); the CS2 QUEST_STATUS_GET=4029 primitive (re_cs2_intstack, live-verified) is the better long-term source but needs engine-thread marshal — cache results with a TTL, don't call per-edge.
  • E3 — full operator grammar (S): implement >, <, & (BIT_SET), @ (cooldown-minutes, epoch-minute delta) in checkVarbitString (PathfinderConfig.cpp:59-112) for both varbits and varplayers, per TransportVarbit.java:18-33 semantics. Pre-parse to structs at load, not per-eval.
  • E4 — blocked_edges + restrictions (S-M): bind both shipped files (FILE_BINDINGS, TransportRegistry.cpp:17-42) into a packed-key edge set (with Bidirectional) and a restricted-tile set; check in walking expansion (StaticPathfinder.cpp:359 step), transport expansion, and PathSmoother LOS. Dynamic half: an AGILITY/GRAPPLE shortcut that fails E2 requirements inserts its origin→dest as a blocked walking edge (Microbot's PathfinderConfig.java:509-514/:598-604 mechanism), reusing the WS-C set plumbing.
  • E5 — wilderness v1 (S): compute wilderness level from coords; gate teleport seeding on startWildyLevel <= t->maxWildernessLevel (kills the guaranteed click-fail class given start-only seeding); add an avoidWilderness tile filter in expansion. Full band state machine + frontier injection deferred (Phase 4).
  • Effort: M overall. Impact: completeness HIGH, speed HIGH — the audit calls unfiltered transports "the dominant stall source"; this removes the wrong-path class at graph-build time instead of discovering it at click time. Deps: C1 recommended first (net under new rejection logic); E4-dynamic depends on E2.

docs.title: WS-F: Terminal states, blocked goals, recalc discipline — speed-blocked-goal-burns-full-budget, accuracy-silent-inexact-arrival, speed-recalc-storms-unbounded, speed-no-partial-path-lookahead-handoff, speed-slow-stuck-escalation-no-retry, accuracy-arrival-api-contract-defects
docs.text:
• F1 — blocked-goal short-circuit (S): in walkTo, if the goal tile is statically unwalkable and the player is already within a small radius → ARRIVED immediately (Microbot Rs2Walker.java:996-1000 pattern). Otherwise mark goalBlocked and run the static search with a reduced budget — burning the full 5000ms (PathExecutor.cpp:293) to discover what a static-map lookup already knew is pure idle.
  • F2 — partial-path semantics (S): plumb result.found through consumePendingStatic (cpp:350-369, currently log-only) into an m_partialPath flag; cap partial-path recalcs at 3 (counter at the :753-758 trigger), then terminate in a new UNREACHABLE state (repurpose the unused STUCK enum, PathExecutor.h:112). Surface via a Walk::state() enum; fix the contract defects in the same pass: unwired hasArrived() returning true (Walk.cpp:248 → false + add Walk::isReady()), and the Walk.h:26-28 doc/behavior mismatch (implementation is right — fix the doc).
  • F3 — lookahead recalc (M): when m_partialPath and within ~10 waypoints of segment end, dispatch the next static search from the current position while continuing to click the remaining waypoints (new background-recalc flag; swap path on arrival). Eliminates the dead-stop-per-segment on every long route. Add a 3500ms-class cooldown between partial recalcs.
  • F4 — recalc discipline (S): global ~1.5s cross-trigger recalc cooldown (transport-success exempt); count recalcs into WS-C telemetry. Thread-per-recalc is acceptable for now given cancelFlag semantics — don't build an executor pool yet.
  • F5 — faster stuck escalation (S): sidestep on the first 12s stall instead of the second (PathExecutor.h:396), and add a click-issued-but-position-unchanged tick counter to attempt sidestep at ~5-6s; on give-up, one automatic full recalc retry before UNREACHABLE (never silent IDLE, cpp:926-931). Optional: drop the 5000ms budget to Microbot's 3000ms after WS-I's underground wrap lands (the wrap removes a major false no-progress class).
  • F6 — signal inexact arrivals (S): record final chebyshev-to-goal at ARRIVED and expose it (Walk::arrivalDistance()); mercy-arrivals (cpp:873-878, :908-913) and post-pin silent accepts (:788-795) become detectable instead of indistinguishable from exact landings.
  • Effort: M total. Impact: speed MED-HIGH, accuracy MED. Deps: none hard; F2 before F3.

docs.title: WS-G: Teleport item/minigame/multi-dest enablement — completeness-teleport-item-minigame-seasonal-unsearched, completeness-multidest-and-home-teleport-excluded, completeness-minigames-tsv-header-bug, speed-per-tick-teleport-recompute, part of completeness-executor-handler-coverage
docs.text:
• G1 — header fix (S, immediate): TransportRegistry.cpp:95-117 — adopt Microbot's semantics (first non-comment line is the header, # optional, Transport.java:475-535). Without this, fixing seeding silently leaves minigames at 0/20 rows.
  • G2 — handler table (S-M): replace the single m_fireTeleportSpellFn (PathExecutor.h:147-149) with a per-TransportType handler map, and make the edge-fire path dispatch by type instead of unconditionally building TargetKind::Object (cpp:672-681 — today an NPC row fires OPLOC1 against an NPC id, an invalid packet). Add a graph-side capability gate: only admit edge types with a registered handler (today: object-click types + TELEPORTATION_SPELL). This is the prior roadmap's "per-type enable flags," now confirmed as an active bug fix, and it must land before WS-H floods the graph with NPC/widget edges.
  • G3 — TELEPORTATION_ITEM end-to-end (M): widen all three gates the verdict found — refreshUsableTeleports filter (dllmain.cpp:624), seeding filter (StaticPathfinder.cpp:250), executor branch. Usability = Inventory::contains || Equipment::isWearing (E2 snapshot). Fire = inventory/equipped item interact with the action keyword from displayInfo, dialogue/menu continuation via Resume*Dialog wire packets (P2GR catalog) rather than widget clicking. Jewellery + tabs first; scroll books later.
  • G4 — ':' grammar + Home Teleport (S): implement prefix:suffix displayInfo resolution at refresh (dllmain.cpp:625) and in the fire callback (dllmain.cpp:1451-1503) — the suffix selects the spell-widget menu op (IfButton/IfSubOp packet with op index). Home Teleport: fix the name-resolution miss (TSV "Lumbridge Home Teleport" vs Spells.cpp:81 "Home Teleport" — add alias), drop the level==0 exclusion (dllmain.cpp:629), and generalize the flat 6s timeout (PathExecutor.h:182) to max(6000, duration*600 + margin) per edge — needed for the ~21s home teleport and later for boats.
  • G5 — refresh memoization (S, while in this code): fingerprint (inventory hash, magic level, spellbook varbit, bank-cache generation) and skip the per-tick rebuild on no change. Matters more once item teleports multiply the per-tick work. Keep the render-thread snapshot architecture — it is the correct threading answer; only the redundant recompute is waste.
  • Effort: M-L. Impact: completeness HIGH (jewellery/tabs are the dominant fast-travel class), speed HIGH indirectly. Deps: C1 (failure net), E2 (item snapshot), G2 before G3.

docs.title: WS-H: Permutation networks + network verbs — completeness-permutation-expansion-absent, rest of completeness-executor-handler-coverage
docs.text:
• H1 — cartesian expansion (M): post-load pass in TransportRegistry replicating Transport.java:537-613: per-network bucketing of origin-only/dest-only rows, cartesian product with per-network radiusThreshold (gliders 6, spirit 5, quetzal 6, balloon 7, mushtree 5, fairy 0), merge ctor (requirements union, duration max, displayInfo from dest, action/objectId from origin). Two SafeRS-specific traps: distinguish "blank cell = permute" (network files) from "blank origin = origin-less teleport" via a per-file flag in FILE_BINDINGS; and do the expansion before the reserve-then-store-pointers step (TransportRegistry.cpp:148-177) or the pointer table dangles.
  • H2 — network verbs, one vertical at a time, each behind its G2 capability flag: fairy rings first (highest route value; needs E2 quest gate + dramen/lunar staff check + dial interface via IfButton packets), then NPC-dialogue boats/ships (OPNPC1 + Resume*Dialog packets — strictly better than Microbot's widget-click chains), then spirit trees, then gliders/charter/quetzal maps.
  • Effort: M (H1) + L (H2, amortized). Impact: completeness HIGH. Deps: G2 (capability gate — H1 without it floods the graph with unfireable/misfiring edges), E1-E3 (these networks are quest/item-gated as a category), C1.

docs.title: WS-I: Plane correctness — accuracy-no-cross-plane-goal, accuracy-smoother-start-plane-bug, accuracy-underground-y-heuristic-missing
docs.text:
• I1 — plane plumbing (M): the search nodes already carry plane bits — only reconstruction drops them (StaticPathfinder.cpp:476-484 unpacks X/Y only). Add plane to PathNode (Pathfinder.h:10-12); pack the goal with the requested plane (StaticPathfinder.cpp:178-179) — termination already requires exact packed match, so goal support is plumbing, not redesign. Walk::to(x,y,plane) overload, PathExecutor::walkTo goal-plane member, plane-aware arrival (cpp:716-722), stop hardcoding Dax goal z=0 (cpp:189), Lua overloads (ScriptAPI.cpp:389-429).
  • I2 — per-segment smoothing (S-M, with I1): split the path at plane changes; smooth each segment with its own plane; segment boundaries (transport origins and destinations) are non-collapsible anchors — fixing both the wrong-plane LOS validation and the missing-destination-anchor gap vs Pathfinder.java:187-203.
  • I3 — mod-6400 heuristic wrap (S): h = min(direct, wrapped) per Pathfinder.java:224-247, one helper applied at the hCost sites (StaticPathfinder.cpp:103-109 et al.). Fixes inadmissible overestimates for every dungeon-bound search and the premature-partial class; prerequisite for safely lowering the budget to 3000ms (F5).
  • Effort: M. Impact: accuracy HIGH (eliminates the systematic silent wrong-floor arrival class). Deps: none; independent of WS-E/G/H, parallelizable.

docs.title: Drive-bys (bundle into whichever PR touches the file)
docs.text:
• speed-local-astar-iteration-cap: bump MAX_ITERATIONS (Pathfinder.h:62) to ~20000 (iterations count duplicate pops). One line.
  • accuracy-walksmart-double-instance-translation: guard maybeTranslateInstanceGoal — reject inputs already inside the live instance band (RegionBaseX/Y already read at Walk.cpp:53-56). ~5 lines; closes the unverified-idempotence hole at Walk.cpp:188/219.
  • accuracy-permissive-degradation-on-offset-failure: cheap collision health check at scene load — compare N known tiles vs the static map; on mismatch or m_valid=false, log loudly + telemetry flag. Don't redesign the permissive policy; just make failure visible. Pair with the next game-update playbook.

docs.title: 2. Recommended execution order
docs.text:
Phase 0 — quick wins / de-risking (all S, ~days): 1. WS-A run toggle + run-on (single biggest speed lever, zero deps) 2. WS-C3 same-goal dedupe (livelock fix) 3. WS-B1+B2 collision refresh + width clamp (one file; unblocks doors) 4. WS-C1+C2 failed-edge blacklist + telemetry (safety net before anything adds edges) 5. WS-G1 minigame header fix, WS-G2 capability gate (stops NPC-edge misfires today), drive-bys

Phase 1 — speed/accuracy core (M): 6. WS-B3-B5 reachability flood + consumers 7. WS-D door handling v1 + anchor snap (depends 3,4,6) 8. WS-F blocked-goal short-circuit, UNREACHABLE terminal, lookahead recalc, faster escalation 9. WS-A potions (v1.1)

Phase 2 — graph correctness (M, parallelizable with Phase 1 tail): 10. WS-E1-E4 requirements + operators + blocked_edges/restrictions 11. WS-E5 wilderness v1 gate 12. WS-I plane correctness + underground wrap (independent file area — can run parallel to 10-11)

Phase 3 — completeness expansion: 13. WS-G3-G5 teleport items + ':' grammar + Home Teleport + refresh memo 14. WS-H1 permutation expansion (now safe behind capability gates + requirements) 15. WS-H2 verbs: fairy rings → NPC boats → spirit trees → gliders/charter/quetzal

Phase 4 — long pole: 16. Full wilderness band machine + frontier teleport injection (completeness-teleports-start-only-seeding proper fix) 17. POH integration (completeness-poh-transports-absent — needs registry runtime-injection rework + POH-instance start remap) 18. Banked-transport planning (completeness-banked-transport-planning — direct-vs-via-bank comparison; reuses E2 bank snapshot)

Prior-roadmap validation against the verified gap data: - "type+displayInfo on PathTransportEdge" — DONE (edges are type-gated at PathExecutor.cpp:587/614; spells fire by displayInfo). - "executor TELEPORTATION_SPELL branch via Magic::cast" and "availability via canCast + RunePouch/Bank" — DONE (cpp:587-628 incl. bank-rune sequence; refreshUsableTeleports). - "stop dropping non-object edges in StaticPathfinder" — INVALIDATED by the refuted claim: zero shipped rows fail the action parse; non-object edges already enter the graph. The real problem is the inverse — they enter and misfire as OPLOC1 against NPC ids. Re-scoped to WS-G2 (type dispatch + capability gate). - "per-type enable flags" — CONFIRMED and upgraded from future-proofing to an active bug fix (WS-G2, Phase 0). - "then items (keyword resolution + dialogue + Consumable column)" — CONFIRMED as Phase 3, with additions the prior roadmap missed: the minigame header bug (G1), ':' multi-dest grammar + Home Teleport alias (G4), and per-edge duration-based timeouts.

docs.title: 3. Where NOT to copy Microbot (native client does better)
docs.text:
Area Microbot approach Do instead Run toggle / potion dosing Orb mouse-click + blocking sleeps IfButton/wire packet via EngineDispatch; tick-counted intervals, zero sleeps Door opening Camera-turn prep + canvas click + sleepUntil OPLOC1 packet with always-on spoof (feedback_doaction_must_spoof); no camera/LOS needed; tick-based state poll Dialogue transports (boats/ships/NPCs) Widget click chains with per-step sleeps OPNPC1 + Resume*Dialog wire packets from the P2GR catalog — faster, focus-independent, multi-client safe Fairy ring dials Widget click rotation IfButton/IfSubOp packets per dial press Quest state Hand-maintained varbit tables CS2 QUEST_STATUS_GET=4029 via EngineDispatch (live-verified), TTL-cached; varbit tables only as v1 bootstrap Reachability BFS flood recomputed per call site One per-tick cached flood (WS-B3) — strictly cheaper Pathfinder readiness 1200ms poll slices + random sleeps Keep onFrame consumption (speed-adv-frame-rate-consumption-eager-map) Minimap walking Sets minimap zoom to 5 before clicking Never write zoom; we project with live zoom (re_minimap_zoom) Persona thresholds mix64(name)^installSeed Reuse existing MovementProfile FNV-1a seeding

Regression guards (the two ADVANTAGE entries): any ported Microbot behavior arrives stripped of its sleeps, mouse emulation, and zoom manipulation. Protect: packet-dispatch click path (PathExecutor.cpp:1248-1312), frame-rate async consumption (:1252-1254), no-recalc transport handoff + same-tick chain advance (:483-517, :554-566), eager SCM1 load. Note the verdict correction: Microbot's collision map is also eager all-RAM — don't cite lazy-zip as our edge; the real edges are click latency and handoff.

docs.title: 4. Do-not-bother list
docs.text:
1. speed-no-bidirectional-search — 2000+ tile single-target requests are rare; the progress-reset budget keeps them alive; high implementation complexity (reverse transport index). No meaningful idle-time win.
  2. speed-visited-hashset-vs-bitset — micro-optimization; reserve(8192) mitigates. Revisit only if WS-C2 telemetry shows worker searches pressing the budget after the underground-wrap fix.
  3. Canoe state machine (part of executor coverage) — largest per-transport verb effort in Microbot's table for routes teleports/fairy rings dominate anyway. Permanently behind a disabled flag.
  4. SEASONAL transports (169 rows) — leagues-only content; irrelevant to production accounts.
  5. Consumable-vs-reusable preference engine (completeness-consumable-preference-absent, second half) — Microbot ships it default-disabled (maxSimilarTransportDistance=0). Do parse the column (E1, one line); don't build filterSimilarTransports' 200-line centroid pruner.
  6. completeness-multi-target-unsupported — real but low: Bank::nearestBank's straight-line guess is usually right, and goal-set termination is easy to add later if AccountBuilder demands it. Not worth scheduling now.
  7. Microbot's ~15-entry object exception table + Motherlode rockfall handler — content-specific patches; add individual entries only when a shipped script hits one.
  8. Full Microbot-parity double-door family components / diagonal corner probes — door v1 + blacklist covers the cost-dominant cases; escalate only if telemetry shows residual door stalls.
  9. Recalc thread pool — thread-per-recalc is fine once F4's cooldown + C1's blacklist bound recalc frequency; cancelFlag already prevents useful-work pileup.
  10. Fail-closed redesign of the collision offset chain — the permissive degradation is a deliberate trade; the cheap health-check alarm (drive-by) plus the existing game-update offset playbook is the right-sized fix.

Bottom line: Phase 0 is roughly a week of S-effort changes that capture the single largest speed win (run energy), fix two livelock/loop classes (same-goal dedupe, failed-edge memory), and un-defeat the live-collision design — and every later workstream gets safer because of items 4-5. The completeness program (G/H) is exactly the prior roadmap's shape, but the verification moved its first step: the capability gate and failure memory go in before any new transport class, because the audit's most expensive recurring cost is not missing edges — it is edges the executor fires into a 6-second timeout forever.

docs.title: [critical / speed] speed-no-run-energy-management
docs.text:
No run-energy management — walker never toggles run or doses stamina/energy potions

Ours: Run handling is completely ABSENT from PathExecutor (zero references). srs::api::Player::toggleRunEnergy exists but delegates to GameData::setRunToggle which is an explicit stub ('needs DoAction wired up'). No automatic run-on at any energy threshold, no potion usage.

Microbot: manageRunEnergy runs every processWalk pass: enables run when energy>10, doses stamina/energy/super-energy potions when path >=20 tiles remain and energy is below a per-account persona-seeded threshold (FNV-1a(name)^installSeed, 12-24 'hardcore' or 35-55 'casual'), 10s min interval. walkFastCanvas also toggles run.

Why it matters: Walk speed is literally 2x with run on. A bot that walks (not runs) any fraction of thousands of daily paths pays the single largest time penalty in this entire comparison — dwarfing every recalc/stall optimization. This is also a behavioral fingerprint: real players run.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate with two minor precision fixes. (1) The stub spans GameData.cpp:214-223 (printf at :220-221); note it returns TRUE after doing nothing (false-success to callers) — it reads varp 173 via getRunToggle (:207-212) and early-returns false only if already in the desired state, then logs '[GameData] setRunToggle -- stub, needs DoAction wired up' with a '// TODO: actually send the DoAction toggle' comment. (2) Player::toggleRunEnergy is Player.cpp:93-97 (not 93-96). Everything else holds exactly: zero run/energy/stamina references in E:\SafeRS\OSRSClient\Pathfinding\PathExecutor.cpp (or anywhere in Pathfinding/), no potion dosing anywhere in the walker stack, and the only consumers of the inert toggle are the Lua binding (ScriptAPI.cpp:1844-1846) and the API facade. Microbot side verified verbatim: Rs2Walker.manageRunEnergy (:2226-2245) called per processWalk pass (:1272) — run-on when energy>10, stamina/energy/super-energy dose when pathRemaining>=20 (STAMINA_MIN_PATH_TILES, :2174) and energy below FNV-1a(lowercase name)^installSeed persona threshold (computeStaminaThreshold :2185-2198; 30% 'hardcore' 12-24, else 'casual' 35-55, constants :2166-2173), 10s min interval (:2175); walkFastCanvas(WorldPoint,boolean) toggles run at :2381/2386.

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor — run references absent; GameSDK/GameData.cpp:214-220 (stub); PluginAPI/API/Player.cpp:93-96 | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:2226-2245 (manageRunEnergy), :2185-2198 (computeStaminaThreshold), :2386 (walkFastCanvas run toggle)

docs.title: [critical / completeness] completeness-requirements-unevaluated
docs.text:
PRIOR GAP 2 CONFIRMED: 6 of 8 requirement dimensions stubbed (skills/quests/items/currency/varplayers/wilderness) — search routes through unusable transports, producing repeating 6s timeout + recalc loops

Ours: PathfinderConfig::isAllowed evaluates only isMembers + varbit '=' (PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57). skillsRaw/questsRaw/itemIdsRaw/currencyRaw/varplayersRaw/maxWildernessLevel are stored as raw strings on Transport with no reader anywhere (Transport.h:57-62); item IDs are never even tokenized to ints (ours-transports §2). Stub status re-verified on disk: PathfinderConfig.h:11-17 lists Skills/Quests/Items/Varplayers/maxWildernessLevel as 'STUBBED (returns true)'. Consequence: a low-Agility account is routed through high-level shortcuts and quest-gated transports; failure is discovered only at click time → 6s TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS (PathExecutor.h:182) → recalc → the search re-picks the SAME cost-optimal edge, a repeating loop since the graph never learns the edge is unusable. ours-transports calls unfiltered transports 'the dominant stall source'.

Microbot: useTransport gate pipeline (PathfinderConfig.java:798-888): feature toggles incl. F2P-world hard-denylist of 14 member types (:975-1049), BOOSTED skill levels (:908-919), quest state-order comparison NOT_STARTED<IN_PROGRESS<FINISHED (TransportRequirementPolicy.java:14-26), varbit AND varplayer operators, currency vs inventory/bank (:837-853), teleport-item mode, spell runes, generic any-of item matching vs an inv+equip+bank snapshot (:1066-1079), Chronicle charge tracking (:1107-1138), plus network-level quest pre-gates: fairy rings need Fairytale II + dramen/lunar staff, gliders Grand Tree, spirit trees Tree Gnome Village, quetzals Twilight's Promise (:305-312). Failed AGILITY/GRAPPLE shortcuts additionally insert their origin→dest as a BLOCKED walking edge so the search cannot even walk through the gap (PathfinderConfig.java:509-514, 598-604).

Why it matters: The graph is systematically over-permissive: every path through a requirement-gated transport the account fails is a wrong path, and at production volume this is the largest recurring stall source we have — each occurrence costs 6s dead time plus a 5s-class recalc and repeats on the same route until the 12-15s stall watchdogs escalate to sidestep/give-up IDLE (script dead). Microbot avoids the entire class at graph-build time. It also blocks ever shipping fairy rings/gliders safely, since those networks are quest-gated as a category.

Verification (high confidence): Claim confirmed on current disk (2026-06-10 uncommitted changes included) with one refinement: the "6 of 8 dimensions stubbed" statement is exactly true for origin-bearing (object) transports — agility shortcuts, quest-gated doors, currency-gated boats — which are gated solely by PathfinderConfig::isAllowed (PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57: isMembers + varbit '=' only) at StaticPathfinder.cpp:383. However, TELEPORTATION_SPELL transports DO get skill (magic level) and item (runes, incl. cached-bank) evaluation via the render-thread refreshUsableTeleports (dllmain.cpp:614-669) consulted at StaticPathfinder.cpp:255 — though it resolves via the Spells table by displayInfo, not the Transport raw requirement strings, so the "no reader anywhere" statement about skillsRaw/questsRaw/itemIdsRaw/currencyRaw/varplayersRaw/maxWildernessLevel remains literally true (writes only, Transport.cpp:101-111; zero reads repo-wide). The timeout-recalc loop is real: TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS=6000.0 (PathExecutor.h:182), timeout → recalculatePath() (PathExecutor.cpp:477, 541-551), which re-runs the identical pathfinder/config (PathExecutor.cpp:214-266) with no failed-edge blacklist anywhere; the 2026-06-10 uncommitted PathExecutor changes added multi-step chain-advance (:488-517), not failure learning. Only escape hatch is the caller-level walkTo(useTransports=false) blunt switch (PathExecutor.cpp:65-72, StaticPathfinder.h:43-53), which disables ALL transports, not the failing one.

Citations: ours-search: PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57, 77-81; PathfinderConfig.h:11-17 (stub list, re-verified on disk 2026-06-10); Transport.h:52, 57-62 (no reader); StaticPathfinder.cpp:383 | ours-executor: PathExecutor.h:182; PathExecutor.cpp:541-552 | ours-transports: §4 (stubbed columns, stall consequences — PathExecutor.h:252, 396-397), §9 (stall constants) | mb-transports: PathfinderConfig.java:798-888, 908-919, 975-1049, 1066-1079, 1107-1138, 305-312, 509-514, 598-604; TransportRequirementPolicy.java:14-26 | mb-search: PathfinderConfig.java:475-528 (blocked-edge decomposition); Pathfinder.java:381-399 | prior-audit gap 2: CONFIRMED

docs.title: [critical / accuracy] accuracy-no-dynamic-door-handling
docs.text:
No door/obstacle handling outside the transport catalog — closed doors, gates, webs, and rockfalls are invisible obstacles causing 12-48s stall-escalation and walk abandonment

Ours: The executor's only obstacle verbs are object-transport Interact::perform (PathExecutor.cpp:687) and the teleport-spell callback (cpp:588/615); the full tick loop (audited end-to-end, cpp:433-1245) contains no door detection, no path-edge blocker probe, no closed-variant 'Open' resolution, no quest-locked-door blacklisting, no rockfall handler — the only obstacle-adjacent logic is wall-distance click adjustment (cpp:1641-1688). Doors exist only as catalog TSV TRANSPORT rows (TransportType.h:11; grep: 'door' appears only in comments in Pathfinding/). A closed door across the path fails the live-reachability gate (cpp:1070), falls back to the furthest-reachable raw tile (cpp:1076-1084), walks up to the door, deliberately does not click (cpp:1085-1087), then waits out the watchdogs: 12s stall → recalc that yields the SAME path (the static map marks the doorway walkable) → sidestep after 2 stalls (≥24s) → IDLE give-up after 4 (≥48s) (cpp:898-946). The stale collision snapshot (separate gap) means live checks may not even see the closed state.

Microbot: Multi-stage door chain: per-path-edge WallObject/GameObject probes with orientation matching (Rs2Walker.java:3509-3747, Rs2DoorAheadResolver.java:15-37), door-like name/action tables (:632-643), diagonal corner probes, path-adjacent blocker scan grouping double doors into family components (:4727-4927, :4969-5129), quest-locked door dialogue detection with session blacklist + restriction refresh + recalc (:3301-3308, :3709-3719), 10s opened-door suppression memory (:3292-3293), post-door fast minimap continuation click (:3985-4027), unreachable-path-tile recovery (:1497-1638), slashable webs and ~15 object exceptions (:6320-6496), closed-trapdoor 'Open' variant resolution for catalog transports (:5893-5957), Motherlode rockfall handler (:2855-2897), all throttled/gated against catalog transports so the two systems never fight (:4210-4241), plus a startup policy so none of this delays the first click (:297-332).

Why it matters: Closed doors and gates are among the most common dynamic obstacles in the game (farm gates, building interiors, city gates closed by other players) and sit on a huge fraction of real routes. Each un-handled one costs 12s minimum, often 48s, and frequently terminates the walk in IDLE without arriving — a top-tier reliability and accuracy failure at production path volumes. Microbot's improvement plan invested more code in doors than in the search itself — strong evidence of production impact.

Verification (high confidence): Claim confirmed against current on-disk code including 2026-06-10 uncommitted changes. The executor's only obstacle verbs are catalog-transport Interact::perform (PathExecutor.cpp:687) and teleport-spell callbacks (cpp:588, 615). Grep for door/gate/web/rockfall across Pathfinding/ hits comments only; PluginAPI/API has zero door logic (Walk.cpp: no matches). Closed-door-on-path behavior is exactly as claimed: live-reachability gate at cpp:1070 (isTileReachable), raw-path fallback cpp:1076-1084, then deliberate no-click ("Leave haveTarget=false so we don't click. Stall timer + recompute will handle it.", cpp:1085-1087); stall escalation block at cpp:898-946 with STALL_THRESHOLD_MS=12000 (PathExecutor.h:252), MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_SIDESTEP=2 / MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_GIVE_UP=4 (h:396-397), so ~12s recalc / ~24s sidestep / ~48s IDLE give-up (stallMultiplier can stretch these 1.5-2x in combat/interim-minimap). StaticPathfinder.cpp:545-547 explicitly acknowledges the failure mode: recalc returns the same path "closed door because the static map marks the tile as walkable". Minor corrections: (1) the collision file is GameSDK/CollisionMap.cpp (not Pathfinding/) — update() is called every game tick (dllmain.cpp:741) but the same-region fast path (CollisionMap.cpp:89-92) returns the cached snapshot, so within-region door-state flips are invisible; forceRefresh() (CollisionMap.h:26) still has zero callers. (2) Doors that ARE in the transports.tsv catalog do get clicked correctly via transport edges (including multi-step chain advance, cpp:479-517) — the gap is strictly doors/gates/webs/rockfalls outside the catalog or normally-open doors closed at runtime, as the claim's title states. (3) The 2026-06-10 uncommitted changes add only async path-request timeout watchdogs (PATH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=20s → IDLE), DaxWalker WinHTTP timeouts, a Pathfinder scene-bounds guard, and delete GlobalCollisionMap — no door handling. Microbot contrast verified: handleDoors at Rs2Walker.java:3509/3513, handleDoorsWithTimeout :4429, handleRockfall :2855, raw-path door recovery :3098/:3131/:3140, and util/walker/door/ package with Rs2DoorAheadResolver.java (49 lines) + Rs2DoorHandler.java.

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor.cpp:687, 588, 1070, 1076-1087 (no-click stall fallback), 898-946; §1 (full tick-loop gate inventory cpp:433-1245 — no door logic present), §3 (only two fire verbs); wall-adjust only cpp:1641-1688 | ours-transports: TransportType.h:11; §9 (stall constants: 12s stall, sidestep at 2, give-up at 4) | ours-collision: finding 1 — CollisionMap.cpp:89-92 stale snapshot, forceRefresh zero callers — closed doors invisible to live checks | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:3509-3747 (handleDoors), :4727-4927 + :4969-5129 (path-adjacent blocker, double-door families), :3709-3719 (quest-lock blacklist + recalc), :3985-4027 (post-door fast click), :3292-3293 (opened-door memory), :1497-1638 (unreachable-path-tile recovery), :6320-6496 (webs + exceptions), :5893-5957 (closed-variant resolution), :2855-2897 (rockfall), :4210-4241 (transport gating), :297-332 (startup policy); door/Rs2DoorAheadResolver.java:15-37

docs.title: [critical / accuracy] accuracy-stale-live-collision-snapshot
docs.text:
Live collision snapshot only rebuilds on region change — forceRefresh has ZERO callers, so every reachability gate runs on scene-load-time data and door state changes are invisible until a scene crossing

Ours: CollisionMap::update() takes a fast path and returns without re-reading engine memory whenever the region base is unchanged (CollisionMap.cpp:89-92, verified in working tree); forceRefresh() exists but has zero callers (CollisionMap.h:26, grep-confirmed). Door/gate state changes after scene load are invisible until a scene-boundary crossing. Every 'live' check the executor relies on consumes this stale snapshot: isTileReachable (PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639), the smoothed-waypoint reachability gate (cpp:1070), adjustForWallDistance probes (cpp:1641-1688), findClosestPathIndex BFS (cpp:1385-1445), canTraverse, and tryDirectShortWalk (cpp:129-144). This silently defeats PathExecutor.h:543-544's stated purpose: catching a closed door the static map doesn't know about BEFORE clicking.

Microbot: Reads collision flags live from the client on every query (no snapshot layer), and even does live game-object lookups inside the search hotpath where collision data lies (ToA region handling, CollisionMap.java:159-176). Its reachability checks (isNearPath BFS, getClosestTileIndex) therefore always see current door state; door opens/closes are reflected immediately in reachability and click decisions.

Why it matters: Reachability gating of picked tiles is a focus accuracy mechanism, and ours is built on data that is wrong the moment any door or gate changes state — including doors the script itself just opened. A door opened mid-walk still reads as blocked → walker refuses valid clicks → stall watchdog cycles; a door closed mid-walk reads as open → wasted clicks into a wall. Both convert directly into idle seconds, recurring thousands of times per day, and the gap nullifies the one mechanism we built specifically to bridge static-vs-live disagreement.

Verification (high confidence): SafeRS side is accurate as claimed: CollisionMap::update() short-circuits when region base is unchanged (E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/GameSDK/CollisionMap.cpp:89-92) and forceRefresh() (CollisionMap.h:26) plus needsRefresh() (h:27) have zero callers repo-wide. update() IS called every game tick (dllmain.cpp:741) — staleness is purely the fast path, not missing cadence. g_collisionProvider = g_collisionMap (dllmain.cpp:1275) feeds both Pathfinder (1316) and PathExecutor (1322); PathExecutor holds it as const ICollisionProvider& so it cannot refresh. All cited consumers confirmed in working tree: isTileReachable (PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639, which also calls m_pathfinder.findPath over the same snapshot), smoothed-waypoint gate (cpp:1070-1087), adjustForWallDistance (cpp:1641-1688), findClosestPathIndex BFS canTraverse (cpp:1434), tryDirectShortWalk (cpp:124-144); design-intent comment is at PathExecutor.h:540-545 (claim said 543-544). Blast radius is wider than claimed: plugin-facing srs::api Tile/Walk also consume the stale snapshot (PluginAPI/API/Tile.cpp:10-27, Walk.cpp:135). CORRECTION on Microbot: its shortestpath A* hotpath does NOT read live client collision — it uses the static SplitFlagMap (same Skretzo dataset SafeRS ported), and CollisionMap.java:159-176 is only a 5s-cached region-ID helper for the ToA puzzle ground-object special case, not live collision reads. The live reads happen in its reachability/click-gating utilities: Rs2Tile.getReachableTilesFromTileInternal reads wv.getCollisionMaps()[plane].getFlags() fresh per call (Rs2Tile.java:369-373), consumed by Rs2Walker.getClosestTileIndex (Rs2Walker.java:5373-5383), isNearPath (6771-6790), and direct flag reads (2089-2090). So the comparative gap is real exactly where it matters — the reachability gates: Microbot's see current door state, SafeRS's see scene-load-time state.

docs.title: [critical / completeness] completeness-permutation-expansion-absent
docs.text:
PRIOR GAP 4 CONFIRMED: no origin×destination permutation expansion — fairy rings, spirit trees, gliders, balloons, mushtrees, quetzals, obelisks contribute ZERO graph edges

Ours: Transport::fromTsvRow hard-requires a Destination (Transport.cpp:93-96) and treats empty Origin as an origin-less teleport (Transport.cpp:88-92); no cartesian-product logic exists anywhere (grep 'permutat' over OSRSClient: 0 hits, re-verified 2026-06-10). Measured against shipped TSVs: fairy_rings 109 rows -> 0 usable edges (54 origin-only rejected, 55 dest-only stranded as never-seeded 'teleports'); spirit_trees 132/144 rejected -> 0 usable; gnome_gliders 0/22; hot_air_balloons 0/51; magic_mushtrees 0/12; quetzals 0/28; wilderness_obelisks 0/60; minecarts only 14 of 47 rows usable. Net ~363 rows rejected at parse + ~560 loaded-but-unreachable while logging as 'loaded'.

Microbot: addTransports (Transport.java:537-584) buckets origin-only and dest-only rows into transportOrigins/transportDestinations and expands the full cartesian product, skipping self-pairs within per-network radiusThreshold (gliders=6, spirit_trees=5, quetzals=6, balloons=7, mushtrees=5, fairy_rings=0; Transport.java:590-613). The merge constructor (Transport.java:126-171) takes requirements union, duration max, displayInfo from the destination row (the interface option — what makes the edge executable) and action from the origin row.

Why it matters: Entire long-distance transport networks are absent from the search graph while logging as 'loaded'. Fairy rings and spirit trees are the backbone of mid/late-game routing; their absence forces multi-minute walking detours on thousands of daily paths and makes large regions (Zanaris, Ape Atoll fringe, Poison Waste, Varlamore quetzal net) effectively unroutable without manual scripting. Compounds with the executor verb gap — but the data layer is the blocker first.

Verification (high confidence): Gap confirmed in current code with minor numeric corrections. E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/Pathfinding/Transport.cpp:90-92 treats empty Origin as origin-less; :93-96 hard-rejects empty Destination (returns false). TransportRegistry.cpp:121-126 counts those as 'rejected'; :171-177 buckets origin-less rows into m_teleports. StaticPathfinder.cpp:248-250 seeds only TransportType::TELEPORTATION_SPELL from m_teleports, so all network dest-only rows are loaded but unreachable. No permutation/cartesian logic exists (grep 'permutat|cartesian|transportOrigins|transportDestinations|radiusThreshold' over OSRSClient = 0 hits outside this audit). Header-aware counts vs shipped TSVs (E:/SafeRS/x64/Release/transports/): fairy_rings 109 rows = 54 rejected + 55 stranded, 0 usable; spirit_trees 144 = 132 + 12, 0 usable; gnome_gliders 22 = 15 + 7, 0; hot_air_balloons 51 = 45 + 6, 0; magic_mushtrees 12 = 8 + 4, 0; quetzals 28 = 14 + 14, 0; wilderness_obelisks 60 = 54 + 6, 0; minecarts 47 = 21 + 12, 14 usable. Corrections to claim figures: exact parse-rejected total is 343 (claim said ~363); loaded-but-unreachable m_teleports total is 581 = 116 network dest-only rows + 465 origin-less teleport rows (items 275, minigames 21, seasonal 169) that are also never seeded (claim's ~560 is approximately right but conflates the network-stranding with the separate ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL executor gap; only the 47 teleportation_spells rows are ever seeded). Microbot side verified: addTransports buckets LOCATION_PERMUTATION(-1,-1,-1) rows (blank cell -> sentinel at Transport.java:232/240) into transportOrigins/transportDestinations and expands the cartesian product skipping pairs within radiusThreshold (~lines 555-585); merge constructor at :126-171 takes max skill levels/duration/wilderness, union of quests/items/varbits/varplayers, displayInfo from destination, action/objectId from origin; thresholds: gliders=6, spirit_trees=5, quetzals=6, balloons=7, mushtrees=5, fairy_rings default(0). The 2026-06-10 uncommitted changes touch only DaxWalker.cpp/PathExecutor.cpp/.h/Pathfinder.cpp (timeouts, watchdogs, bounds guard) plus GlobalCollisionMap deletion — nothing related to permutation expansion.

docs.title: [critical / completeness] completeness-teleport-item-minigame-seasonal-unsearched
docs.text:
PRIOR GAP 1 PARTIALLY STALE: considerTeleports is now TRUE, but TELEPORTATION_ITEM / MINIGAME / SEASONAL never enter the search graph — only spells are seeded

Ours: Prior-audit claim 'considerTeleports=false hardcoded' is STALE — it is set true at dllmain.cpp:1509 (verified live 2026-06-10) and TELEPORTATION_SPELL teleports are seeded at the start tile plus synthetic bank-rune edges. But teleport seeding filters t->type != TransportType::TELEPORTATION_SPELL -> continue (StaticPathfinder.cpp:250; comment :242-244 confirms ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL hard-excluded, re-verified on disk): 275 teleportation-item rows and 169 seasonal rows load into m_teleports but never enter any search; MINIGAME is additionally 0 rows due to a separate header-parse bug (tracked separately); origin-bearing expansion also skips teleport-typed rows (StaticPathfinder.cpp:382). Multi-destination ':' rows / Home Teleport exclusion and start-tile-only seeding are tracked as separate gaps.

Microbot: TransportType.isTeleport covers TELEPORTATION_ITEM/MINIGAME/SPELL plus origin-less SEASONAL (TransportType.java:52-67); all land under the null-origin key and are injected as usableTeleports at the search frontier (PathfinderConfig.java:74-78, 419-423, 250-276), with the wilderness-level state machine re-injecting newly-legal teleports at popped nodes as the search leaves wilderness bands (Pathfinder.java:368, 381-399, 496-513) — so walk-then-teleport routes are found. Item usability honours TeleportationItem mode NONE/INVENTORY/INVENTORY_NON_CONSUMABLE, default INVENTORY (TeleportationItem.java:8-12; PathfinderConfig.java:1054-1061), and the executor fires via handleTeleportItem incl. wearable/inventory/dialogue/scroll-book flows (Rs2Walker.java:6546-6699, 7572-7592).

Why it matters: Teleport tabs, jewellery (games necklace, dueling ring, glory), scrolls, and minigame group-teleports are the dominant fast-travel class for real accounts — the bread-and-butter of fast travel. Excluding them forces long walking routes Microbot would teleport past — minutes of extra travel per affected path, multiplied across thousands of daily paths — and produces a walking-heavy behavioural profile that looks nothing like the human population using the same items.

Verification (high confidence): Claim accurate as written; one strengthening correction: the non-spell exclusion is TRIPLE-gated, not just the seeding filter. (1) StaticPathfinder.cpp:250 seeds only TELEPORTATION_SPELL at the start tile (comment :242-244 explicitly defers ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL "until their executor branches land"); (2) refreshUsableTeleports (dllmain.cpp:624) also filters t->type != TELEPORTATION_SPELL, so the usable-teleport set consulted by isTeleportUsable can never contain non-spell types even if seeding were widened; (3) PathExecutor.cpp:587/614 only handles TELEPORTATION_SPELL edges — no ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL fire branch exists. Origin-bearing expansion (StaticPathfinder.cpp:382) skips all isTeleport types (TransportType.h:43-48 includes ITEM/MINIGAME/SPELL/SEASONAL), and bank-rune synthetic edges are spell-only (dllmain.cpp:623-666; StaticPathfinder.cpp:442). Rows DO load into m_teleports (TransportRegistry.cpp:33/35/38/175). Minor count nit: teleportation_items.tsv has 293 lines on disk (~292 data rows) vs the claimed 275 loaded — plausible after row-level filtering, exact runtime count not re-verified; seasonal_transports.tsv = 169 matches exactly. considerTeleports=true at dllmain.cpp:1509 confirmed — flag portion of the prior gap is fixed.

Citations: ours-search: §5B — StaticPathfinder.cpp:236-282, 248-250 (comment :242-244 — ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL hard-excluded), :382 (expansion skips teleport types); dllmain.cpp:1509 (considerTeleports=true — prior gap 1 flag portion fixed); PathfinderConfig.h:63 | ours-transports: §6 (275 ITEM + 169 SEASONAL rows loaded but never seeded) | mb-search: Pathfinder.java:368, 381-399, 496-513; PathfinderConfig.java:74-78, 250-276, 419-423 | mb-transports: TransportType.java:52-67; PathfinderConfig.java:1054-1061; TeleportationItem.java:8-12 | mb-executor: handleTeleportItem Rs2Walker.java:6546-6699, 7572-7592 | prior-audit gap 1: flag portion STALE (fixed), type-exclusion portion CONFIRMED

docs.title: [critical / completeness] completeness-executor-handler-coverage
docs.text:
PRIOR GAP 3 NARROWED BUT PRESENT: executor fires only object-interact (OPLOC1) + teleport-spell callback vs Microbot's ~15 type-specific handlers

Ours: PathExecutor's only fire verbs are Interact::perform(action, ObjectTarget) (PathExecutor.cpp:687) and the injected teleport-spell callback (cpp:588/615) — the prior 'ONE verb' claim is stale: spell support now exists, including the walk-to-bank→withdraw→cast bank-rune sequence (cpp:587-628) and same-tick multi-step chain advance (cpp:483-517). Still absent: teleport items, NPC dialogue transports (ships, boats, charters, gliders, spirit trees, magic carpets), widget transports (fairy-ring interface, charter map, quetzal map, minigame grouping tab), and canoe state machines. Any graph edge that parses but needs a dialogue/widget continuation after the object click fires the click then burns the 6s TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT and recalcs (cpp:541-552); non-parsing action rows are dropped from the graph entirely (StaticPathfinder.cpp:396-399 — graph-side half tracked separately), avoiding timeout dead time at the cost of coverage. Dax paths are transport-blind (cpp:420-424).

Microbot: handleTransports (Rs2Walker.java:5552-5995) dispatches per type: SHIP/NPC/BOAT named dialogue chains (:5657-5719), CHARTER_SHIP widget 885.4 (:7606-7640), POH (:6004-6009), CANOE full chop/shape/float/paddle state machine (:7243-7351), SPIRIT_TREE adventure log (:7107-7158), QUETZAL coordinate-table map (:7546-7570, :7380-7402), MAGIC_CARPET (:7594-7604), WILDERNESS_OBELISK (:6498-6513), GNOME_GLIDER widget 138 (:7666-7728), FAIRY_RING staff-equip + dial rotation (:7743-7819), MINIGAME grouping-tab chain (:7160-7241), TELEPORTATION_ITEM (wearable + inventory + dialogue + scroll book), TELEPORTATION_SPELL, SEASONAL plugin chain, plus generic objects with closed-variant 'Open' resolution (:5893-5957) and ~15 hardcoded exceptions (:6320-6496); displayInfo doubles as the runtime interaction script (mb-transports §6).

Why it matters: Even if the graph gaps were fixed, SafeRS cannot physically traverse most non-object transport classes — every category Microbot's handler table covers is a route class our walker either cannot use (longer travel) or half-fires into a 6s timeout + recalc loop with the search re-selecting the same unfireable edge. As requirement checks and permutation expansion get fixed, more of these edges enter the graph and the timeout class grows unless verbs land with them.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate against the current (uncommitted 2026-06-10) code; every cited line checks out. PathExecutor has exactly two fire verbs: (1) object-interact via m_interact.perform(edge.action, t) at PathExecutor.cpp:687, and (2) the injected teleport-spell callback m_fireTeleportSpellFn at :588 (origin-less) and :615 (bank-teleport), wired in dllmain.cpp:1451-1503 including the bank-open/withdraw-runes/close/cast sequence. PathExecutor.h:147-149 confirms the spell callback is the ONLY injected handler — no item/NPC/widget/fairy-ring/canoe callbacks exist anywhere (grep of Pathfinding/ and PluginAPI/ finds zero handlers for TELEPORTATION_ITEM, FAIRY_RING, NPC, BOAT, SHIP, CANOE, CHARTER_SHIP, QUETZAL, GNOME_GLIDER, SPIRIT_TREE, MAGIC_CARPET, WILDERNESS_OBELISK, MINIGAME). One sharpening the claim understates: for non-object edge types that do parse into the graph (isAllowed at PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57 filters only members+varbit, NOT type; origin-bearing expansion at StaticPathfinder.cpp:380-399 admits NPC/SHIP/FAIRY_RING rows whose action column parses as action;name;objectId), the executor unconditionally builds TargetKind::Object (PathExecutor.cpp:672-681) — so an NPC-dialogue transport row fires an OPLOC1 packet against an NPC id, which is not just a half-fire but likely an invalid/silently-rejected packet, then burns TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS=6000 (PathExecutor.h:182) and recalcs (cpp:541-552). Spell-only graph seeding confirmed at StaticPathfinder.cpp:242-250 ('Only TELEPORTATION_SPELL is seeded today — that's the only teleport type the executor can fire. ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL stay out until their executor branches land'); parse-or-drop at :396-399; chain advance at cpp:488-517; Dax transport-blindness at cpp:419-424. Microbot side verified: handleTransports at Rs2Walker.java:5552 dispatching handleTeleportItem:6546, handleSpiritTree:7107, handleMinigameTeleport:7160, handleCanoe:7243, handleQuetzal:7546, handleMagicCarpet:7594, handleCharterShip:7606, handleGlider:7666, handleFairyRing:7743 — all within a few lines of the claimed citations.

Citations: ours-executor: §3, §6 — PathExecutor.cpp:687, 588/615, 587-628, 672-687, 541-552, 483-517 (chain advance — improvement since prior audit), 420-424 (Dax paths transport-blind) | ours-search: StaticPathfinder.cpp:396-399 (parse-or-drop) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:5552-5995, 6320-6496, 7107-7861 | mb-transports: §6 (displayInfo as execution driver — fairy ring codes :7804-7806, dialogue clickOption :5670-5684) | memory: project_transport_gap_vs_microbot | prior-audit gap 3: CONFIRMED (partially narrowed by spell support)

docs.title: [high / speed] speed-no-failed-edge-memory
docs.text:
No failed-transport memory: failed edges are skipped once, then re-picked by every subsequent recalc

Ours: Interact::perform failure skips the edge immediately and keeps walking (PathExecutor.cpp:690-697), but nothing records the failure — no per-edge retry counter, no session blacklist, no dynamic blocked-edge insertion. The next recalc regenerates the same plan with the same edge. There is also no telemetry counting stall/off-path/unreachable recalcs to detect this in production.

Microbot: sessionBlacklistedDoors for quest-locked obstacles with restriction refresh (Rs2Walker.java:3709-3719), wrong-traversal blacklisting (:4284-4309), dynamic blockedTransportEdgesPacked for unusable shortcuts (PathfinderConfig.java:509-514), partial-path retry cap of 3 then UNREACHABLE (:1955-1970), and Telemetry counters (offPathRecalcCount/stallRecalcCount/unreachableCount, :715-821) for regression benchmarking.

Why it matters: Without failure memory, a single bad edge converts into an unbounded retry loop terminated only by the 48s give-up. With thousands of paths daily, the absence of telemetry also means these loops are invisible until a user reports a stuck bot.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed on current (uncommitted, 2026-06-10) code, with two refinements. (1) The cited skip-without-memory block is real: PathExecutor.cpp:687-697 — Interact::perform failure logs and does ++m_nextTransportIdx only. Nothing records the failure: recalculatePath (PathExecutor.cpp:214-270) re-runs the same pathfinder with the same goal and same m_useTransports, and every path result wholesale replaces m_transportEdges and resets m_nextTransportIdx=0 (lines 151-152, 252-253, 359-360), so the skip does not survive a recalc. StaticPathfinder::findPath (StaticPathfinder.h:48-53) accepts only an all-or-nothing useTransports bool — no blocked-edge parameter exists in the planner, and PathfinderConfig.h has only static usability filters (varbits/members/usable-teleports) with no dynamic failed-edge set. (2) Nuance: teleport-SPELL edges do have a per-edge retry counter (m_spellFireAttempts, MAX_SPELL_FIRE_ATTEMPTS=20, PathExecutor.h:154-159; used at .cpp:595-599, 622-626), but it only bounds fire-dispatch attempts within one path and is wiped by recalc — it is not failure memory; object transports have nothing at all. (3) The claim understates the worst case: for a transport that fires successfully but never completes (e.g. quest-locked door — exactly Microbot's sessionBlacklistedDoors case), the loop is UNBOUNDED, not 48s-bounded. The timeout branch (PathExecutor.cpp:518-552) refreshes m_lastMovedTime on every 6s timeout (line 532) and recalcs; the transport gate (lines 463-700) returns before the stall watchdog (lines ~800-944) ever runs while at-origin/awaiting, so m_consecutiveStalls never accumulates and the 6s-timeout→recalc→re-fire cycle repeats forever. The ~48s give-up (MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_GIVE_UP=4 × STALL_THRESHOLD_MS=12000, PathExecutor.h:252,397) only terminates the perform()-fails-immediately variant where the player keeps walking and stalls at the obstacle. (4) Telemetry: PathPerf.h is timing-only (ScopedTimer feeding srs::prof + [Perf] prints); the recently added Core/Profiler is also duration-based. No counters exist anywhere for off-path/stall/unreachable recalc causes — only TPRINTF console lines. Microbot citations all verified: sessionBlacklistedDoors quest-lock blacklist + config refresh + recalc (Rs2Walker.java:3705-3726, declared :3291, consulted :3520-3521, :3764), shouldBlacklistDoorAfterWrongTraversal (:4284-4309), partialRetriesWorking cap of 3 then Telemetry.recordUnreachable + UNREACHABLE (:1955-1970), Telemetry class with offPathRecalcCount/stallRecalcCount/partialRetryCount/unreachableCount (:715-821), and PathfinderConfig.addBlockedTransportEdgeIfNeeded/blocksWalkingEdgeWhenUnavailable for agility/grapple shortcuts (PathfinderConfig.java:509-514, 598-604).

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor.cpp:690-697 ('No per-edge retry counter for object transports — retry pressure comes only from the stall machinery') | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:3709-3719, 4284-4309, 1955-1970, 715-821 | mb-transports: PathfinderConfig.java:509-514, 598-604

docs.title: [high / speed] speed-blocked-goal-burns-full-budget
docs.text:
Blocked/unreachable goals: no upfront walkability check or nearest-reachable fallback — full 5s budget burned, then unbounded partial-path retries with no UNREACHABLE terminal

Ours: Local A* hard-aborts on a blocked goal tile with no nearest-reachable fallback (Pathfinder.cpp:37), falling through to static (PathExecutor.cpp:160-163). StaticPathfinder has NO upfront blocked-goal check: a goal on an unwalkable tile (the standard 'walk to object tile' call) burns the entire 5000ms no-progress budget (StaticPathfinder.h:51 — vs Microbot's 3000ms default) on the worker while the executor sits in WAITING_FOR_PATH, then returns a best-effort partial via the chebyshev+manhattan best-node metric (StaticPathfinder.cpp:284-308, 339-346, 470-484). The executor walks any >=2-node path even with found=false, with no partial flag plumbed through (PathExecutor.cpp:350-369); at path-end >4 from goal it recalcs with no retry bound (cpp:753-758), so a permanently blocked goal cycles recalc->stall->sidestep->IDLE over ~48s+ (cpp:926-931) with no UNREACHABLE state distinguishable from a generic failure.

Microbot: Same progress-reset cutoff design but defaults to 5 ticks = 3000ms (ShortestPathConfig.java:494-504); the walker short-circuits immediately for unwalkable-but-near targets before any search (Rs2Walker.java:996-1000); every popped node is scored against every target so the search ALWAYS yields a path to the closest reached tile (Pathfinder.java:145-162, 410-429); multi-target support lets callers pass tile sets instead of a single possibly-blocked tile (:101-105). The walker detects partial paths explicitly (Rs2Walker.java:1139-1150), recalculates with a 3500ms cooldown (:1156-1184), and caps partial retries at 3 before returning the explicit UNREACHABLE terminal state (:1955-1970).

Why it matters: Object-adjacent walking is the most common walk pattern in scripts, and destinations on occupied/blocked tiles (object stand tiles, busy spots) are routine. Each one is up to 5 seconds of guaranteed idle discovering the goal is blocked, then up to ~48s of recalc/stall churn ending in an ambiguous IDLE; Microbot caps discovery at 3s (and usually avoids it entirely), converges in 3 bounded retries, and tells the caller why. At production path volume this is hours of daily dead time plus a missing unreachable signal scripts need to choose an alternative tile.

Verification (high confidence): Core gap is real in current code: no upfront blocked-goal check (Pathfinder.cpp:37-40 hard-aborts found=false; StaticPathfinder.cpp findPath has no goal-walkability test), static search burns its full 5000ms no-progress budget (StaticPathfinder.h:51, hardcoded 5000 at PathExecutor.cpp:293; deadline-reset at StaticPathfinder.cpp:339-346) vs Microbot's 3000ms default (ShortestPathConfig.java:501-504), best-node partial returned with found=false (cpp:284-286, 470-486, 577), executor walks any >=2-node path discarding result.found (PathExecutor.cpp:350-369, found used only in a log string), path-end>4 recalc has no retry counter (cpp:753-758), and there is no UNREACHABLE terminal — give-up is plain IDLE (cpp:926-931; State enum h:112; scripts see only isMoving/hasArrived, cpp:1359-1365, Walk.cpp:240-250). CORRECTION: the "~48s+ unbounded churn" end-game is the worst case, not the typical one. (a) The common object-stand-tile case (closest reachable tile within TIGHT_PATH_GOAL_GAP=4 of goal) ends ARRIVED gracefully via tightFinishThreshold + one-shot pin-goal click (PathExecutor.cpp:716-722, 760-795) after a single ~5s discovery burn. (b) When path-end is >4 from goal, the uncapped recalc loop typically self-terminates after a SECOND ~5s static search: searching from the already-best reachable tile yields a 1-node path, which fails the >=2 check and drops to IDLE (cpp:350-355) — so ~10-11s total, bounded emergently but not by any enforced cap. (c) The full 4x12s stall->sidestep->IDLE chain (MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_GIVE_UP=4, STALL_THRESHOLD_MS=12000, h:252,396-397) applies only when the partial path is also untraversable live. All Microbot citations verified: short-circuit ARRIVED for unwalkable-but-near (Rs2Walker.java:995-1000), per-node multi-target scoring with cutoff reset (Pathfinder.java:95-105, 401-419), partial detection + 3500ms recalc cooldown (Rs2Walker.java:1139-1184, :132), 3-retry cap -> WalkerState.UNREACHABLE (:1955-1970).

Citations: ours-search: StaticPathfinder.cpp:284-308, 339-346, 470-484 (no upfront check, progress deadline, best-node partial); StaticPathfinder.h:51 (5000ms); Pathfinder.cpp:37 (local layer hard-abort); §10a | ours-executor: PathExecutor.cpp:160-163, 350-369, 753-758, 926-931 | mb-search: ShortestPathConfig.java:494-504; Pathfinder.java:101-105, 145-162, 410-429, 417 (progress resets cutoff) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:996-1000, 1139-1150, 1156-1184, 1955-1970

docs.title: [high / speed] speed-reachability-full-astar-per-call
docs.text:
isTileReachable runs a full local A* per call — up to 10-25 full searches in one tick on the raw-fallback path

Ours: PathExecutor::isTileReachable (PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639) runs a complete local A per query. Each call memsets ~60KB of stack arrays and loop-fills 12,100 gCost entries (Pathfinder.cpp:63-72); unreachable targets burn the full MAX_ITERATIONS=10000 cap. Call sites per tick: short-walk gate (:131), goal check (:763), waypoint gate (:1070), wall-adjust (:1684), and findFurthestReachableRawPathPoint loops it per raw tile within MAX_REACH=13 (:1708-1713) — 10-25 full A runs in a single tick, on the tick thread.

Microbot: One BFS flood (getReachableTilesFromTile / Rs2Tile reachability) computed once and reused for all candidate ranking — closest-tile-index selection, isNearPath, sidestep ranking all consume the same flood (Rs2Walker.java:5373-5408, 6771-6798, 3320-3325).

Why it matters: This is pure redundant computation in the hot per-tick loop, worst exactly when the bot is already struggling (raw-fallback near obstacles), adding CPU latency at the moment responsiveness matters most. SafeRS even has the capped-BFS pattern in findClosestPathIndex (cpp:1405-1444) but does not reuse it for reachability.

Verification (high confidence): Core deficiency confirmed in current code: PathExecutor::isTileReachable (PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639) runs a full local A per query with zero caching; each Pathfinder::findPath call memsets ~60.5KB of stack arrays (parent+closed) and loop-fills 12,100 gCost entries (Pathfinder.cpp:63-72, SCENE_SIZE=110, MAX_ITERATIONS=10000 at Pathfinder.h:62); unreachable targets exhaust the player's entire reachable component per query. findFurthestReachableRawPathPoint (PathExecutor.cpp:1708-1713) calls it per raw tile within MAX_REACH=13 using continue (not break) on unreachable tiles, so every in-radius raw tile behind a blocked door pays a full failed search. The capped-BFS primitive already exists at findClosestPathIndex (PathExecutor.cpp:1405-1444) but is not reused for reachability. Framing corrections: (1) the :131 call is in walkTo(), once per walk request, not per-tick; (2) steady-state ticks skip target selection via the sticky interim (evalInterim early-return, PathExecutor.cpp:1003), so the multi-A burst fires only on selection ticks — but in the claimed stuck scenario (smoothed waypoint unreachable, raw fallback also fails → haveTarget=false, no interim set) selection re-runs nearly every tick until the stall watchdog recomputes; (3) realistic worst case is ~15-17 full A runs per selection tick (1 at :1070 + ~13-15 in raw loop + 1 at :1684), within the claimed 10-25 range only if the raw path meanders; (4) the cost lands on the RENDER thread, not just the tick thread — renderFrame (dllmain.cpp:686, PresentHook callback registered at :1754) calls onGameTick at dllmain.cpp:742, so the burst manifests as a frame hitch; (5) Microbot recomputes its flood per call site rather than literally reusing one flood for everything, but each operation is a single bounded BFS (Rs2Walker.java:5373-5408, 6771-6798, 3320-3325) vs SafeRS's N full-scene A — the contrast stands.

Citations: ours-collision: finding 2 — PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639, 131, 763, 1070, 1684, 1708-1713; Pathfinder.cpp:63-72; Pathfinder.h:62; PathExecutor.cpp:1405-1444 | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:5373-5408, 6771-6798, 3320-3325

docs.title: [high / accuracy] accuracy-blocked-edges-restrictions-unbound
docs.text:
PRIOR GAP 6 CONFIRMED: blocked_edges.tsv (13 rows) and restrictions.tsv (218 rows) shipped but have zero consumers; no dynamic blocked-edge derivation either

Ours: Both files ship in x64/Release/transports/ (blocked_edges.tsv 13 rows, restrictions.tsv 218 rows) and are fetched by tools/fetch_transport_tsvs.py:29-40, but FILE_BINDINGS binds 22 other files only (TransportRegistry.cpp:17-42) and grep over OSRSClient .cpp/.h finds zero consumers (re-verified 2026-06-10). There is also no dynamic equivalent: an agility shortcut that fails availability cannot block the walking gap it spans (requirements are never evaluated at all), so A* can walk 'through' shortcut gaps and route across tiles and edges Microbot hard-forbids.

Microbot: blocked_edges.tsv loads into packed origin<<32^dest keys with Bidirectional support, re-seeded each refresh (PathfinderConfig.java:530-596); unusable AGILITY_SHORTCUT/GRAPPLE_SHORTCUT rows dynamically add their origin->dest as blocked walking edges incl. diagonal corner decomposition (:509-514, 483-507, 598-604); restrictions.tsv marks tiles hard no-go unless ALL members/quests/varbits/varplayers/skills/items requirements are met (Restriction.java; refreshRestrictionData :670-715). All three are consumed in forward expansion (CollisionMap.java:238-240), reverse expansion (:329-335), and PathSmoother LOS (PathSmoother.java:107), plus ignoreCollision whitelist and live ToA special-casing (CollisionMap.java:143-176).

Why it matters: These files encode hand-curated 'walkable in the collision data but you must not path here' knowledge — quest-gated areas, one-way drops, shortcut gaps, tiles that strand the walker. Without them our search and smoother produce confidently wrong paths through forbidden tiles that strand the player at click time, surfacing as unexplainable 12-48s stall cycles no executor recovery can fix — and with requirements also unevaluated there is no compensating mechanism whatsoever.

Verification (high confidence): Core gap confirmed as of 2026-06-10 disk state: blocked_edges.tsv (13 data rows) and restrictions.tsv (218 data rows) ship in E:/SafeRS/x64/Release/transports/ and are fetched by E:/SafeRS/tools/fetch_transport_tsvs.py (FILES list :30-55), but FILE_BINDINGS in E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/Pathfinding/TransportRegistry.cpp:17-42 binds exactly 22 other TSVs and a full sweep (incl. gitignored paths) finds zero C++ consumers of either file or any Restriction/BlockedEdge concept. No dynamic blocked-edge derivation exists: walking expansion (StaticPathfinder.cpp:123-153 fillTraversable) consults only StaticCollisionMap, and transport expansion (StaticPathfinder.cpp:380-399) drops a disallowed/unfireable transport edge without blocking the walking step it spans — there is no equivalent of Microbot's addBlockedTransportEdgeIfNeeded (PathfinderConfig.java:509-514, called from the refresh rejection path :410-412). PathSmoother.cpp likewise has no restriction/blocked-edge check. ONE OVERSTATEMENT to correct: 'requirements are never evaluated at all' is too broad. PathfinderConfig::isAllowed (OSRSClient/Pathfinding/PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57) DOES evaluate isMembers (live world byte) and varbit gates (live VarpSystem, fail-permissive on cold cache), and teleport-spell usability (magic level + runes, incl. bank runes) is precomputed per tick into usableTeleports (dllmain.cpp:630). What is never evaluated: skills, quests, items, varplayers, maxWildernessLevel — stored raw on Transport (Transport.cpp:101-111) and documented STUBBED (PathfinderConfig.h:11-16). So for AGILITY_SHORTCUT specifically the Agility-level requirement is indeed never checked, and even when a transport IS rejected (members/varbit), nothing blocks the underlying walking edge — both halves of the Microbot mechanism (restriction tiles, blocked edges static+dynamic) are absent.

Citations: ours-transports: §1 — tools/fetch_transport_tsvs.py:29-40; FILE_BINDINGS TransportRegistry.cpp:17-42; grep 0 consumers (re-verified 2026-06-10) | mb-transports: PathfinderConfig.java:530-596, 509-514, 483-507, 598-604, 670-715; CollisionMap.java:238-240, 329-335, 143-176; PathSmoother.java:107 | prior-audit gap 6: CONFIRMED

docs.title: [high / completeness] completeness-var-operator-coverage
docs.text:
PRIOR GAP 5 CONFIRMED: varbit '=' only — '>' '<' '&' '@cooldown' operators skipped fail-permissive and varplayers never evaluated

Ours: Varbit checks support only the '=' operator; '>'/'<' forms are skipped fail-permissive (PathfinderConfig.cpp:77-81), malformed pairs skipped (:89-92), '&' BIT_SET and '@' COOLDOWN_MINUTES are unimplemented, and varplayersRaw has no reader at all (Transport.h:57-62; PathfinderConfig.h:15). Cold varbits are also fail-permissive by design. Distinct from the requirement-stub gap: the varbit reader EXISTS but its grammar is incomplete.

Microbot: Five operators on BOTH varbits and varplayers: EQUAL, GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, BIT_SET ((actual & value) > 0), COOLDOWN_MINUTES (epoch-minute delta — implements the shared 20-min minigame teleport cooldown), parsed at Transport.java:341-415 (TransportVarbit.java:18-33, identical TransportVarPlayer.java:18-33); varplayers read live on the client thread (PathfinderConfig.java:792-796, 825-834; ShortestPathConfig.java:298-308).

Why it matters: TSV rows using >, <, &, or @ silently pass, admitting state-gated transports (levers, portals, diary-gated shortcuts, cooldown teleports) the account can't currently use — feeding the same click-fail -> 6s timeout -> recalc loop as the stubbed requirement columns; cooldown-gated minigame teleports would be re-attempted while on cooldown even after the seeding gap is fixed. Impact grows as more transport classes become fireable.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate as stated against current code. SafeRS: PathfinderConfig::checkVarbitString (E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/Pathfinding/PathfinderConfig.cpp:59-112) parses only "id=value" pairs — tokens without '=' (i.e. '>', '<', '&', '@' forms) hit the eq == npos branch at :76-81 and are skipped fail-permissive, with a comment explicitly acknowledging Skretzo's >/< operators; unparseable ids/values skipped at :88-92; cold (nullopt) varbit reads pass at :94-106 by documented design. Transport.h:54-62 stores varplayersRaw verbatim ("id=value" or "id@value") and grep confirms its ONLY consumer is the TSV writer (Transport.cpp:105) — no evaluation anywhere in OSRSClient. PathfinderConfig.h:15 still lists "Varplayer requirements — format quirks (@ operator), defer" as STUBBED. Microbot: Transport.java:341-416 parses 5 operators (> < = & @) on both Varbits and Varplayers columns; TransportVarbit.java:18-33 and TransportVarPlayer.java:18-33 implement EQUAL/GREATER_THAN/LESS_THAN/BIT_SET((actual&value)>0)/COOLDOWN_MINUTES(epoch-minute delta); pathfinder/PathfinderConfig.java enforces both at :825-834 via varbitChecks (:782-784) and varplayerChecks (:786-790), with live client-thread varplayer reads in getLiveVarplayerValue (:792-796) and pre-warm reads at :370-375. Only citation nit: "ShortestPathConfig.java:298-308" is misattributed — that content (refreshTransports gating, ~:303-312) lives in pathfinder/PathfinderConfig.java; ShortestPathConfig.java is the RuneLite config interface. Does not affect the verdict.

docs.title: [high / accuracy] accuracy-no-cross-plane-goal
docs.text:
Walk API cannot express a goal on another plane — goal plane silently forced to the player's current plane, arriving on the wrong floor and reporting success

Ours: Walk::to takes (x,y) only and the header explicitly documents 'Plane is read from the player's current plane — there's no cross-plane pathing in the executor surface' (Walk.h:24-26, verified in working tree; Walk.cpp:82-83). StaticPathfinder is documented 'Single-plane only... plane mismatch -> empty result' (StaticPathfinder.h:5-6); the Chebyshev heuristic ignores plane entirely (StaticPathfinder.cpp:103-109) and walking expansion never changes z (:359) — plane changes happen only as transport-edge side effects mid-path. A script targeting e.g. the plane-2 Lumbridge bank gets a search for the same (x,y) on the player's plane, arrives at the wrong floor, and hasArrived() reports success; 'walk to the first floor of this building' is inexpressible.

Microbot: Targets are full packed WorldPoints including 2 plane bits (WorldPointUtil.java:29-31); exact-hit termination requires the packed match incl. plane (Pathfinder.java:401-423); cross-plane distance returns Integer.MAX_VALUE so heuristics/costs never conflate floors (WorldPointUtil.java:86-93); plane transitions ride transport edges in the same graph, with a mod-6400 underground-Y heuristic fallback so underground targets don't misdirect surface expansion (Pathfinder.java:226-250).

Why it matters: Ending on the EXACT requested tile is impossible for any multi-floor destination — the walker arrives at the right (x,y) on the wrong z and declares ARRIVED, a systematic silent-wrong-arrival class. Upper-floor banks, quest rooms, and dungeon entrances are routine destinations for an account-builder, so every such script must hand-script the stairs/ladder leg where Microbot scripts pass a 3D point and walk away.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate against the 2026-06-10 working tree, with three refinements. (1) The entire pathed-walk surface is 2D: Walk::to(ctx,x,y) (E:\SafeRS\OSRSClient\PluginAPI\API\Walk.h:32-34, doc at :24-26 verbatim) -> PathExecutor::walkTo(goalX,goalY,...) (PathExecutor.h:83-84; PathExecutor.cpp:65-71 stores only m_finalGoalX/Y) and every Lua entry (game.moveTo/walkTo/minimapWalkTo, ScriptAPI.cpp:389-429) is (x,y[,useTransports]) — no plane anywhere. The goal plane is forced to the player's plane at dispatch (PathExecutor.cpp:147, :166, :262-263). (2) Worse than claimed: the DaxWalker fallback hardcodes goal plane to 0 — dax->findPath(sx,sy,sp,goalX,goalY,0) at PathExecutor.cpp:189, despite DaxWalker::findPath accepting endZ (DaxWalker.h:26-27). (3) Mechanism refinement: StaticPathfinder packs the goal with the START plane (StaticPathfinder.cpp:178-179) and termination requires exact packed match incl. plane bits (:329), so even though transport edges can change z mid-search (:380-424) the search can only 'find' the goal back on the player's original plane; the heuristic is plane-blind chebyshev (:101-109) and walking expansion keeps z (:359). Arrival is plane-blind too: chebyshev(px,py,m_finalGoalX,m_finalGoalY) at PathExecutor.cpp:716-722 fires ARRIVED on any plane, and hasArrived()==state==ARRIVED (:1363-1365) — the silent wrong-floor success class is real. Only escape hatch: Walk::fastCanvas/walkSmart accept an optional plane (Walk.h:80-104), but fastCanvas is a single no-pathfinding click requiring the tile on-canvas, and walkSmart's off-canvas fallback DROPS the plane (Walk.cpp:199 calls to() with no plane). Microbot citations all check out (Pathfinder.java lives at shortestpath/pathfinder/, not shortestpath/): packed targets carry 2 plane bits (WorldPointUtil.java:29-31), cross-plane distance = Integer.MAX_VALUE (:86-93), exact packed-match termination (Pathfinder.java:401-423), mod-6400 underground heuristic (:224-250).

Citations: ours-transports: §8 — Walk.h:24-26; Walk.cpp:82-83 (goal plane = player plane) | ours-executor: §5 — StaticPathfinder.h:5-6 ('plane mismatch -> empty result') | ours-search: §1 — StaticPathfinder.cpp:103-109 (plane-blind heuristic), :359 (expansion never changes z) | mb-search: WorldPointUtil.java:29-31, 86-93; Pathfinder.java:226-250, 401-423

docs.title: [high / accuracy] accuracy-smoother-start-plane-bug
docs.text:
Path smoothing and anchor matching use the START plane for the whole path; post-transport segments validated against the wrong plane

Ours: StaticPathfinder passes a single plane argument (the start plane) to smoothing and anchor packing (StaticPathfinder.cpp:554, 568), and PathNode carries no plane (Pathfinder.h:10-12). After a plane-changing transport (stairs/ladder/manhole), post-transport tiles are LOS-checked against the start plane's collision data; same-xy stairs (dx,dy<=1 so the adjacency rejection does not protect) can be smoothed ACROSS the transport, and transport anchors on other planes pack with plane=start so isAnchor misses them (PathSmoother.cpp:39-43) — the anchor that exists precisely to stop the smoother collapsing the transport tile (PathSmoother.h:25-27) is defeated.

Microbot: Smoothing operates on packed positions that include plane bits, transport origins AND destinations on the path are non-collapsible anchors (Pathfinder.java:187-203), and the LOS test additionally consults blocked transport edges (PathSmoother.java:107). Segments are capped at Chebyshev 10 so isNearPath keeps intersecting (PathSmoother.java:40-84).

Why it matters: Smoothing/interpolation aiming errors on the far side of every stair or ladder: the smoothed path can cut through walls that only exist on the actual plane, and a collapsed transport-origin waypoint makes the executor click past the stairs instead of onto them. Multi-floor routes are extremely common, so this corrupts a large fraction of daily paths.

Verification (high confidence): Core claim verified against current (2026-06-10) code, with four precision corrections. (1) The A* search itself is plane-correct — nodes carry packed coords with plane bits and collision is queried at the unpacked z (StaticPathfinder.cpp:349-374); the plane is lost only at reconstruction, where PathNode{x,y} (Pathfinder.h:10-12) drops it (StaticPathfinder.cpp:476-484). Smoothing then runs once over the whole mixed-plane path with the START plane: anchors packed via pack(step.x, step.y, plane) at StaticPathfinder.cpp:554, smooth(reversed, m_map, plane, anchors) at :568, LOS canStep(x,y,plane,..) at PathSmoother.cpp:24/32, isAnchor pack at :39-43, and adjacent() at :16-18 is plane-blind (PathSmoother.h:15-16 comment "Plane changes are rejected by the adjacency check" is stale/false for cross-plane paths). (2) The anchor is NOT fully defeated: transport ORIGINS on the start plane (the common first transport) anchor correctly and are pushed verbatim (PathSmoother.cpp:65-69). Defeated cases are (a) origins of later transports on a different plane — the :554 registry lookup packs the wrong plane and misses unless a vertically-stacked same-xy transport coincidentally exists on the start plane — and (b) ALL destinations: SafeRS anchors only tiles with transportsAt() (origins), while Microbot anchors origins AND destinations (Pathfinder.java:192-201) and rejects cross-plane adjacency/LOS outright (PathSmoother.java:86-89, 96) plus blocked-edge checks (:107). So a same-xy stair's plane-1 destination can be smoothed into a plane-0-validated LOS segment even when the origin anchor holds. (3) Executor partially mitigates: pathClipIndex (PathExecutor.cpp:1809-1820) clips clicks at the pending transport origin but its dropped-anchor fallback is literally "no clip" (line 1819 comment "smoother dropped the anchor (shouldn't happen)") — codifying the invariant this bug violates; the per-tick fire gate (PathExecutor.cpp:609-610) fires whenever the player passes within Chebyshev-1 of the origin on the right plane, often rescuing collapsed origins; live isTileReachable + raw-path fallback (PathExecutor.cpp:1070-1084) gates clicks against live collision on the player's current plane, so wrong-plane smoothed waypoints usually degrade to raw-path clicking in-scene rather than wall-cutting clicks. (4) Scope narrower than "every stair or ladder": dungeon ladders/manholes go to plane-0 y+6400 underground (non-adjacent xy → adjacency check protects, and start-plane packing stays correct), and goalPacked is forced to the start plane (StaticPathfinder.cpp:178-179), so cross-plane exposure is limited to mid-path segments through other planes (multi-floor buildings, cross-plane teleport landings) — real but less than "a large fraction of daily paths". Net: genuine accuracy gap vs Microbot; practical severity closer to medium than high given the executor mitigations.

Citations: ours-search: StaticPathfinder.cpp:554, 568; Pathfinder.h:10-12; PathSmoother.cpp:39-43 | ours-collision: PathSmoother.cpp:23-37, 62-79 | mb-search: Pathfinder.java:187-203; PathSmoother.java:40-84, 107

docs.title: [high / accuracy] accuracy-silent-inexact-arrival
docs.text:
Arrival acceptance silently allows landings up to 5 tiles off the requested tile; pin-goal exact click is one-shot

Ours: Minimap-only mode accepts +/-2 by design (ARRIVAL_DIST=2, PathExecutor.h:239, cpp:716-717). Both watchdogs mercy-declare ARRIVED at <=CLOSE_ENOUGH=5 after 12-15s without progress (cpp:873-878, 908-913; h:243 verified). tightFinishThreshold loosens acceptance to 1-2 tiles when path-end is 1-4 from goal (cpp:1462-1471). The exact-tile mechanism, pin-goal, fires exactly ONE canvas click (m_finalClickFired, cpp:760-786); if that click fails to land, the next escalation is the 12s mercy path. None of these inexact outcomes are signalled — hasArrived() is just true (ours-transports: 'scripts can see hasArrived() with the player up to 5 tiles off').

Microbot: Same tightFinishThreshold concept (Rs2Walker.java:425-441), but the end-of-path sequence is richer: final canvas click + pinGoal exact-goal click when reachable (:1926-1930) followed by a two-phase idle wait with a 4s refinement window (waitUntilIdleAfterSceneWalk, :465-503), and inexact ends are DETECTABLE — partialPath is computed explicitly (:1139-1150) and walkWithState returns distinct terminal states consumed by the script harness (ShortestPathScript.java:104-173).
