Microbot's finishDistance=5/randomizeFinalTile defaults also tolerate inexactness (ShortestPathConfig.java:448-461, 694-704), but as overridable configuration rather than a silent hardcoded override.

Why it matters: Scripts position for object/NPC interactions assuming the requested tile. A silent 2-5 tile miss breaks the downstream action (wrong side of a booth, out of reach of an object), and because the walker reports success the failure is misattributed to the interaction layer — the worst kind of accuracy bug to debug at fleet scale.

Verification (high confidence): All cited SafeRS thresholds and behaviors verified in current code: ARRIVAL_DIST=2 (PathExecutor.h:239), CLOSE_ENOUGH=5 (h:243), minimap base ±2 / canvas base exact (cpp:716-718), tightFinishThreshold 1-2 tile loosening (cpp:1462-1471), watchdog mercy-ARRIVED at <=5 after 12s/15s (cpp:873-878, 908-913; STALL_THRESHOLD_MS=12000 h:252, PROGRESS_STALL_MS=15000 h:293), and hasArrived()==(m_state==ARRIVED) with no exactness signal (cpp:1363-1365; Walk.h:106-116; Walk.cpp:246-250). Two detail corrections: (1) the pin-goal click is one-shot PER COMPUTED PATH, not per walk — recalculatePath() resets m_finalClickFired (cpp:234-238) granting one new attempt per recalc; (2) a failed pin click does NOT escalate to the 12s mercy path — if the player remains at path-end, case (3) at cpp:788-795 declares ARRIVED immediately on the NEXT game tick, 1-4 tiles off, silently. The 12-15s mercy paths only apply when the player is off path-end. So the silent-inexact-arrival gap is real and in the pin-failure case faster/more silent than claimed. Also: repeated-stall give-up silently sets state to IDLE (cpp:926-930), indistinguishable from cancel via the Walk facade — there is no UNREACHABLE/partial-path surface anywhere in OSRSClient (grep confirmed, including the 2026-06-10 uncommitted changes).

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor.h:239, 243; PathExecutor.cpp:716-722, 760-786, 873-878, 908-913, 1462-1471 | ours-transports: Walk API §8 (hasArrived up to 5 off) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:425-441, 465-503, 1926-1954, 1139-1150 | mb-transports: ShortestPathConfig.java:448-461, 694-704; ShortestPathScript.java:104-173

docs.title: [high / completeness] completeness-wilderness-model-absent
docs.text:
No wilderness model: maxWildernessLevel stored but never read, no avoidWilderness, no level-gated teleport injection

Ours: Transport.maxWildernessLevel is parsed and stored (Transport.h:52) but has no reader (ours-search §6); PathfinderConfig.h:16 confirms 'no live wilderness-level tracker' (re-verified on disk). There is no avoidWilderness edge/target filtering and no wilderness-level state machine in the search — teleports are treated as usable anywhere, and routes into/through wilderness are indistinguishable from safe routes.

Microbot: Search-loop wilderness state machine: wildernessLevel starts at 31 and lowers as popped nodes exit level-30/20/wilderness areas, calling refreshTeleports(node, level) to inject newly-legal teleports at the frontier tile, gated by level <= transport.getMaxWildernessLevel() (Pathfinder.java:368, 381-399, 496-513; PathfinderConfig.java:250-276). avoidWilderness blocks non-wildy->wildy steps unless the target is in wildy (PathfinderConfig.java:763-766) and filterLocations strips wilderness targets with restore fallback (:278-296).

Why it matters: Two production failure classes: (1) the graph schedules teleports above level 20/30 wilderness where the game blocks them -> guaranteed click-time failure with no alternative route found, and the legitimate walk-to-safety-then-teleport escape is unfindable; (2) no guard against routing a bot through PKer territory — in a botting context wilderness deaths mean lost gear and a behavioural red flag. Microbot treats both as first-class search constraints.

Verification (high confidence): Claim fully accurate against current disk (incl. uncommitted 2026-06-10 changes). One precision: SafeRS's exposure is narrower than "teleports anywhere" — StaticPathfinder.cpp:235-282 seeds TELEPORTATION_SPELL edges only at the start tile (plus bank-origin edges, PathfinderConfig.h:87-94), never mid-path. So the failure mode is: start tile inside wilderness => all usable spell teleports seeded with no level gate (guaranteed click-time failure above level 20/30, and the walk-out-then-teleport escape is structurally unfindable since teleports are never injected at later nodes); plus no avoidWilderness edge/target filtering anywhere, and no executor-side wilderness guard (zero wilderness references in PluginAPI/API; Microbot has one at Rs2Walker.java:6546-6550).

Citations: ours-search §6: Transport.h:52 stored never evaluated; PathfinderConfig.h:11-16 stub list | mb-search §1: Pathfinder.java:368, 381-399, 496-513; PathfinderConfig.java:250-276; maxWildernessLevel from TSV Transport.java:333-335 | mb-transports §4: avoidWilderness PathfinderConfig.java:763-766, target filtering :278-296 | mb-executor §3: wilderness guard in handleTeleportItem Rs2Walker.java:6548

docs.title: [medium / speed] speed-recalc-storms-unbounded
docs.text:
Recalcs have no cooldown, no retry cap, and spawn one detached thread each

Ours: Recalc triggers (off-path, transport timeout, path-end gap, stalls) fire immediately with no minimum spacing between successive recalcs of the same walk; there is no partial-path retry cap — only the 4-consecutive-stall give-up bounds the loop. Each static recalc spawns a fresh detached std::thread (PathExecutor.cpp:290) — 'cheap but unbounded under recalc storms' (ours-search §10c). No telemetry counts recalc frequency.

Microbot: PARTIAL_TRANS_RECAL_COOLDOWN_MS=3500 between partial-path recalcs (Rs2Walker.java:131-132), max 3 partial retries then UNREACHABLE (:1955-1970), 64-iteration processWalk hard cap (:215, 1063), all searches on one dedicated single-thread executor (ShortestPathPlugin.java:326-328), recalc counts exported via Telemetry.

Why it matters: When the graph contains a bad edge (see stall-loop gaps) every retry costs a full 5s-budget search plus a thread spawn. Under pathological conditions (oscillating off-path near a closed door) recalc frequency is bounded only by the watchdog timers, wasting CPU and producing visible click thrash.

Verification (high confidence): Claim holds in current code with one wording refinement. PathExecutor::recalculatePath (PathExecutor.cpp:214) has no cooldown, no retry counter, and no telemetry; six call sites (empty-path :727, path-end gap :756, transport timeout :550, no-progress :894, stall :944, off-path :993). The only bound, MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_GIVE_UP=4 (PathExecutor.h:397), counts only consecutive position-stalls at the SAME tile — the partial-path loop (consumePendingStatic accepts partial results at :350-369, then path-end-gap recalc at :756) is uncapped and can cycle forever at ~one 5s-search period per iteration. Each static recalc spawns a fresh detached std::thread (PathExecutor.cpp:290-300; Dax at :187-195). Refinement vs claim text: watchdog-driven recalcs are NOT literally unspaced — each watchdog timer resets after firing (STALL_THRESHOLD_MS=12s xmultiplier, PROGRESS_STALL_MS=15s, OFF_PATH_TOLERANCE_MS=2s) and WAITING_FOR_PATH suppresses triggers while a search is in flight, so same-trigger spacing is implicit; only path-end-gap and transport-timeout recalcs fire instantly, and there is no cross-trigger cooldown or global cap. Also a mild mitigation exists: each new dispatch sets the prior request's cancelFlag (:222-224, :302-304) so stale worker threads exit early — threads are unbounded in spawn count but not in useful concurrent work. Microbot side verified as cited: PARTIAL_TRANS_RECAL_COOLDOWN_MS=3500 (Rs2Walker.java:131-132, used :1171), 3-partial-retry cap then UNREACHABLE (:1959-1970), MAX_PROCESS_WALK_TAIL_ITERATIONS=64 (:215), single-thread pathfindingExecutor (ShortestPathPlugin.java:184, 325-328), recalc telemetry counters (Rs2Walker.java:718, 781-786, 819).

Citations: ours-search: §10c — PathExecutor.cpp:290 (detached thread per request), §4 (no caching, recalc triggers list) | ours-executor: §2 (recalc triggers and cadence) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:131-132, 1955-1970, 215, 1063; ShortestPathPlugin.java:326-328

docs.title: [medium / speed] speed-no-partial-path-lookahead-handoff
docs.text:
No lookahead recalc on partial paths — player dead-stops at segment end waiting for the next search

Ours: Partial paths (found=false) are walked silently; the path-end-gap recalc fires only when the player has REACHED the path end >=4 tiles from goal (PathExecutor.cpp:753-758). For static recalcs the player then stands idle for the full search round-trip. (Transport completion is well handled — success skips recalc since the path already contains post-transport tiles.)

Microbot: Partial-segment lookahead: when within 12 tiles / 10 steps of the segment end and still far from goal, recalculates WHILE STILL MOVING with a 3500ms cooldown — explicitly 'smooth handoff vs dead stop at segment end' (Rs2Walker.java:1156-1184). Transport completion gets destination-aware repath from the known landing tile BEFORE arrival, plus a pre-primed expected-destination queue to skip repath entirely (:6150-6230).

Why it matters: Long-distance routes are chains of partial segments. Each dead stop costs the search latency (hundreds of ms to seconds) in pure idle, several times per long route; Microbot overlaps that latency with movement.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed against current (2026-06-10 uncommitted) code. Two precision fixes: (1) the path-end recalc fires when dLastToGoal > TIGHT_PATH_GOAL_GAP (=4) — strictly greater, so 5+ tiles, not >=4 (PathExecutor.cpp:753, PathExecutor.h:360) — and only once the player is within baseArrivalDist (0 canvas / 2 minimap ARRIVAL_DIST) of the path's last tile (cpp:749). (2) The dead-stop applies when the goal is out-of-scene (the normal partial case): recalculatePath() then dispatches the async StaticPathfinder and parks in WAITING_FOR_PATH (cpp:261-265, 309) where onGameTick() returns without clicking (cpp:444); if the goal happens to be in the loaded scene, local A* resolves synchronously same-tick with no idle (cpp:245-258), but partial segments imply a far goal so this rarely helps. Async results are consumed at frame rate (onFrame, cpp:1253) so only the search itself is idle time, not result polling. Everything else in the claim is accurate: partial results (found=false) are accepted with no partial flag stored (cpp:350-369, 'partial path arrived' log :366); no lookahead/prefetch mechanism exists anywhere in OSRSClient/Pathfinding/ or PluginAPI/API/Walk.cpp; transport success deliberately skips recalc (cpp:554-566). Microbot side verified verbatim: Rs2Walker.java:1156-1184 partial-segment lookahead (12 tiles / 10 steps, 3500ms cooldown at :132, comment 'smooth handoff vs dead stop at segment end'), and :6150-6230 transport handoff with pre-primed expectedTransportDestinations queue + destination-aware restartPathfinding(transportDest, goal).

Citations: ours-search: partial results accepted (PathExecutor.cpp:350-369); recalc trigger at :753 | ours-executor: §3 (success -> no recalc, cpp:554-566), §1 (path-end handling 748-796) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:1156-1184, 6150-6230

docs.title: [medium / speed] speed-per-tick-teleport-recompute
docs.text:
Teleport usability recomputed EVERY game tick on the render thread vs Microbot's memoized per-restart refresh

Ours: refreshUsableTeleports runs every game tick on the render thread regardless of whether any walk is active (dllmain.cpp:606-669): Spells-table resolution + Magic::canCast over all spell rows, plus bank-teleport edge synthesis for all 13 bank locations. No memoization or change-detection on inventory/varbits.

Microbot: refreshTransports runs once per pathfinder restart, and TransportRefreshSnapshot memoizes the entire filtered transport map keyed on a fingerprint of toggles + inventory/equipment/bank + target + members + leagues/PoH state, verified per-hit against live skills/varbits/quests (PathfinderConfig.java:317-335, 1416-1441); skill/varbit prewarm batched in ONE client-thread hop (365-377).

Why it matters: Steady render-thread cost on a game client every 600ms whether or not pathing, scaling with spell-table size. The flip side is genuinely fresh data at search time (no refresh latency at walk start), so this is a CPU/frame-time trade, not pure loss — but the recompute does redundant work ~99% of ticks.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed in current code with two precision fixes. (1) SafeRS: refreshUsableTeleports (E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/dllmain.cpp:614-669) is called from renderFrame inside the newGameTick block (dllmain.cpp:951-961), i.e. every ~600ms game tick on the render thread, with no gate on walk activity and no memoization/change-detection — setUsableTeleports/setBankTeleports unconditionally rebuild and swap under mutex every tick (E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/Pathfinding/PathfinderConfig.cpp:114-132). The only gate is considerTeleports, set true unconditionally at init (dllmain.cpp:1509-1510). Precision fix A: the per-tick loop is over the ~146 TELEPORTATION_SPELL transport rows (x64/Release/transports/teleportation_spells.tsv), each doing a linear substring scan of the 33-entry Spells table via Spells::idByName (Spells.cpp:117-126, ~4.8K name comparisons/tick); Magic::canCast (inventory+pouch+bank memory reads per rune, Magic.cpp:24-51) runs only for the ~7 transports that resolve to table spells — not 'over all spell rows'. Precision fix B: the 13-bank-location edge synthesis (dllmain.cpp:656-665) fires only per spell whose runes are bank-covered but not live-castable, and only when BankCache is populated (gates at dllmain.cpp:618, 643) — it is skipped entirely before any bank snapshot exists. (2) Microbot: exactly as claimed — refresh(target)→refreshTransports runs per pathfinder restart (ShortestPathPlugin.java:337/558 → PathfinderConfig.java:191-244), TransportRefreshSnapshot memoizes the filtered map keyed on toggles+inventory/equipment/bank fingerprint+target+members+leagues/PoH (PathfinderConfig.java:315-335, 1416-1441, 1502-1519), verified per-hit against live boosted skills/varbits/varplayers/quests (1521-1550), with skill/varbit prewarm batched in one client-thread hop (365-377). Note the trade-off is deliberate and documented (dllmain.cpp:606-613, PathfinderConfig.h:71-78): the varbit/inventory reads are unsafe on the StaticPathfinder worker thread, so freshness is pushed to the render thread — but nothing dirty-gates the recompute, so ~99% of ticks do redundant work. Absolute cost is modest (low tens of microseconds class), consistent with severity=medium.

Citations: ours-search: §4 — dllmain.cpp:606-669, PathfinderConfig.cpp:114-132 | mb-transports: PathfinderConfig.java:317-335, 365-377, 1416-1441, 1521-1550

docs.title: [medium / speed] speed-no-pathfinder-reuse-or-cache
docs.text:
No path caching or same-target search reuse — every beginWalk/recalc is a fresh full search

Ours: NO path caching anywhere; every beginWalk and every recalculatePath performs a fresh search from scratch (ours-search §4). Nothing in the reports indicates a same-goal dedupe if a script re-issues walkTo to the same destination.

Microbot: walkWithStateInternal reuses the existing pathfinder when its target set already contains the requested target (Rs2Walker.java:1006-1013), and the transport-refresh snapshot memo avoids redundant config refresh work across restarts (PathfinderConfig.java:317-335).

Why it matters: Script loops that re-request the same destination (a common pattern) pay a full search dispatch each time instead of a no-op. Combined with the 5s budget class, redundant searches translate directly into worker churn and delayed first clicks.

Verification (high confidence): Core gap confirmed in current code, and it is slightly WORSE than claimed for the expensive case. PathExecutor::walkTo (OSRSClient/Pathfinding/PathExecutor.cpp:65-69) unconditionally cancel()s then re-plans; cancel() (PathExecutor.cpp:1314-1351) zeroes m_finalGoalX/Y and sets the cancelFlag on any pending StaticPathfinder worker — so there is no same-goal comparison, no record to compare against, and no path cache anywhere in OSRSClient/Pathfinding/. Re-issuing walkTo to the SAME destination while a cross-region search is in flight cancels and restarts that search from scratch; a script loop re-calling faster than the 5000ms search budget (PathExecutor.cpp:293) never obtains a path — Microbot's '!pathfinder.isDone() -> return MOVING' no-op (util/walker/Rs2Walker.java:1003-1005) plus getTargets().contains(target) reuse (1006-1013) prevents both failure modes. However the claim overstates breadth: (1) walkTo to a goal already within arrival distance is a no-op returning ARRIVED (PathExecutor.cpp:100-113); (2) tryDirectShortWalk skips pathfinding entirely for in-scene, live-reachable goals <=12 tiles (PathExecutor.cpp:124-144); (3) in-scene re-issues use synchronous local A* (~ms, PathExecutor.cpp:146-159), so redundant-search cost is only material for cross-region StaticPathfinder dispatches; (4) Bank::walkTo self-guards with Walk::isMoving() (PluginAPI/API/Bank.cpp:126-128), but that is caller discipline — Walk::to (PluginAPI/API/Walk.cpp:69-84) and the Lua bindings game.moveTo/walkTo/minimapWalkTo (ScriptEngine/ScriptAPI.cpp:388-429) pass straight through with no dedupe. The transport-refresh-memo half of the Microbot comparison is apples-to-oranges: SafeRS pushes usable-teleport/bank-teleport sets to PathfinderConfig every game tick from dllmain (Pathfinding/PathfinderConfig.h:70-94), so search dispatch pays no refresh cost at all (it instead pays a small per-tick recompute); Microbot's snapshot memo (shortestpath/pathfinder/PathfinderConfig.java:~314-336) optimizes a per-search refresh SafeRS does not have. Also note: no symbol 'beginWalk' exists — the entry point is PathExecutor::walkTo.

Citations: ours-search: §4 ('NO path caching anywhere — every beginWalk/recalc is a fresh search') | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:1006-1013 | mb-transports: PathfinderConfig.java:317-335

docs.title: [medium / speed] speed-slow-stuck-escalation-no-retry
docs.text:
Stuck escalation is slow (sidestep at >=24s, give-up at >=48s) and give-up lands in IDLE with no auto-retry

Ours: Sidestep requires 2 consecutive 12s same-tile stall periods (>=24s, more with combat 2.0x / interim 1.75x multipliers); give-up to IDLE after 4 (>=48s) with no retry — the walk just dies and the script sees a silent failure (PathExecutor.h:252, 396-397; cpp:926-945). ours-executor explicitly flags this as conservative vs Microbot.

Microbot: stuckCount-based sidestep increments per processWalk pass (sub-tick cadence) and fires at count>10 with weighted-random tile selection (Rs2Walker.java:1229-1242, 6841-6867); terminal EXIT states are auto-retried up to 3 times by ShortestPathScript unless user-stopped (ShortestPathScript.java:104-173).

Why it matters: Every genuinely-stuck event costs us roughly twice Microbot's wall-clock before recovery even attempts, and a give-up wastes the entire walk plus whatever script logic depended on arrival. Across thousands of paths the tail latency adds up and shows up as 'bot standing still' reports.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed in current code. Ours: PathExecutor.h:252 STALL_THRESHOLD_MS=12000; h:262-263 combat 2.0x / interim-minimap 1.75x (max, not stacked — cpp:1447-1460); h:396-397 MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_SIDESTEP=2 / MAX_STALLS_BEFORE_GIVE_UP=4. cpp:917-924 resets m_lastMovedTime per stall firing so each same-tile stall period is a full 12s×mult: sidestep first attempted at >=24s (cpp:933-940), give-up at >=48s sets m_state=IDLE and returns (cpp:926-930). No retry at any layer: Walk.cpp is a thin facade, ScriptAPI.cpp binds walkTo/isMoving/hasArrived with no wrapper, and hasArrived() is true only on ARRIVED (cpp:1363-1365) — so a script following the documented poll-hasArrived pattern (Walk.h:5-6) hangs forever on give-up; failure is only inferable via !isMoving() && !hasArrived(). STUCK enum exists but is never set (h:47-49). Microbot: checkIfStuck() increments stuckCount per processWalk pass (Rs2Walker.java:6841-6867), sidestep at stuckCount>10 with rankSidestepTilesToward + weighted-random top-3 pool (1229-1242); ShortestPathScript auto-retries terminal EXIT up to MAX_CONSECUTIVE_EXIT_RETRIES=3 unless user-stopped/dead/target-changed (ShortestPathScript.java:29,104-148). Two softening nuances: (1) Microbot ALSO has a 12s stall-recalc (STALL_BASE_MS=12_000, Rs2Walker.java:6872, fired 1204-1227) so recalc cadence is comparable — the real gap is the fast stuckCount sidestep path and the terminal-state retry; (2) our give-up is bypassed within CLOSE_ENOUGH=5 tiles of goal (mercy-ARRIVED, cpp:908-913), so the IDLE death only occurs when genuinely far from goal.

Citations: ours-executor: §2, notable flags — PathExecutor.h:252, 396-397; cpp:926-945, 1447-1460 | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:1229-1242, 6841-6867 | mb-transports: ShortestPathScript.java:104-173

docs.title: [medium / accuracy] accuracy-scene-size-garbage-band
docs.text:
SCENE_SIZE=110 vs engine width 104: 6-tile band of garbage collision flags accepted as in-scene

Ours: TileFlags.h:24 defines SCENE_SIZE=110 but the live-verified engine scene width is 104 (Offsets.h:608-610). CollisionMap.cpp:96 reads the engine width into 'sw' and then never uses it for iteration — the rebuild loops x=0..109 and copies 110 ints per column (CollisionMap.cpp:119-121, 133, verified in working tree), reading 6 rows/cols past the real data. Tiles in the base+104..109 band hold garbage flags yet isInScene accepts them (CollisionMap.cpp:215-220), so local A*, isTileReachable, and canTraverse can return phantom walkability verdicts near scene edges (plus a latent OOB read currently absorbed by SEH).

Microbot: No equivalent failure mode: Microbot has no oversized live-scene snapshot — collision queries go to client data at valid coordinates only, and its static map indexes by exact region extents (SplitFlagMap.java:27-47).

Why it matters: Path tiles and reachability probes near region boundaries can land in the garbage band, yielding phantom corridors or phantom walls precisely where long walks cross scene loads. Random per-scene garbage means non-reproducible misclicks that are nearly impossible to diagnose from logs.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate with two refinements. (1) Path: the cited CollisionMap.cpp lives at E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/GameSDK/CollisionMap.cpp (not Pathfinding/), but every cited line number matches the current working tree exactly: line 96 reads engine width into sw which is never referenced again; line 119 loops x=0..SCENE_SIZE-1 (110); line 133 copies colBytes=1104=440 bytes per column into m_flags[4][110][110] (CollisionMap.h:35); lines 215-220/222-227 accept scene indices up to 109. TileFlags.h:24 (Pathfinding/) defines SCENE_SIZE=110; Offsets.h:606-610+619 records Scene::Width=0x968 live-verified ==104 on 238.5 (2026-06-09). (2) Nuance: the width actually read at CollisionMap.cpp:95 is CollisionMap_::Width (colMapBase+0x08, marked [UNVERIFIED] at Offsets.h:852), and depending on heap layout the OOB reads can also fail (null/unreadable column ptr at x=104..109 → update() returns false at lines 122-144), so the failure mode is either a garbage flag band OR intermittent total collision-map invalidation — both stem from ignoring the engine-reported width. The uncommitted 2026-06-10 changes do NOT fix this: CollisionMap.cpp/.h and TileFlags.h are unmodified; the new guard in Pathfinder.cpp:49-54 still bounds-checks against SCENE_SIZE=110, and A neighbor expansion (Pathfinder.cpp:127) still explores the 104..109 band. Exposed consumers: local A (Pathfinder.cpp:135), PathExecutor::isTileReachable (PathExecutor.cpp:1629-1639 — garbage-band tiles pass the isInScene gate at line 1632 and get A-judged on garbage flags), adjustForWallDistance (PathExecutor.cpp:1648-1657), and script-facing Tile::isInScene/canTraverse (PluginAPI/API/Tile.cpp:13-22). Microbot side holds: SplitFlagMap.java:27-48 sizes region maps from exact extents and returns false for out-of-range/missing regions.

Citations: ours-collision: TileFlags.h:24; Offsets.h:608-610; CollisionMap.cpp:95-96, 119-121, 133, 215-220 | mb-search: SplitFlagMap.java:27-47

docs.title: [medium / accuracy] accuracy-interpolation-not-reachability-gated
docs.text:
Interpolated click targets checked for walkability only; geometric canvas fallback has no tile validation

Ours: The smoothed-waypoint pick IS live-reachability gated with a furthest-reachable-raw-tile fallback (PathExecutor.cpp:1070, 1076-1084) — the prior-audit 'smoothed-pick not reachability-gated' failure is fixed. But the interpolation branch (kickoff beyond MAX_REACH, cpp:1098-1106) steps back along the player->kickoff ray testing only WALKABILITY at radii {12,10,8,6,4} (cpp:1775-1786), and its final geometric fallback goes straight to canvas with no tile validation at all (cpp:1803-1806). A walkable-but-unreachable tile across a wall/fence can be aimed at; the deliberate no-click-on-unreachable policy applied to waypoints (cpp:1085-1087) is not applied here.

Microbot: Interpolation similarly leans on server walk-here routing (Rs2Walker.java:3372-3407), but Microbot's fallback ladder is reachability-first: walkReachableMiniMapToward sorts BFS-reachable tiles by distance-to-target before any scaled-vector geometric fallback (:2265-2323), and unreachable forward waypoints are substituted with the furthest REACHABLE rawPath tile (:1771-1779).

Why it matters: Long-segment paths (post-smoothing) hit the interpolation branch constantly. Aiming at tiles across walls makes the engine path the player somewhere unintended, producing off-path drift, wall-hugging behavior, and occasional stall cycles — exactly the interpolation aiming-error class this audit targets.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed against current on-disk code. SafeRS PathExecutor.cpp: smoothed-pick branch is reachability-gated (isTileReachable :1070; findFurthestReachableRawPathPoint fallback :1076-1084; no-click policy :1085-1087), but the interpolation branch (:1098-1106, fires when kickoff is beyond MAX_REACH=13, PathExecutor.h:227) sets haveTarget=true unconditionally. interpolateClickableTarget (:1728-1807) tests only m_collision.isWalkable per radius {12,10,8,6,4} including the ray step-back (:1772-1786); it never calls isTileReachable. Its final geometric fallback (:1803-1806) returns the scaled point with NO validation at all (no walkability, reachability, or in-scene check) and projectTileForClick (:1559) falls through to canvas. The only reachability check in the interpolated click path is adjustForWallDistance:1684, which gates the wall-offset NEIGHBOR, not the interpolated tile. Microbot Rs2Walker.java: interpolation (:1711-1728) is likewise walkability-only at creation, BUT the resulting clickTarget is then reachability-gated at :1772 (Rs2Tile.isTileReachable) with furthest-reachable-rawPath substitution :1773-1779 BEFORE the click (:1792); and walkMiniMapToward (:2265-2303) tries BFS-reachable-tile selection first (walkReachableMiniMapToward :2277, :2305-2323) before its geometric radii fallback (:2281-2300). Net gap: SafeRS never reachability-validates interpolated targets at any point in the chain; Microbot does, at two layers. One nuance shrinking the delta slightly: Microbot's own last-rung geometric fallback (:2281-2300) is also reachability-unvalidated (clip-check only), and SafeRS's stall-timer/recompute + comment :1063-1067 show the team knows interpolating toward unreachable targets causes oscillation — the guard just wasn't applied to case (b). Severity medium is fair: minimap clicks use server-side routing, so a walkable-but-unreachable aim tile usually causes route-around drift/wall-hugging rather than hard failure.

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor.cpp:1070, 1076-1087, 1098-1106, 1728-1807 (esp. 1775-1786, 1803-1806) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:3372-3407, 2265-2323, 1771-1779

docs.title: [medium / accuracy] accuracy-underground-y-heuristic-missing
docs.text:
No mod-6400 underground-Y heuristic wrap: dungeon-bound searches misdirected and prone to premature partials

Ours: Static heuristic is plain Chebyshev on x/y (StaticPathfinder.cpp:103-109, plane ignored). The Skretzo-derived map data places underground areas at y+6400, so a dungeon goal inflates h by ~6400 for every surface node — an inadmissible overestimate relative to a cheap trapdoor transport, in a search with no node re-opening (visited locked at insert, :360-361). Worse, the best-effort progress metric (chebyshev+manhattan to goal, :284-286, 339-346) barely improves while walking toward the entrance, so the 5s no-progress deadline can fire and return a partial path even though a valid route exists.

Microbot: Heuristic takes min(direct, mod-6400-wrapped) distance explicitly so underground targets don't misdirect surface expansion, with an admissibility argument documented at Pathfinder.java:226-250; its progress-based cutoff therefore keeps resetting while approaching the entrance.

Why it matters: Every walk into a dungeon/cave (mining, slayer, quests — daily bread for a botting client) searches against a wrong heuristic: suboptimal routes from the frozen-g/no-reopen scheme, and intermittent 5s-timeout partials that the executor then walks, ending far from the requested tile.

Verification (high confidence): Core claim verified against current (2026-06-10) code. StaticPathfinder.cpp: chebyshev() at :103-109 is plain L-inf on x/y with no mod-6400 wrap, used for all hCost (:210/:273/:369/:416/:457); goal packed on the same plane as start (:178-179) so underground goals (y+6400 convention) inflate h by ~6400 for every surface node — inadmissible vs trapdoor edges costing t->duration (:412); visited locked at insert with no re-opening (:360-361 walking, :386-387 transports); progress metric = chebyshev+manhattan (:284-286 init, :339-346 reset) with 5000ms no-progress budget (StaticPathfinder.h:51, PathExecutor.cpp:293); timeout partials are walked — PathExecutor::consumePendingStatic (PathExecutor.cpp:350-359) accepts any path.size()>=2 and never checks result.found. No compensation upstream: Walk.cpp maybeTranslateInstanceGoal (:75-82) only handles instance-template coords (~13000+), unrelated to the y+6400 convention; grep for 6400/wrap across Pathfinding/ and PluginAPI/ finds nothing. Microbot comparison accurate: Pathfinder.java has UNDERGROUND_Y_OFFSET=6400 with min(direct, wrapped) heuristic and documented admissibility argument at :224-247 (claim cited 226-250; trivially off). ONE REFINEMENT: the claim overstates the progress-stall — the y+6400 goal is always coordinate-north, so northward surface expansion DOES keep resetting the 5s deadline. The premature-partial fires conditionally: when northward progress is blocked (coast/fences) or the entrance lies opposite the mirrored-goal direction (south / wrong-x), no popped node improves chebyshev+manhattan and a found=false partial is returned and walked. The heuristic misdirection and inadmissibility (suboptimal routes under the frozen-g/no-reopen scheme) are unconditional for every underground-bound search.

Citations: ours-search: StaticPathfinder.cpp:103-109, 284-286, 339-346, 360-361 | mb-search: Pathfinder.java:226-250

docs.title: [medium / accuracy] accuracy-transport-anchor-size-hardcoded
docs.text:
Transport firing hardcodes sizeX/sizeY=1, bypassing SW-anchor auto-snap for multi-tile objects

Ours: When firing an object transport, the executor builds the ActionTarget manually with sizeX/sizeY hardcoded to 1 (PathExecutor.cpp:680-681) instead of going through GameObject::interact, which auto-snaps to the SW anchor and fills sizeX/sizeY (per re_oploc_anchor_in_api). The live object is resolved by id nearest the TSV origin within 3 tiles (cpp:630-670), but a multi-tile transport object (large stairs, gangplanks, big trapdoors) can still be mis-anchored in the OPLOC1 packet — the server silently rejects, leading to the 6s TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT and a recalc.

Microbot: Resolves the live object within 10 tiles of origin, preferring objects that advertise the required action, and interacts via Rs2GameObject.interact which handles the object footprint/anchor; failed interacts get a canvas/minimap nudge fallback rather than a silent timeout (Rs2Walker.java:5885-5990, 6051-6059).

Why it matters: OPLOC packets with wrong anchor coordinates are silently dropped server-side (established in OPOBJ/OPLOC RE work), so each affected transport costs 6s + recalc and can loop on routes whose only viable edge is the multi-tile object.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed on current (2026-06-10) code, with one mechanism correction. PathExecutor.cpp:672-681 builds the ActionTarget manually with t.sizeX=1/t.sizeY=1 and fires via Interact::perform, bypassing GameObject::interact. The real server-reject vector is NOT the hardcoded size — it is the tile pick: PathExecutor.cpp:639-670 resolves the live object via raw ObjectQuery::byId (ObjectQuery.cpp:224-229), which returns one entry PER OCCUPIED TILE with no SW-anchor dedupe (the anchor snap + LocType size backfill live in dedupeByAnchor, ObjectQuery.cpp:108-128, and in GameObject::interact, GameObject.cpp:95-112 — neither is on this path). The executor picks the footprint tile nearest the TSV origin (<=3 tiles), and Interact::perform (Interact.cpp:936-948) puts target.tileX/tileY verbatim into the OPLOC coordType with no anchor correction. For a multi-tile object approached from the non-SW side, a non-anchor footprint tile is strictly closer to the stand tile and wins, producing OPLOC1 coords the server silently drops — the codebase itself documents this failure (GameObject.cpp:80-82). Mitigations that narrow but don't close the gap: walkScene iterates plane->x->z so the SW-most tile wins distance ties (strict d edge skipped + immediate recalculatePath() (PathExecutor.cpp:518-552), no retry or interact-level fallback, so a route whose only edge is a multi-tile object can loop. Microbot contrast verified: Rs2Walker.java ~5898-5917 resolves within 10 tiles of origin preferring objects advertising the required action, interacts via footprint-aware Rs2GameObject.interact with camera-turn prep (prepareTransportObjectForInteraction, ~6050-6058) and handleObjectExceptions recovery.

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor.cpp:630-670, 680-681 | ours-executor: COMPLETENESS note (re_oploc_anchor_in_api: GameObject::interact auto-snaps, this path builds ActionTarget manually) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:5885-5990, 6051-6059

docs.title: [medium / completeness] completeness-minigames-tsv-header-bug
docs.text:
Header-detection defect: 0 of 20 minigame teleports load from teleportation_minigames.tsv

Ours: Loader only accepts a '#'-prefixed header line (TransportRegistry.cpp:95-114, re-verified on disk); teleportation_minigames.tsv has an UNcommented header row, which is skipped as 'data row before header' (:117), then the first commented section line ('# Barbarian Assault - ...' with trailing pad-tabs passing the >=2-cell guard at :104) is adopted as the header. With no 'Destination' column key every row fails the required-destination check (Transport.cpp:94) -> 0 of 20 rows load. Our-side parser defect, distinct from the ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL seeding exclusion.

Microbot: Header is simply the first line stripped of '#'/'# ' whether commented or not (Transport.java:475-535); all minigame rows load, and the minigame grouping-tab teleport handler executes them (Rs2Walker.java:7160-7241) with the @cooldown varplayer guarding the shared 20-min cooldown.

Why it matters: Minigame teleports are free, cooldown-shared long-range hops (Barbarian Assault, Pest Control, Tithe Farm, etc.) that Microbot uses as zero-cost route anchors. Currently doubly dead for us (parse bug + ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL seeding exclusion) — fixing the seeding gap alone would silently leave this file at zero rows.

Verification (high confidence): Claim verified verbatim against current uncommitted code. TransportRegistry.cpp:95 only treats '#'-prefixed lines as header candidates; the uncommented header row (teleportation_minigames.tsv line 1, runtime copy at E:/SafeRS/x64/Release/transports/, loaded via dllmain.cpp:1283) is dropped by the data-before-header guard at TransportRegistry.cpp:117. The next line '# Barbarian Assault - Barbarian Outpost' carries 8 trailing pad-tabs (9 cells), passes the >=2-cell guard at :104, and is adopted as a garbage header whose sole key is the section title. With no 'Destination' column, all 20 data rows fail Transport.cpp:94 (destination required) and are rejected — 0/20 load (loadOneFile would log '0 loaded, 20 rejected'). Microbot (Transport.java:479-535, addTransports) takes the first line as header and strips '#'/'# ' only if present, so the same uncommented header parses fine; minigame file registered at :603 and executed by Rs2Walker.handleMinigameTeleport (:7160, dispatched :5845). The 'doubly dead' qualifier also holds: StaticPathfinder.cpp:242-243 still seeds only TELEPORTATION_SPELL, excluding ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL.

Citations: ours-transports: §1 — TransportRegistry.cpp:95-117 (header logic, re-verified 2026-06-10), Transport.cpp:94, 0/20 rows loaded | mb-transports: §2 — Transport.java:475-535 (tolerant header parse) | mb-executor: §3 — Rs2Walker.java:7160-7241 (minigame handler)

docs.title: [medium / completeness] completeness-teleports-start-only-seeding
docs.text:
Teleports seeded at the start tile only — no frontier injection, no multi-teleport chaining

Ours: Teleport seeding happens once, at the start tile (StaticPathfinder.cpp:236-282; comment :240-241 'multi-teleport paths unsupported'). A route of the form walk-somewhere-then-teleport (e.g. exit a teleport-blocked zone, then cast) is structurally unfindable; recalcs re-seeding from the current position only partially mitigate. Bank-tile synthetic spell edges (:433-467) are the single mid-path exception.

Microbot: Origin-less teleports are injected at frontier tiles via refreshTeleports as the search progresses — specifically at wilderness-level transitions, so a teleport unusable at the level-31 start becomes available the moment the search pops a sub-30/20/0 tile (Pathfinder.java:368, 392-397, 483, 506-511; PathfinderConfig.java:250-276) — wilderness exits via walking-then-teleport are found in-graph.

Why it matters: Combined with the missing wilderness model this makes every escape-then-teleport route invisible; more broadly any plan where the optimal teleport departure point is not the start tile (teleblock zones, instances exits) degrades to pure walking. Lower standalone severity because outside wilderness Microbot's injection also effectively concentrates near the start.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed in current working tree. SafeRS: teleport seeding happens once at the start node only — StaticPathfinder.cpp:235-282 (comment at :238-240: "We simplify: consider teleports only at the start... Multi-teleport paths aren't supported in v1"); mid-search transport expansion explicitly skips teleports at :382 (if (TransportTypeUtil::isTeleport(t->type)) continue;); the bank-tile synthetic spell edges at :433-467 are indeed the single mid-path exception. The gap is slightly WIDER than claimed: only TELEPORTATION_SPELL is seeded even at start (:250) — ITEM/MINIGAME/SEASONAL teleports are excluded entirely; and there is no wilderness model at all (PathfinderConfig.h:16 "no live wilderness-level tracker"; Transport.cpp:111 parses maxWildernessLevel from TSV but no code consults it). PathExecutor::recalculatePath (PathExecutor.cpp:214,246) re-runs findPath from the current position on stall/off-path/path-end, which re-seeds teleports there — a reactive partial mitigation, not in-graph planning, exactly as claimed. Microbot: Pathfinder.java:108 inits wildernessLevel=31; :368/:483 call config.refreshTeleports(start,31); :381-399 and :496-511 re-inject teleports at the popped frontier node whenever the wilderness level transitions (31→30→20→0); PathfinderConfig.java:250-275 refreshTeleports() keys usable teleports into the transports map at that frontier tile — so walk-out-of-wilderness-then-teleport routes are found in-graph. The uncommitted 2026-06-10 changes (DaxWalker WinHTTP timeouts, PathExecutor PATH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS watchdog, Pathfinder.cpp out-of-scene-bounds guard, GlobalCollisionMap deletion) do not alter teleport seeding.

Citations: ours-search §5B: StaticPathfinder.cpp:236-282, comment :240-241; bank-edge exception :433-467 | mb-search §1/§7: Pathfinder.java:368, 392-397, 506-511; PathfinderConfig.java:250-276 | ours-collision finding 5: 'teleports only from start tile — mid-path teleport opportunities never considered'

docs.title: [medium / completeness] completeness-multidest-and-home-teleport-excluded
docs.text:
Multi-destination ':' spell rows and Home Teleport excluded from usable-teleport computation

Ours: refreshUsableTeleports excludes rows with ':' multi-destination displayInfo (dllmain.cpp:625, marked TODO) and Home Teleport via info.level == 0 (dllmain.cpp:629). Multi-destination spells (Camelot Seers/outside, Watchtower variants, etc.) and the free 30-min home teleport contribute nothing.

Microbot: displayInfo 'Prefix: suffix' grammar resolves spell name + destination/menu option at both refresh and execution (PathfinderConfig.java:1092-1102; Rs2Walker.java:6517-6524); Lumbridge Home Teleport is supported with a special 35s completion wait (Rs2Walker.java:5864-5865).

Why it matters: Home teleport is the only zero-cost teleport every account always has — its absence penalizes exactly the low-level/fresh accounts a bot farm runs most. Multi-destination spell variants are standard members routing.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate against current (2026-06-10, uncommitted) code, with two precision notes. (1) SafeRS refresh side: dllmain.cpp:625 skips any row whose displayInfo contains ':' (comment "multi-dest: TODO"); dllmain.cpp:629 skips level-0 spells (comment "Home — excluded v1"). However, the TSV row is named "Lumbridge Home Teleport" while the Spells table entry (PluginAPI/API/Spells.cpp:81) is "Home Teleport"; Spells::idByName uses nameContains(tableName, query) (GameSDK/IdLookupHelpers.cpp:19-22), so the lookup fails first and the row is actually dropped at dllmain.cpp:627 ("not in Spells table") — line 629 is a backstop that would catch it if the name resolved. Net effect identical to the claim. (2) The gap is doubly enforced: the executor fire callback (dllmain.cpp:1451-1454) resolves the raw displayInfo via Spells::byName with no ':' prefix/suffix grammar and no home-teleport branch, so these rows could not execute even if the refresh-side skips were removed; the code comment at dllmain.cpp:611-612 explicitly says the exclusions "match the executor". Impact confirmed in data: E:/SafeRS/x64/Release/transports/teleportation_spells.tsv contains 10 ':' multi-dest rows (e.g. "Varrock Teleport: Grand Exchange", "Teleport to House: Outside") plus the Lumbridge Home Teleport row — all contribute nothing. Microbot behavior verified as cited, with one path correction: PathfinderConfig.java is at shortestpath/pathfinder/PathfinderConfig.java, where isTeleportationSpellUsable (~lines 1092-1100) splits displayInfo on ':' and resolves the prefix; Rs2Walker.java handleTeleportSpell (~6515-6531) splits ':' into spell name + menu option (identifier 2 vs 1, default "cast") and special-cases MagicAction.LUMBRIDGE_HOME_TELEPORT via Rs2Magic.quickCast; Rs2Walker.java ~5864-5866 applies the dedicated 35s landing wait (sleepUntilTrue ..., 600, 35000) for home teleport.

Citations: ours-search §5 (usability pipeline): dllmain.cpp:625 (':' rows excluded), dllmain.cpp:629 (Home Teleport excluded) | ours-transports §4: same exclusions listed with TODO | mb-transports §6: PathfinderConfig.java:1092-1102, Rs2Walker.java:6517-6524 | mb-executor §3: Rs2Walker.java:5864-5865 (home teleport 35s wait)

docs.title: [medium / completeness] completeness-poh-transports-absent
docs.text:
No POH transport integration — house portals, jewellery box, nexus invisible to routing

Ours: The POH enum value is permanently zero-count: no file binding exists and the comment notes POH was folded into teleportation_portals upstream (TransportRegistry.cpp:40-41). There is no runtime injection of house-specific transports and no POH-instance start handling.

Microbot: POH transports are injected at runtime by PohPanel and merged into the transport set each refresh, skipping to-PoH teleports when already in the house (createMergedList, PathfinderConfig.java:607-634); executor fires PohTransport.execute (Rs2Walker.java:6004-6009); when starting inside the POH instance the pathfinder start is remapped to the configured exit portal so origins match (ShortestPathPlugin.java:818-845 — without this the walker tight-loops).

Why it matters: A built POH (jewellery box + nexus + portals) is the single best teleport hub for mid/high-level accounts; Microbot accounts route through it constantly. Also implies SafeRS paths that START inside a POH have no valid graph position at all.

Verification (high confidence): Claim holds in full against the 2026-06-10 working tree, with two sharpening points. (1) TransportRegistry.cpp:17-42 FILE_BINDINGS has no POH entry and the line 40-41 comment claims POH-portals were "folded into teleportation_portals" — but the shipped teleportation_portals.tsv (E:/SafeRS/x64/Release/transports/) contains zero house/nexus/jewellery rows (only world portals like Castle Wars), so the comment is misleading: Microbot's POH transports are runtime-generated (PohPanel/PohTransport), never TSV rows, and SafeRS gets no POH coverage from any file. (2) The gap is structural, not just missing data: TransportRegistry has no runtime-injection API at all (only loadFromDirectory/loadOneFile), and its reserve-then-store-pointers design (TransportRegistry.cpp:148-177) assumes the transport vector never grows after load — adding Microbot-style per-refresh POH merging requires registry rework. (3) POH-instance start handling is absent as claimed: Walk.cpp:35-65 maybeTranslateInstanceGoal only translates the GOAL into instance space when the goal's template chunk is mapped in the current scene; a POH-start/overworld-goal walk leaves start in raw instance coords (~13000) vs template-space goal with no exit-portal remap — the exact tight-loop failure Microbot patched in ShortestPathPlugin.java ~824-845.

Citations: ours-transports §5: TransportRegistry.cpp:40-41 (POH zero-count, no binding) | mb-transports §1/§3: PathfinderConfig.java:607-634 (runtime PohPanel injection) | mb-executor §3: Rs2Walker.java:6004-6009; ShortestPathPlugin.java:818-845 (POH start remap)

docs.title: [medium / completeness] completeness-banked-transport-planning
docs.text:
No banked-transport planning for items/staves/currency — bank awareness exists for spell runes only

Ours: Bank awareness is limited to synthetic bank-teleport SPELL edges: cast-from-bank rune coverage using the (stale-after-close) BankCache across 13 hardcoded bank locations (dllmain.cpp:644-665; consumed StaticPathfinder.cpp:433-467). There is no plan-a-bank-trip phase for teleport items, fairy-ring staves, or boat/cart fare currency, and itemIdsRaw/currencyRaw are never evaluated against bank or inventory at all.

Microbot: walkWithBankedTransportsAndState (Rs2Walker.java:8176-8282) compares direct vs via-bank route costs, withdraws missing transport items — fairy-ring staves auto-required unless elite diary, currency for boats/carts (:2799-2833) — then walks; useBankItems threads bank contents through staff checks, item snapshots, currency, spell runes, and generic item requirements (PathfinderConfig.java:308, 348-354, 837-853, 1092-1102, 1066-1079), with bank-mirror bootstrap when the cache is cold (:8284-8319).

Why it matters: Real long-haul efficiency comes from 'bank first, grab the tab/staff/coins, then travel'. Without it, even after the item-teleport and fairy-ring gaps are fixed, an account whose teleport consumables sit in the bank routes as if it owns nothing.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate against current (2026-06-10 uncommitted) code. Bank awareness = spell-rune bank-teleport edges only: dllmain.cpp:614-669 (considerBankRunes gate :618, BankCache::count :651, 13 hardcoded bank locations via kBankLocCount :656-665), consumed StaticPathfinder.cpp:427-467; BankCache stale-after-close dllmain.cpp:671-684. itemIdsRaw/currencyRaw are parsed (Transport.cpp:102,106) but have zero consumers repo-wide; PathfinderConfig.h:14 still marks item requirements STUBBED and isAllowed (PathfinderConfig.cpp:34-57) checks only members+varbits. Only TELEPORTATION_SPELL is considered (dllmain.cpp:624) — no fairy-ring staff, no boat/cart currency, no direct-vs-via-bank comparison, no withdraw-then-walk phase. Minor nuance: with a bank OPEN, Magic::canCast(live.bank=true) at dllmain.cpp:635-637 counts live (not stale) bank runes — still spell-runes-only.

Citations: ours-search §5C: dllmain.cpp:656-665 (bank-rune spell edges, the only bank awareness); BankCache stale-after-close dllmain.cpp:671-684 | mb-executor §3: Rs2Walker.java:8176-8282, :2799-2833, :8284-8319 | mb-transports §3: useBankItems threading PathfinderConfig.java:348-354, 837-853, 1066-1079, 1092-1102

docs.title: [low / speed] speed-local-astar-iteration-cap
docs.text:
Local A* MAX_ITERATIONS=10000 < 12100 scene tiles — hard in-scene mazes fail local and fall through to a needless async static dispatch

Ours: MAX_ITERATIONS=10000 (Pathfinder.h:62) is below the 110x110=12100 tile count, so a worst-case scene maze exhausts before full exploration and returns found=false with NO partial path (Pathfinder.cpp:147-149); beginWalk then falls through to the async StaticPathfinder worker (PathExecutor.cpp:160-163) — thread spawn + queue latency for a path that was solvable in-scene.

Microbot: Single search engine with progress-based cutoff and an always-available best-node partial path; no equivalent two-tier fail-over for in-scene targets (Pathfinder.java:145-162, 425-429).

Why it matters: Rare but pure waste when it hits: milliseconds of sync work discarded for a multi-hundred-ms async round-trip. Low frequency keeps this low severity.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed on current disk (2026-06-10 working tree). Pathfinder.h:62 still has MAX_ITERATIONS=10000 vs SCENE_SIZE=110 (TileFlags.h:24) = 12100 tiles. Pathfinder.cpp:88 caps the loop; exhaustion returns found=false with an EMPTY path (no partial/best-node) at Pathfinder.cpp:147-149. The cap is effectively tighter than 10000 unique tiles: ++iterations (line 89) precedes the closed/stale-pop skip (line 120), so duplicate PQ pops burn budget too. PathExecutor::beginWalk uses the local result only if found && size>=2 (PathExecutor.cpp:148); on failure it falls through (comment 160-163) to dispatchStaticPathfinder at PathExecutor.cpp:165-170 — the dispatch body (272-311) spawns a detached std::thread per request (line 290, 5000ms budget) and parks in WAITING_FOR_PATH, drained by per-tick polling (consumePendingStatic, 313+). Microbot side as claimed: single engine with progress-resetting time cutoff (Pathfinder.java:411-418 reset, 425-429 cutoff) and always-available bestLastNode partial path via getPath() (145-162). Caveat: the static fall-through is correct design for genuinely unreachable in-scene goals (small reachable region drains the open queue before the cap); the waste occurs only in the rare cap-exhaustion case where the goal was reachable but needed >10000 pops — matching the claim's low severity.

Citations: ours-search: Pathfinder.h:62, Pathfinder.cpp:147-149, §10d; PathExecutor.cpp:160-163 | mb-search: Pathfinder.java:145-162, 425-429

docs.title: [low / speed] speed-visited-hashset-vs-bitset
docs.text:
Static search visited-set is std::unordered_set vs Microbot's lazily-allocated per-region bitsets

Ours: visited = std::unordered_set of packed tiles (StaticPathfinder.cpp:195) — per-node hash + bucket cost on every insert/lookup; ours-collision notes this is 'measurable on long searches' vs upstream's dedicated bitset.

Microbot: VisitedTiles: per-64x64-region long[] bitsets allocated only when first touched, 1 bit/tile, O(1) bit math, with out-of-bounds reads reporting 'visited' as a prune (VisitedTiles.java:56-69, 83-113).

Why it matters: Continent-scale searches touch hundreds of thousands of nodes; hash overhead inflates worker time on exactly the searches that already flirt with the progress budget. Micro-optimization, but free upstream design to copy.

Verification (high confidence):

Citations: ours-collision: port fidelity section — StaticPathfinder.cpp:195 | mb-search: VisitedTiles.java:56-69, 83-113

docs.title: [low / speed] speed-no-bidirectional-search
docs.text:
No bidirectional search mode for very long routes

Ours: StaticPathfinder is strictly unidirectional; no reverse-neighbor expansion or meet-in-the-middle exists in the port (ours-search §1 — no equivalent mechanism listed).

Microbot: Bidirectional meet-in-the-middle when single target and start-target Chebyshev >= 2000: backward search via CollisionMap.getReverseNeighbors with an incoming-transports-by-destination index, forward/backward join bookkeeping (Pathfinder.java:36, 599-601, 276-357; CollisionMap.java:286-376). Microbot's own docs note the backward half drops origin-less teleports.

Why it matters: Cross-map searches explore roughly twice the frontier unidirectionally — longer worker occupancy and later first click. 2000+ tile requests are rare in practice and our progress budget keeps them alive, so impact is small.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed against current uncommitted code (2026-06-10). SafeRS StaticPathfinder (E:/SafeRS/OSRSClient/Pathfinding/StaticPathfinder.cpp) is strictly unidirectional: one start node seeded (lines 210-213), forward-only 8-neighbor expansion (356-374), forward transport-edge expansion (380-425), start-tile-only teleport seeding (247-282), boundary+pending two-queue pop selector (314-325). No reverse-neighbor, backward-frontier, or meeting logic exists anywhere in OSRSClient (grep for getReverseNeighbors/boundaryBackward/bidirectional returns only a PathExecutor.cpp:1405-1409 comment about a small one-sided closest-waypoint recovery BFS — unrelated to route search). Microbot side matches the claim exactly: BIDIRECTIONAL_MIN_CHEBYSHEV=2000 (pathfinder/Pathfinder.java:36), gate targetsPacked.length == 1 && minCheb >= 2000 → runBidirectional() (599-611), backward queues boundaryBackward/pendingBackward (74-75), meet bookkeeping maybeImproveMeeting/combineBidirectionalPath/addNeighbors{Forward,Backward}WithMeet (289-357), runBidirectional (451-590), and CollisionMap.getReverseNeighbors with incomingByDestPacked transport index (CollisionMap.java:286-376) whose javadoc (282-284) explicitly states origin-less teleports are omitted from the backward half. Minor citation drift only: meet bookkeeping starts at Pathfinder.java:289, not 276. The low-severity framing is also supported: SafeRS's progress-reset budget (StaticPathfinder.cpp:339-346) keeps long unidirectional searches alive rather than timing them out.

Citations: ours-search: §1 (single-direction two-queue design) | mb-search: Pathfinder.java:36, 599-601, 276-357; CollisionMap.java:286-376

docs.title: [low / speed] speed-adv-packet-click-dispatch
docs.text:
ADVANTAGE (ours): packet/engine-dispatch clicks with zero mouse emulation overhead or post-click sleeps

Ours: Clicks are queued per tick and fired on the render/engine threads via EngineDispatch — slot 1006 minimap synth or slot 23 DoAction wire packet with explicit tile coords (PathExecutor.cpp:1248-1312). No cursor movement, no minimap zoom manipulation, no blocking sleeps in the click path; focus-independent and multi-client safe per the input architecture.

Microbot: walkMiniMap sets minimap zoom to 5 then physically mouse-clicks the worldToMinimap point (Rs2Walker.java:2247-2263); every click is followed by a blocking sleepUntil up to 2000ms with a 600ms minimum elapsed (:1810-1827); recovery paths add sleepGaussian(1000,300) (:1229-1242); pathfinder readiness is polled in 1200ms slices with 120-220ms random sleeps (:1097-1120).

Why it matters: Per-click overhead is effectively zero for us vs hundreds of ms of mandatory sleeps for Microbot — a structural speed edge worth protecting. Listed so the gap analysis is not one-sided; do not regress this while porting Microbot behaviors that assume mouse latency.

Verification (high confidence): Advantage is real with two precision fixes. (1) SafeRS minimap leg is NOT a client-side slot-1006 DoAction dispatch — DoAction has no slot-1006 arm; Interact::walkToMinimapPoint (E:\SafeRS\OSRSClient\GameSDK\Interact.cpp:1222-1267) synthesizes three CallWindowProcW messages (WM_MOUSEMOVE/LBUTTONDOWN/LBUTTONUP) per-HWND, after which the engine fires slot 1006 internally. Still zero motion interpolation, zero sleeps, focus-independent — but it is message-level mouse synthesis and memory flags WndProc as a temporary stopgap. Canvas leg is as claimed: slot 23 forces the 0x6F MOVE_GAME_CLICK wire packet with explicit tile coords (Interact.cpp:1583-1596), queued via EngineDispatch from PathExecutor::onFrame (PathExecutor.cpp:1256-1311); no Sleep/sleep_for anywhere in Pathfinding/ or Interact.cpp; no minimap zoom writes. (2) Microbot's click is synthetic AWT canvas events, not OS-physical mouse (VirtualMouse.java:66-111), but it blocks the walker thread on NaturalMouse human-motion simulation per click (VirtualMouse.java:132-136, NaturalMouse.java:62-91) — so the per-click latency point stands. Microbot citations confirmed but file is util/walker/Rs2Walker.java (not shortestpath/): walkMiniMap zoom-set+click :2247-2263; post-click sleepUntil 2000ms cap with 600ms hard floor :1820-1827 (plus a second 2000ms sleepUntil :1831-1835); recovery sleepGaussian(1000,300) :1229-1242; pathfinder polling 1200ms slices + 120-220ms sleeps :1097-1120 (constants :144-146).

Citations: ours-executor: §1 — PathExecutor.cpp:1248-1312, 1294-1309 | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:2247-2263, 1810-1827, 1229-1242, 1097-1120 | memory: feedback_input_background_multiclient, feedback_packet_path_default

docs.title: [low / speed] speed-adv-frame-rate-consumption-eager-map
docs.text:
ADVANTAGE (ours): frame-rate async path consumption, eager all-RAM collision map, and no-recalc transport handoff

Ours: Async static results are consumed in onFrame, landing within ~7-16ms of completion (PathExecutor.cpp:1252-1254). Collision data is pre-converted to SCM1 and loaded fully into RAM at inject — no mid-search zip inflation (SplitFlagMap.cpp:44-101; ours-collision calls it a 'SPEED win'). Transport success deliberately skips recalc (path already contains post-transport tiles, cpp:554-566) and multi-step chains advance the SAME tick when the next object appears (cpp:483-517). The 2026-05-19 fixes (path clipping at transport origin, wall-adjust transport-origin exemption) are verified still present.

Microbot: Pathfinder-done waits are 1200ms poll slices + random 120-220ms sleeps with a 10s budget (Rs2Walker.java:1097-1120); upstream lazily inflates zip regions on first touch; transport completion usually triggers restartPathfinding unless the precomputed-continuation check hits (:6150-6284).

Why it matters: First-click latency after a path lands and transport-chain throughput are structurally better in our design. Recorded so the comparison stays two-sided and these properties are treated as regressions if lost during gap-closing work.

Verification (high confidence): Two of three claimed advantages hold as stated; the collision-map advantage is overstated to the point of being wrong about Microbot. (1) CONFIRMED: frame-rate async consumption — PathExecutor::onFrame (PathExecutor.cpp:1248-1254) consumes pending static/dax results per frame, driven from the present hook (dllmain.cpp:738). But Microbot's effective post-completion latency is ~0-100ms, not 1200ms: awaitPathfinderDone = sleepUntilTrue(isDone, 100, 1200) (Rs2WalkerRuntimeAwaits.java:14-19), with occasional +120-220ms inter-slice sleeps (Rs2Walker.java:1116, constants :144-146, 10s budget :1108). Advantage is real but ~6-13x, not vs-1200ms. (2) REFUTED sub-claim: Microbot does NOT lazily inflate zip regions mid-search — ShortestPathPlugin.startUp() (ShortestPathPlugin.java:215-217) calls SplitFlagMap.fromResources() (pathfinder/SplitFlagMap.java:88-115) which decompresses the ENTIRE collision-map.zip and materializes all regions as BitSet-backed FlagMaps at plugin startup. Both sides are eager all-RAM; only trivial startup decompress cost differs (ours: raw SCM1 read, SplitFlagMap.cpp:19-102, loaded at inject dllmain.cpp:1301-1303). Lazy inflation describes Skretzo upstream, not the audited Microbot fork. (3) CONFIRMED: success no-recalc (PathExecutor.cpp:554-566), same-tick chain advance (cpp:479-517 falls through to fire next edge same tick), timeout-only recalc (cpp:541-551). Microbot side slightly understated: finishHandledTransport (Rs2Walker.java:6150-6201) has TWO no-restart hatches — expected-destination queue primed from the planned path (:1255, :6203-6230) AND precomputed-continuation (:6260-6284) — so planned catalog transports usually avoid restart there too; restart when taken is destination-aware (:6178). (4) CONFIRMED: 2026-05-19 fixes present — pathClipIndex cpp:1809-1820, wall-adjust transport-origin exemption cpp:1151-1173 (plus newer final-goal exemption :1157-1166).

Citations: ours-executor: §2 (cpp:1252-1254), §3 (cpp:483-517, 554-566), §1 (pathClipIndex cpp:1809-1820, wall-adjust exemptions cpp:1151-1173) | ours-collision: SplitFlagMap.cpp:44-101 (eager SCM1 load vs lazy zip) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:1097-1120, 6150-6284

docs.title: [low / accuracy] accuracy-offpath-detection-chebyshev-not-reachability
docs.text:
Off-path detection is Chebyshev-distance based, blind to across-the-wall divergence

Ours: Off-path triggers at chebyshev >10 from the nearest waypoint (OFF_PATH_THRESHOLD, PathExecutor.h:276; cpp:964-997). A player separated from the path by a wall but within 10 tiles is considered on-path; the divergence is only caught by the 12s position-stall watchdog. (findClosestPathIndex does use a capped BFS for kickoff selection, cpp:1385-1445, but that reachability awareness is not applied to off-path detection.)

Microbot: isNearPath is BFS-reachability based: on-path means some walkable path point is within recalculateDistance-1 REACHABLE tiles (Rs2Walker.java:6771-6798), with a chebyshev<=3 variance bypass (:6800-6812) — across-the-wall divergence is detected and recalculated immediately.

Why it matters: Wrong-side-of-wall states (after a missed door, bad interpolation click, or sidestep) persist up to 12s before recovery instead of triggering an immediate recalc; at fleet path volumes this adds up and occasionally compounds into the sidestep/give-up escalation.

Verification (high confidence): The gap is real but the claim's mechanism is half-wrong. The off-path distance IS measured against the BFS-reachability-selected waypoint: PathExecutor.cpp:954 calls findClosestPathIndex (canTraverse-gated BFS, cap CLOSEST_INDEX_BFS_MAX_DIST=20, h:496) and cpp:964-967 takes chebyshev to m_path[newIdx] vs OFF_PATH_THRESHOLD=10 (h:276). So reachability awareness IS applied — contrary to the claim's parenthetical. The blindness enters via the fallback: when NO path tile is BFS-reachable within 20 steps (the hard wall-separation case — missed door, fully cut off), findClosestPathIndex falls back to pure Chebyshev argmin (cpp:1442-1444, findClosestPathIndexChebyshev cpp:1375-1383), which returns the geometrically-near-but-unreachable tile; its distance is <=10, so the off-path check passes and the divergence is masked — exactly the claimed wrong-side-of-wall blind spot. Recovery then waits for the 12s position-stall watchdog (STALL_THRESHOLD_MS h:252, scaled up to 2.0x in combat / 1.75x interim-minimap h:262-263); the interim no-progress drop at 2.5s (h:328, cpp:1539-1540) only re-picks a click on the same stale path, it does not recalc. Two further semantic differences vs Microbot: (1) SafeRS's off-path recalc only fires after the player has been STATIONARY >=2000ms (OFF_PATH_TOLERANCE_MS gate, cpp:968-970, h:282) — a still-moving wall-separated player never triggers it; Microbot's isNearPath is the inverse, short-circuiting TRUE when position is unchanged (Rs2Walker.java:6781) and detecting divergence while moving. (2) When a path tile IS reachable within 20 BFS steps at chebyshev <=10, SafeRS stays on-path even if the walking distance is 10-20 tiles, where Microbot's 9-tile reachable flood (recalculateDistance()-1, default 10, ShortestPathConfig.java:444-446) would recalc — a leniency difference, not blindness. Microbot side verified as claimed: BFS flood Rs2Walker.java:6771-6798, chebyshev<=3 variance bypass :6800-6812 (PATH_VARIANCE_TOLERANCE_CHEBYSHEV=3, :159) — note Microbot itself tolerates wall-separation within 3 chebyshev via that bypass. Severity low is appropriate.

Citations: ours-executor: PathExecutor.h:276; PathExecutor.cpp:964-997, 1385-1445 | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:6771-6798, 6800-6812

docs.title: [low / accuracy] accuracy-permissive-degradation-on-offset-failure
docs.text:
Live collision chain on [UNVERIFIED] offsets degrades to trust-everything with no alarm

Ours: The entire live collision pointer chain (CollisionMap_::* and WorldMap::ScenePtr/RegionBase) is marked [UNVERIFIED] in Offsets.h:848-866. On failure m_valid=false and every provider query returns permissive defaults — isTileReachable returns true when collision is invalid or the target is out of scene (PathExecutor.cpp:1624, 1630-1636) — silently flipping every reachability gate, wall-adjust probe, and direct-short-walk check to 'allow' after any game update that shifts these offsets, with no detection or alert.

Microbot: No offset dependency for collision: data comes from the RuneLite client API, so a client update breaks loudly (compile/API errors) rather than silently returning permissive garbage.

Why it matters: OSRS updates land roughly biweekly. The failure mode is not a crash but a fleet-wide silent accuracy regression — every walker clicking through walls and doors — that only manifests as diffuse stall/ban-risk symptoms until someone notices the offsets moved.

Verification (high confidence): Core claim holds on current (uncommitted, 2026-06-10) code, with two corrections. (1) "No detection or alert" is slightly overstated: CollisionMap::update() (E:\SafeRS\OSRSClient\GameSDK\CollisionMap.cpp:21-144) emits a ONE-SHOT printf on pointer-chain failure (static logged flag, reset only after a successful rebuild at line 162); but it is stdout-only (not OSRS_LOG/UI/telemetry), its return value is ignored at dllmain.cpp:741, no GUI panel surfaces collision validity, and the worst case — shifted offsets landing on non-null garbage so readBytes succeeds — sets m_valid=true over garbage flags with zero signal at all. (2) "Direct-short-walk check flips to allow" is wrong in the invalid-collision case: the short-walk and local-A* branches are gated on m_collision.isValid() (PathExecutor.cpp:119-131, 146) and are SKIPPED when invalid, falling back to the offset-independent StaticPathfinder (collision-map.bin), so routes still respect static walls. What actually flips permissive on m_valid=false is the per-waypoint live gating: isKnownWalkableOrUnloaded→true (PathExecutor.cpp:1624), isTileReachable→true (1630, and out-of-scene→true 1632-1636), waypoint filters at 1070/1712 pass everything, wall-adjust probe disabled (1648 returns target unadjusted), smoothed-pick reachability degrades to chebyshev-closest (1387), and stall-recovery trySidestep fails closed (1858 returns false). Net effect: silent loss of door/dynamic-obstacle awareness, wall-offset clicking, and sidestep recovery — a real fleet-wide silent accuracy regression — but not literally "every walker clicking through walls" since static collision still constrains planned routes. Note the provider itself fails closed (CollisionMap::isWalkable returns false when invalid, CollisionMap.cpp:174); the permissive flip lives entirely in PathExecutor's wrapper helpers. Offsets confirmed [UNVERIFIED]: E:\SafeRS\OSRSClient\GameSDK\Offsets.h:848-857 (CollisionMap_) and 862-866 (WorldMap::ScenePtr/RegionBaseX/Y); Config/generated_offsets.h:210-230 marks both "NOT recovered this run". Microbot side confirmed: Rs2Walker.java:2089-2090 reads collision via Client.getTopLevelWorldView().getCollisionMaps() (RuneLite API, null-checked, no memory offsets).

Citations: ours-collision: Offsets.h:848-866 | ours-collision: PathExecutor.cpp:1624, 1630-1636 (permissive defaults) | ours-collision: finding 4 (m_valid=false -> trust-everything)

docs.title: [low / accuracy] accuracy-walksmart-double-instance-translation
docs.text:
walkSmart double-runs instance translation; correctness rests on an unverified no-op assumption

Ours: walkSmart translates template->instance coords at Walk.cpp:188, then passes the ALREADY-TRANSLATED coords into fastCanvas, which re-runs maybeTranslateInstanceGoal at Walk.cpp:219. Correctness relies on the second translation failing to resolve instance coords as template chunks and acting as a no-op — explicitly flagged 'unverified' in the report. If any instance coordinate happens to also resolve as a template chunk, the canvas click targets a wrong tile.

Microbot: Instance coordinate conversion happens once at each consumption site (e.g., door logic converts path edge coords per-use, Rs2Walker.java:3531-3548); there is no translate-then-retranslate pattern, and transports are simply suppressed inside instances except POH (:1482-1484) with a dedicated POH start remap (ShortestPathPlugin.java:818-845).

Why it matters: Instances (raids, quest instances, POH) are high-value content where a wrong-tile canvas click can mean a failed mechanic, not just a slow walk. An idempotence assumption that has never been verified is a latent exact-tile correctness bug in precisely the environment with the least recovery margin.

Verification (high confidence): Confirmed in current code (Walk.cpp clean of the 2026-06-10 uncommitted changes, which touch only Pathfinding/). walkSmart translates template->instance at Walk.cpp:188, then the on-canvas branch (Walk.cpp:191-192) passes the already-translated goalX/goalY into fastCanvas, which unconditionally re-runs maybeTranslateInstanceGoal at Walk.cpp:219. InstanceQuery::toLocalInstance (InstanceQuery.cpp:107-134) has no idempotence guard: it chunks the input (x/8, y/8) and scans the 13x13 slot grid for a matching stored template chunk, so if any slot's template chunk numerically collides with the instance-band chunk of the already-translated coords, the second call succeeds and remaps the canvas click to a wrong tile. The guard would be trivial (maybeTranslateInstanceGoal already reads RegionBaseX/Y at Walk.cpp:53-56 and could reject inputs inside the live scene band) but is absent. Notably the off-canvas branch (Walk.cpp:195-199) deliberately passes ORIGINAL template coords to Walk::to to translate exactly once, so the double-run is confined to the on-canvas fastCanvas branch. Scope correction: this applies to the srs::api C++ plugin path only; the Lua-facing game.walkSmart/walkFastCanvas in ScriptEngine/ScriptAPI.cpp:438-482 are a separate parallel implementation that performs NO instance translation at all (a related but distinct gap).

Citations: ours-transports: Walk.cpp:188, 192, 219 (double-translation, unverified no-op) | mb-executor: Rs2Walker.java:3531-3548, 1482-1484 | mb-transports: ShortestPathPlugin.java:818-845

docs.title: [low / accuracy] accuracy-arrival-api-contract-defects
docs.text:
Walk API arrival signalling defects: hasArrived() true when unwired; walkTo already-arrived return contradicts its docs

Ours: hasArrived() returns true when the executor is not wired up (Walk.cpp:248) — a silent false-positive for pre-init hosts (isMoving returns false in the same state, Walk.cpp:242-243, so a poll loop exits 'arrived' immediately). Separately, Walk.h:26-28 documents walkTo returning false for the already-arrived case, but the implementation returns true and sets ARRIVED (PathExecutor.cpp:105-113) — callers using to()==false for error detection mis-handle already-there (header doc text verified in working tree).

Microbot: walkWithState returns an explicit terminal-state enum (ARRIVED / UNREACHABLE / EXIT) that the script harness consumes, with EXIT auto-retried up to 3 times (ShortestPathScript.java:97-173) — arrival semantics are unambiguous and failure modes are distinguishable.

Why it matters: Scripts build movement loops directly on these two calls. A false 'arrived' before initialization or a doc-contradicting return value produces skipped walks and misclassified errors that look like script bugs, eroding trust in the walker across every plugin that ships.

Verification (high confidence): Both defects exist in the current tree, with two nuances. (1) Walk.cpp:246-250: hasArrived() returns true when ctx.pathExecutor is null, and isMoving() (Walk.cpp:240-244) returns false in the same state, so a poll loop on a pre-init host exits 'arrived' immediately. Nuance: this is documented intent (Walk.h:10-11 'no-ops returning false/true depending on intent'), so it is a deliberate API design rather than an accidental bug — but it remains a silent false-positive indistinguishable from real arrival, vs Microbot's explicit WalkerState enum. (2) Walk.h:26-27 documents to() returning false for the already-arrived case, but PathExecutor::walkTo (PathExecutor.cpp:100-113) sets m_state=ARRIVED and returns true at line 112, passed through verbatim by Walk::to (Walk.cpp:82-83) — doc/behavior mismatch confirmed; the implementation semantic (true=goal satisfied) is reasonable, the header doc is what is wrong. Additional related doc bug found: Walk.h:114-116 claims hasArrived 'returns true when no walk has been issued yet', but with a WIRED executor in IDLE it returns false (PathExecutor.cpp:1363-1365: m_state == ARRIVED only) — the doc matches only the unwired branch. Microbot citation accurate: ShortestPathScript.java line 101 walkWithState returns WalkerState; ARRIVED/UNREACHABLE/EXIT terminal handling line 108; EXIT auto-retry up to 3 (lines 29, 139-147).

Citations: ours-transports: Walk.cpp:242-243, 248; Walk.h:26-28 (doc/behavior mismatch) | ours-executor: PathExecutor.cpp:105-113 | mb-transports: ShortestPathScript.java:97-173

docs.title: [low / completeness] completeness-consumable-preference-absent
docs.text:
Consumable column unparsed; no consumable-vs-reusable teleport preference

Ours: The 'Consumable' column present in teleportation_items.tsv is never parsed — no getCol for it exists (ours-transports §2) — so even a future item-teleport implementation cannot distinguish a one-use tab from reusable jewellery, and no similar-transport pruning logic exists.

Microbot: Consumable flag parsed (Transport.java:329-331); TeleportationItem.INVENTORY_NON_CONSUMABLE mode rejects consumables outright (PathfinderConfig.java:1054-1061); filterSimilarTransports prunes consumable teleport items whose destination is within N tiles of a reusable alternative (spell/non-consumable/fairy ring/spirit tree/glider/quetzal), target-aware via centroid (PathfinderConfig.java:1152-1367); plus preferNonConsumableTeleportAndSpells knob for banked routing (ShortestPathConfig.java:731-741).

Why it matters: Burning teleport tabs/scrolls when a reusable alternative lands nearby is a direct GP drain multiplied across a bot farm. Low severity because Microbot's distance filter is default-disabled (maxSimilarTransportDistance=0) and the prerequisite item-teleport support is itself missing — but the data model gap (unparsed column) must be fixed first regardless.

Verification (high confidence): Claim holds against current on-disk code. SafeRS: Transport::fromTsvRow (OSRSClient/Pathfinding/Transport.cpp:71-86) parses 13 columns (Origin, Destination, action, Skills, Item IDs, Currency, Quests, Wilderness level, Varbits, Varplayers, isMembers, Duration, Display info) but has no getCol for "Consumable"; Transport.h has no isConsumable field; repo-wide grep finds no consumable-preference, filterSimilarTransports-equivalent, or similar-transport pruning logic anywhere in OSRSClient. The uncommitted 2026-06-10 changes touch only DaxWalker.cpp/PathExecutor.cpp/.h/Pathfinder.cpp (plus PluginAPI loader/scheduler) — Transport.cpp/h and PathfinderConfig.cpp are unmodified, so the claim is not stale. The prerequisite gap also persists: refreshUsableTeleports (dllmain.cpp:614-669) seeds only TELEPORTATION_SPELL rows (line 624 skips all other types), so TELEPORTATION_ITEM rows load into the registry but are never usable. Minor refinement: parsing is column-name driven (unknown columns dropped silently), so adding Consumable is trivial — but today the data is not captured. Note SafeRS does have a partial banked-routing analogue (considerBankRunes + BankTeleportEdge for spells), yet no consumable-vs-reusable distinction since items aren't routed at all. Microbot side verified exactly as cited: Transport.java:329-331 parses Consumable; PathfinderConfig.java:1054-1061 isTeleportationItemUsable rejects consumables under INVENTORY_NON_CONSUMABLE; filterSimilarTransports at PathfinderConfig.java:1152+ (called at 329-330/436-437, gated on useBankItems && maxSimilarTransportDistance>0, consumable checks at 1192/1273/1397); ShortestPathConfig.java:731-741 preferNonConsumableTeleportAndSpells (default false) and 754-765 maxSimilarTransportDistance (default 0, confirming the default-disabled severity caveat).

Citations: ours-transports §2: Consumable column never parsed | mb-transports §2: Transport.java:329-331; §5: PathfinderConfig.java:1054-1061, 1152-1367, ShortestPathConfig.java:731-741, 754-765

docs.title: [low / completeness] completeness-multi-target-unsupported
docs.text:
Single-goal search only — no multi-target support

Ours: walkTo/findPath accept exactly one goal tile (PathExecutor::beginWalk cascade, PathExecutor.cpp:100-212; StaticPathfinder single packed goal). 'Walk to the nearest of N banks' requires N sequential searches scripted by the caller.

Microbot: Pathfinder takes a Set of targets with an unboxed int[] hotpath copy; first target reached wins, and the nearest-reachable fallback ranks every popped node against every target (Pathfinder.java:44-46, 101-105, 401-423); bidirectional mode simply restricts itself to single-target (:600).

Why it matters: Nearest-bank / nearest-altar / nearest-of-resource-spots is a pervasive scripting pattern; lacking it costs N-1 redundant 5s-budget searches and produces suboptimal choices when the caller guesses the nearest target by straight-line distance.

Verification (high confidence): Claim is accurate except one naming detail: there is no PathExecutor::beginWalk — the single-goal cascade is the body of PathExecutor::walkTo(int goalX, int goalY, ...) (PathExecutor.cpp:65, cascade at :100-212). All four path sources are single-goal: tryDirectShortWalk (:129-144), local Pathfinder::findPath(sx,sy,gx,gy,plane) (Pathfinder.h:59), StaticPathfinder::findPath with one packed goal (StaticPathfinder.h:48-53, goalPacked at StaticPathfinder.cpp:179), and DaxWalker (:189). Public facade srs::api::Walk::to is likewise one tile (Walk.h:32-34); no multi-target symbol exists anywhere in OSRSClient.
