docs.title: Types
docs.text:
GeOfferInfo — one offer slot. Fields are read-only; the is* helpers are callable in both C++ and Lua (offer:isFinished()).

Field Type Meaning slot int32 Slot index 0..7 (−1 if invalid) state GeState Lifecycle (see below) itemId int32 Traded item id (−1 if empty) totalQuantity int32 Offer size quantityDone int32 Bought / sold so far price int32 Price per item on the offer spent int64 gp moved so far

Helpers: isEmpty(), isActive(), isComplete(), isFinished().

GeState (GeState / srs.ge.State.*):

Const Value Meaning Empty 0 Slot unused CancelledBuy 1 Buy aborted CancelledSell 2 Sell aborted Buying 3 Active buy Bought 4 Buy complete Selling 5 Active sell Sold 6 Sell complete

Terminal states are best-effort

Empty / Buying / Selling are read directly from the live offer array. The terminal bytes (Bought / Sold, and the cancelled split) are best-effort decodes — gate on isFinished() / anyFinished() rather than a specific terminal value where you can.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Buy 1000 nature runes at the instant-buy price, then collect when done.
local NATURE = 561
script.onTick(function()
    if not srs.ge.isOpen() then return end          -- open via the clerk first
    if srs.ge.slotOf(NATURE) < 0 and srs.ge.firstEmptySlot() >= 0 then
        srs.ge.buyItem(NATURE, 1000, srs.ge.buyPrice(NATURE))
    elseif srs.ge.anyFinished() then
        srs.ge.collectToInventory()
    end
end)

docs.title: GraphicsObjects
docs.text:
srs::api::GraphicsObjects / srs.graphicsObjects

Read-only enumeration of tile-bound SpotAnims — falling debris during boss fights, acid pools (Vasa, Tekton), blood splatters, spell-impact tile effects, teleport sparkles, run-energy regen sparkles, and so on.

Experimental — offset still being verified

The container offset on WorldInstance isn't fully live-verified yet. The query methods return empty / nil until the offset is pinned for your client build — discover it at runtime with scan() and lock it in with setContainerOffset() (see Offset discovery). Treat every field except id as provisional.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua All live gfx objects GraphicsObjects::all(ctx) → vector<GraphicsObjectEntry> srs.graphicsObjects.all() → table[] Filter by tile window GraphicsObjects::nearby(ctx, cx, cz, plane, radius) → vector<…> srs.graphicsObjects.nearby(cx, cz, plane, radius) → table[] Earliest-started entry GraphicsObjects::next(ctx) → optional<…> srs.graphicsObjects.next() → table \| nil

nearby(cx, cz, plane, radius) returns entries whose tileX/tileZ are within Chebyshev distance radius of (cx, cz) on the given plane.

next() returns the graphics object that will finish (disappear) soonest, or nil when none are active.

docs.title: Offset discovery
docs.text:
Helpers for pinning the container offset on a new client build (see the warning above). Most scripts never need these.

Method C++ Lua Probe candidate offsets GraphicsObjects::scan(ctx, base = 0) → vector<GraphicsObjectScanRow> srs.graphicsObjects.scan(base?) → table[] Pin the container offset GraphicsObjects::setContainerOffset(ctx, offset, base = 0) → bool srs.graphicsObjects.setContainerOffset(offset, base?) → bool Read the current offset GraphicsObjects::containerOffset(ctx) → int64 srs.graphicsObjects.containerOffset() → int Read the current base GraphicsObjects::containerBase(ctx) → int32 srs.graphicsObjects.containerBase() → int

scan walks each WorldInstance (base = 0) or its Scene (base = 1) looking for a list shaped like the gfx-object container, returning one row per candidate. Pick the plausible row and pass its offset / base to setContainerOffset; the choice is session-persistent.

GraphicsObjectScanRow:

Field Type Notes offset int64 Base-relative offset probed base int 0 = WorldInstance, 1 = Scene entriesFound int64 Plausible entries at that offset shapeOk bool Begin/end looked like a sorted-set idsLookValid bool Entries had plausible spotanim ids firstId int A sample id, to recognize the effect

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Each entry (Lua: plain table; C++: GraphicsObjectEntry):

Field Type Notes id int SpotAnim cache id. animationId int The bound animation id (resolved from the spotanim's animation definition). Negative until the engine binds the animation. plane int 0..3 tileX int World tile X. tileZ int World tile Y (Z in our naming). fineX int Engine sub-tile coordinate (localTileX * 128 + 64). fineY int Engine sub-tile coordinate. height int Height value relative to the tile. startCycle int The engine cycle at which this gfx began (or will begin) rendering. The gfx is in a "pending" state until currentCycle >= startCycle, then plays for the duration baked into its animation definition. framesSinceStart int currentFrame - startCycle. Negative while pending, positive while rendering. Not a lifetime countdown — the actual end is determined by the animation's own length. finished bool true once the engine has released the bound animation (the gfx is done playing and will be pruned on the next engine tick).

docs.title: List active gfx near the player
Dodge dangerous tiles
docs.text:
A boss-mechanic dodger. Maintains a set of "lethal" spotanim ids and walks the player off any tile currently flagged as dangerous.

-- Tune for the boss you're fighting.
local DANGEROUS_IDS = { [1448]=true, [1295]=true, [1259]=true }

script.onTick(function()
    -- Build the current dangerous-tile list from live gfx.
    local danger = {}
    for _, g in ipairs(srs.graphicsObjects.all()) do
        if DANGEROUS_IDS[g.id] and not g.finished then
            danger[#danger+1] = { x=g.tileX, y=g.tileZ, plane=g.plane }
        end
    end
    if #danger == 0 then return end

    local p = srs.player.position()
    local onDanger = false
    for _, d in ipairs(danger) do
        if d.plane==p.plane and d.x==p.x and d.y==p.y then
            onDanger = true; break
        end
    end
    if not onDanger then return end

    -- Find the closest walkable safe tile and walk there.
    local safe = game.findSafeTile(p.x, p.y, danger, 5)
    if safe then
        game.walkSmart(safe.x, safe.y, safe.plane)
        log.info(string.format("Dodging to (%d, %d)", safe.x, safe.y))
    end
end)

See Walk for findSafeTile / walkSmart / walkFastCanvas documentation. Note game.findSafeTile (used above) is the Lua-side implementation on the global game table; the C++ facade counterpart is Walk::findSafeTile.

docs.title: React to a specific cast
docs.text:
Wait until a particular spotanim id appears and react once it's been rendering for a few frames.

local TARGET_ID = 1042   -- replace with the id you care about

script.onTick(function()
    for _, g in ipairs(srs.graphicsObjects.all()) do
        if g.id == TARGET_ID and g.framesSinceStart >= 0 and not g.finished then
            -- gfx is currently rendering — react now
            log.info(string.format("Target gfx active at (%d, %d)", g.tileX, g.tileZ))
            return
        end
    end
end)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• framesSinceStart is NOT a "time until removal" countdown. The engine prunes the gfx based on the animation's natural length, not from a counter on the gfx-object itself. Use finished to detect end-of-life.
  • fineX/fineY vs tileX/tileZ. Both are exposed for convenience. tileX/tileZ give world tile coordinates; fineX/fineY give the engine's sub-tile units (tile * 128 + 64). For tile-equality comparisons against Player.position(), use tileX/tileZ.
  • Pending gfx. When a spotanim has a start-delay in its packet (chained / sequenced effects), it appears in the list with framesSinceStart < 0 before it actually starts rendering. Filter on framesSinceStart >= 0 if you only care about currently-visible effects.

docs.title: Example
Input
docs.text:
srs.input (Lua only)

Low-level keyboard primitives. Used for camera-rotation calibration (measuring how long an arrow-key hold takes to rotate N yaw units) and antiban scenarios that need hand-rolled key timing rather than the all-in-one srs.camera.keyboardRotateTo* helpers.

There is no public C++ header for this surface — plugins use InputManager directly.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Lua What it does Tap a key (WndProc) srs.input.keyTap(vk, holdMs) Press now, schedule release in holdMs Tap a key (deprecated alias) srs.input.osKeyTap(vk, holdMs) Forwards to keyTap — same WndProc path Any release scheduled? srs.input.isKeyPending() → bool True if a previous tap hasn't released yet

docs.title: keyTap vs osKeyTap
docs.text:
There is now one path: all scripted input goes through WndProc (CallWindowProcW), which is per-window and so works in the background and across multiple clients. osKeyTap is a deprecated alias that forwards to keyTap — it no longer uses SendInput and has no foreground requirement. Prefer keyTap; osKeyTap is kept only so older ported scripts keep compiling.

keyTap release fires from InputManager::update() which runs every rendered frame (~16 ms granularity, driven by PathExecutor::onFrame in dllmain). holdMs < 0 is clamped to 0.

docs.title: VK constants
docs.text:
srs.input.VK.*:

Name Value VK LEFT 0x25 VK_LEFT UP 0x26 VK_UP RIGHT 0x27 VK_RIGHT DOWN 0x28 VK_DOWN SPACE 0x20 VK_SPACE ENTER 0x0D VK_RETURN

For other keys pass the raw VK integer (see Microsoft's Virtual-Key Codes).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Calibrate yaw-rotation rate: hold left arrow for 1s, measure delta
local y0 = srs.camera.getYaw()
srs.input.keyTap(srs.input.VK.LEFT, 1000)
script.nextTick(function()
    local y1 = srs.camera.getYaw()
    log.info(("Δyaw over 1s = %d units"):format((y1 - y0) % 2048))
end)

docs.text:
srs::api::Inventory / srs.inventory

Read-only view of the player's backpack (28 slots) plus item-action helpers. Action calls route through Interact (always-on spoof + DoAction).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Snapshot all slots Inventory::all(ctx) → vector<InventoryItem> srs.inventory.all() → table One slot (0..27) Inventory::at(ctx, slot) → optional<InventoryItem> srs.inventory.at(slot) → InventoryItem \| nil Contains by id Inventory::contains(ctx, id) → bool srs.inventory.contains(id) → bool Contains by name Inventory::contains(ctx, name) → bool srs.inventory.contains(name) → bool Count by id Inventory::count(ctx, id) → int32 srs.inventory.count(id) → int Count by name Inventory::count(ctx, name) → int32 srs.inventory.count(name) → int First slot by id Inventory::firstSlot(ctx, id) → int32 srs.inventory.firstSlot(id) → int First slot by name Inventory::firstSlot(ctx, name) → int32 srs.inventory.firstSlot(name) → int Empty slots count Inventory::emptySlots(ctx) → int32 srs.inventory.emptySlots() → int Full Inventory::isFull(ctx) → bool srs.inventory.isFull() → bool Empty Inventory::isEmpty(ctx) → bool srs.inventory.isEmpty() → bool

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Click action on slot Inventory::interact(ctx, slot, action) → bool srs.inventory.interact(slot, action) → bool Click by id Inventory::interactById(ctx, id, action) → bool srs.inventory.interactById(id, action) → bool Click by name Inventory::interactByName(ctx, name, action) → bool srs.inventory.interactByName(name, action) → bool Click lowest dose of a potion family Inventory::interactByLowestDose(ctx, baseName, action) → bool srs.inventory.interactByLowestDose(baseName, action) → bool Examine slot's item Inventory::examine(ctx, slot) → bool srs.inventory.examine(slot) → bool Drop all by id Inventory::dropAll(ctx, id) → int32 srs.inventory.dropAll(id) → int Drop all by name Inventory::dropAll(ctx, name) → int32 srs.inventory.dropAll(name) → int Drops still queued Inventory::pendingDropCount(ctx) → int32 srs.inventory.pendingDropCount() → int Empty coal bag Inventory::emptyCoalBag(ctx) → bool srs.inventory.emptyCoalBag() → bool

action is the exact menu-option string (e.g. "Eat", "Drop", "Wield", "Bury", "Drink", "Use"). Returns false on any of: slot out of range, slot empty, action not in the opcode table, slot widget not currently rendered, or spoofer failure.

interactByLowestDose targets the lowest dose of a potion family — interactByLowestDose(ctx, "Prayer potion", "Drink") drinks a (1) before a fresh (4) to free inventory slots sooner (the trailing (N) is stripped from baseName).

examine fires the item's right-click Examine and the engine prints the description to chat (info-only, no server cost).

emptyCoalBag empties a coal bag via the captured CC_OP_LOW_PRIORITY op on the main inventory (149, 0). Returns false if no coal bag is held. The fill half lives on the bank facade — Bank::fillCoalBag (bank must be open).

dropAll is asynchronous — poll pendingDropCount

dropAll returns the number of drops it queued and schedules them with human-like spacing (~50–200 ms apart plus a slot-distance term), so a full 28-slot drop plays out over several seconds. Do not call dropAll again each tick to "keep dropping" — that re-queues the whole set. Fire it once, then treat the drop as finished when pendingDropCount() returns 0.

docs.title: Use item on…
docs.text:
Stage an inventory item, then apply it to a target (the Microbot Rs2Inventory.useItemOn* mirror). Each takes either ids or a (srcSlot, entry) overload where entry is the finder result from the matching module.

Method C++ Lua …on object Inventory::useItemOnObject(ctx, itemId, objectId) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnObject(itemId, objectId) → bool …on object (slot + entry) Inventory::useItemOnObject(ctx, srcSlot, GameObjectEntry) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnObject(srcSlot, entry) → bool …on item Inventory::useItemOnItem(ctx, srcItemId, dstItemId) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnItem(srcId, dstId) → bool …on item, burst mode Inventory::useItemOnItemBatch(ctx, srcItemId, dstItemId, count) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnItemBatch(srcId, dstId, count) → bool …on NPC Inventory::useItemOnNpc(ctx, itemId, npcId) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnNpc(itemId, npcId) → bool …on NPC (slot + target) Inventory::useItemOnNpc(ctx, srcSlot, ActionTarget) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnNpc(srcSlot, target) → bool …on ground item Inventory::useItemOnGroundItem(ctx, itemId, groundItemId) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnGroundItem(itemId, groundItemId) → bool …on ground item (slot + entry) Inventory::useItemOnGroundItem(ctx, srcSlot, GroundItemEntry) → bool srs.inventory.useItemOnGroundItem(srcSlot, entry) → bool

useItemOnItem picks the first inventory slot holding each id (returns false if both resolve to the same slot). useItemOnItemBatch repeats the item-on-item up to count ∈ [1, 8] times for fast-fletching-style bursts.

Not yet wired — useItemOnNpc / useItemOnGroundItem are skeletons

All four overloads (id-pair and slot+target forms, C++ and Lua alike) are skeletons — they log and return false pending a captured wire format. useItemOnObject and useItemOnItem are live.

docs.title: Example
Magic
docs.text:
srs::api::Magic / srs.magic

Cast spells using the Spells metadata table. Widget child IDs come from RuneLite gameval/InterfaceID MagicSpellbook (group 218).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Available rune count Magic::runeCount(ctx, runeItemId, src = {}) → int32 srs.magic.runeCount(runeItemId) → int Can cast (level + rune availability) Magic::canCast(ctx, s, src = {}) → bool srs.magic.canCast(s) → bool Cast (no-target / self) Magic::cast(ctx, s) → bool srs.magic.cast(s) → bool Two-click cast on inv slot Magic::castOnInventory(ctx, s, slot) → bool srs.magic.castOnInventory(s, slot) → bool High alch convenience Magic::highAlch(ctx, slot) → bool srs.magic.highAlch(slot) → bool Low alch convenience Magic::lowAlch(ctx, slot) → bool srs.magic.lowAlch(slot) → bool

canCast checks the Magic level plus every per-rune cost; runeCount totals the copies of one rune id across the requested sources. Both count inventory + rune pouch by default (RuneSource defaults). Bank counting (RuneSource.bank, C++ only) is only meaningful while the bank is open / cached. Elemental-staff substitution is still TODO. The Lua bindings don't expose RuneSource and always use the defaults.

cast fires the spell click — works for self-target / no-target spells (teleports, alchemy on self, etc.). It does not pre-select for use-on.

castOnInventory is two-step: click spell, then click the inventory slot. Use for High Alchemy, Bones to Bananas, Superheat, and similar item-target spells.

Returns false if the spellbook tab isn't visible or the spell's metadata is unpopulated (a kTODO entry in Spells.cpp).

Selects where canCast / runeCount look for runes. bank = true is only meaningful while the bank is open / cached.

Known gaps

No castOnNpc and no autocast control yet — srs.magic covers self-target and inventory-item-target casts only.

docs.title: Example
MenuEntry
docs.text:
srs::api::MenuEntry / srs.menuEntry

Typed fluent builder over Interact::doActionRaw. Goes through the same spoof-then-DoAction path as every other facade — fail-closed if the spoofer can't inject.

Use this when you need raw control over MenuAction params (e.g. while RE'ing a new interaction type) without bypassing the input simulation contract.

Equivalent to Microbot's NewMenuEntry, minus the option/target text fields (those route through Interact::perform's higher-level path; this builder targets the raw MenuAction dispatch path).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
C++Lua 
using srs::api::MenuEntry;
MenuEntry()
    .worldX(10).worldY(20)
    .opcode(/*CC_OP*/ 57)
    .screen(450, 300)
    .fire(ctx);

local e = srs.menuEntry.new()
e:worldX(10):worldY(20)
 :opcode(srs.menuEntry.CC_OP)
 :screen(450, 300)
 :fire()

docs.text: Setter C++ signature Lua signature worldX(v) MenuEntry& worldX(int32) entry:worldX(v) → entry worldY(v) MenuEntry& worldY(int32) entry:worldY(v) → entry widget(g, c) MenuEntry& widget(int32, int32) entry:widget(g, c) → entry opcode(op) MenuEntry& opcode(int32) entry:opcode(op) → entry spawnIndex(v) MenuEntry& spawnIndex(int32) entry:spawnIndex(v) → entry subject(v) MenuEntry& subject(uint32) entry:subject(v) → entry screen(x, y) MenuEntry& screen(int32, int32) entry:screen(x, y) → entry fire() bool fire(ctx) entry:fire() → bool

docs.title: Field semantics
docs.text:
• worldX / worldY — primary param pair. For tile actions these are world tile coords; for inventory / widget actions, worldX is the slot/sub-id and worldY is the encoded widget id.
  • widget(g, c) — convenience that encodes (groupId, childId) into worldY = (group << 16) | child.
  • screen(x, y) — required. Pixel coords of the click target. The spoofer needs these to draw a plausible mouse trail. Sentinel (0, 0) causes the spoofer to skip and fail-closed.

docs.title: NPC
docs.text:
srs::api::Npc / srs.npc

Find NPCs in the scene and act on them. The srs.npc table carries both the finders (which NPCs are nearby) and the actions (attack, talk-to, …) so scripts can stay in one table.

A target is identified by its spawn index + world coords. In C++ the finders return NpcEntry (the recommended form for new plugin code); in Lua they return the ActionTarget usertype. The action methods accept either, so srs.npc.attack(npc) / npc:attack() work on whatever a finder handed you.

All interact / attack / talkTo / bank / examine calls route through Interact, which always spoofs mouse motion + click before DoAction (no escape hatch).

docs.title: Finding NPCs
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua All NPCs in scene Npc::all(ctx) → vector<NpcEntry> srs.npc.all() → table By id Npc::byId(ctx, npcId) → vector<NpcEntry> srs.npc.byId(id) → table By name Npc::byName(ctx, name) → vector<NpcEntry> srs.npc.byName(name) → table Nearest (any) Npc::nearest(ctx) → optional<NpcEntry> srs.npc.nearest() → ActionTarget \| nil Nearest by id Npc::nearestById(ctx, npcId) → optional<NpcEntry> srs.npc.nearestById(id) → ActionTarget \| nil Nearest by name Npc::nearestByName(ctx, name) → optional<NpcEntry> srs.npc.nearestByName(name) → ActionTarget \| nil

byName / nearestByName normalize the name internally (case- and whitespace-insensitive), so pass the in-game name as shown ("Banker", "Grand Exchange Clerk"). The srs.npc finders are the recommended going-forward form.

Three equivalent finder surfaces

Lua exposes the same finders three times — all hit the same EntityQuery backend, so pick whichever reads best and don't mix them for "different" results:

Global npc.* srs.npc.* entity.* npc.all() srs.npc.all() entity.npcs() npc.byId(id) srs.npc.byId(id) entity.npcById(id) npc.byName(name) srs.npc.byName(name) entity.npcByName(name) npc.nearest() srs.npc.nearest() entity.nearestNpc() npc.nearestById(id) srs.npc.nearestById(id) — npc.nearestByName(name) srs.npc.nearestByName(name) —

All return ActionTarget (lists or single-or-nil). The global npc table is a plain alias kept for source compatibility.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Generic interact Npc::interact(ctx, target, action) → bool srs.npc.interact(target, action) → bool Attack Npc::attack(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.attack(target) → bool Talk-to Npc::talkTo(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.talkTo(target) → bool Bank (banker NPCs) Npc::bank(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.bank(target) → bool Examine Npc::examine(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.examine(target) → bool Still in world map Npc::isAlive(ctx, target) → bool srs.npc.isAlive(target) → bool Overhead prayer headicon Npc::overheadPrayer(ctx, target) → OverheadPrayer srs.npc.overheadPrayer(target) → OverheadPrayer

action is the exact menu-option string the game shows ("Attack", "Talk-to", "Bank", "Pickpocket", "Trade", "Steal-from", …). examine fires the right-click Examine and the engine prints the NPC's description to chat.

overheadPrayer reads the NPC's protection-prayer headicon (live override when set, else the NpcType definition). Returns OverheadPrayer.None when the NPC shows no prayer icon or has despawned; only prayer-archive (440) icons are reported. The C++ side takes an NpcEntry (a legacy ActionTarget overload also exists). See Prayer for the OverheadPrayer enum values — it's a Lua global enum, not under srs.npc.

isAlive semantics

isAlive is a host-side check that the NPC's NpcInstance is still present in the world hash map. After an NPC dies it lingers a few ticks playing the death animation, then despawns — once that happens isAlive returns false. Currently does not treat HP-0-but-still-rendering as "dead"; callers that need that (loot timing, drop tracking) should poll currentHp via the NPCs panel column or entity.npcById(...).

docs.title: ActionTarget method-call shortcuts (Lua)
docs.text:
The ActionTarget usertype exposes the same set as methods:

local npc = entity.nearestNpc()
if npc and npc:isAlive() then
    npc:attack()         -- == srs.npc.attack(npc)
    npc:talkTo()
    npc:bank()
    npc:interact("Pickpocket")
    npc:overheadPrayer() -- == srs.npc.overheadPrayer(npc)
end

examine has no usertype shortcut

examine is the one action not exposed as an ActionTarget method — there is no npc:examine(). Call srs.npc.examine(npc).

docs.title: Target fields
docs.text:
In Lua, finders return the ActionTarget usertype. In C++, finders return NpcEntry — a plain struct with NPC-specific fields: id, spawnIndex, name, tileX, tileY, plane, animationId (−1 = idle), orientation (−1 = unknown), currentHp / maxHp (−1 = unknown), combatLevel (−1 = unknown), modelMagnitude (engine getXYZMag half-extent; 0 = unknown). The action methods accept either type.

The ActionTarget usertype (Lua return) — read-only:

Field Notes kind TargetKind enum (None / Npc / Player / Object / Tile) tileX, tileY, tileZ World tile coords plane 0..3 spawnIndex Server-assigned spawn index entityId Item/Loc/Npc id depending on kind name Display name currentHp, maxHp Live HP (−1 = unknown; boss HP scaling is approximate) interactTarget Server-side target index (-1 = none) animationId Active anim id modelMagnitude Engine getXYZMag half-extent (0 = unknown) orientation Facing angle 0–2047 (0 = N, 512 = E, 1024 = S, 1536 = W); −1 = unknown combatLevel Combat level (−1 = unknown) isValid() Method, returns bool

orientation / combatLevel population status

The two fields exist on every ActionTarget, but today only the player producer fills them — NPC targets read -1 for both until the NPC-side producer is wired up. C++ NpcEntry carries the real NPC values already.

docs.title: Example
Object
docs.text:
object.* (Lua only — global table)

Live query over scene objects (trees, doors, banks, stairs, etc. — "Locs" in OSRS terminology). Distinct from entity (NPCs / players) and grounditem (lootable items on the floor).

There is no public C++ header — plugins go through ObjectQuery directly.

Global table

Lives at Lua global scope, not under srs.* — object.nearest(), not srs.object.nearest(). Kept this way for source-compat.

See also

For interaction prefer the higher-level srs.gameobject facade, which returns lighter GameObjectEntry tables and ships a built-in interact() helper.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Lua Returns Every loc, every plane object.all() ActionTarget[] By LocType id object.byId(id) ActionTarget[] By name object.byName(name) ActionTarget[] Closest loc (Chebyshev) object.nearest() ActionTarget \| nil Closest matching name object.nearestByName(name) ActionTarget \| nil LocType cache lookup object.lookup(id) → LocTypeData always returns; check .valid

object.all() is heavy — tens of thousands of rows in a typical city. Prefer byId / byName / nearest*, or filter yourself.

Name lookups are case- and whitespace-insensitive ("Bank booth", "bankbooth", "BANK_BOOTH" all match the same target). See IdLookup::normalize for exact normalization rules.

docs.title: LocTypeData
docs.text:
Returned by object.lookup(id). Read-only.

Field Type Notes valid bool False on cache miss (decoder hasn't touched this id) active bool True if the LocType declares any menu options name string In-game display name address int (raw ptr) Internal LocType* — for RE / debug only

A valid=false result usually means the id has never been on screen yet — pan the camera onto an instance and try again.

docs.title: ActionTarget
docs.text: See Entity for the full field/method list. For locs, kind == 3 (TargetKind::Object) and entityId is the LocType id.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- Chop the nearest tree
local tree = object.nearestByName("Tree")
if tree then tree:interact("Chop down") end

-- Find every bank booth in the loaded scene
for _, booth in ipairs(object.byName("Bank booth")) do
    log.info(("booth at %d, %d"):format(booth.tileX, booth.tileY))
end

-- Look up a LocType by id
local loc = object.lookup(10355)
if loc.valid then
    log.info(("LocType #10355 = '%s' (active=%s)"):format(
        loc.name, tostring(loc.active)))
end

docs.title: Overlay
docs.text:
srs::api::Overlay / srs.overlay

Themed HUD kit layered on Drawing: dark-glass panels, per-skill accent colors, tinted icons, XP rows, animated bars, and level rings. Every call is valid only inside IScript::onDraw / script.draw(fn) — the host drives the frame clock and fonts.

onDraw-only

Calling any srs.overlay.* function outside a script.draw(fn) callback (or IScript::onDraw for C++ plugins) is undefined — there is no live ImGui frame. The host calls installFonts / newFrame / clearIconCache itself; scripts never need to.

  • begin_panel / end_panel and begin_card / end_card must always pair — call the end_* regardless of the begin_* return value (same contract as ImGui windows).
  • set_custom sets the accent (and optional icon) used by Skill.Custom; it persists until changed.
  • runtime returns "HH:MM:SS"; pass seconds < 0 to use the internal session accumulator. In C++ the returned pointer is only valid until the next call.
  • short humanizes numbers (8420000 → "8.42M", 1438 → "1,438"). short is a fine Lua table key, but some editors/linters prefer the srs.overlay["short"] spelling.
  • bar / chip / ring percentages are in [0, 1]. stat_row auto-dims / and · characters in the value string.
  • gap(px) with px < 0 inserts the standard section gap.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Overlay::Skill (srs.overlay.Skill.*) — 18 accent identities:

Fishing, Hunter, Cooking, Woodcutting, Mining, Agility, Thieving, Slayer, Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, Magic, Prayer, Crafting, GP, Custom

Not the global Skill enum

srs.overlay.Skill (18 HUD accent identities, nested Overlay::Skill) is a different enum from the global Skill (24 game skills, see Player). The values do not line up — never pass one where the other is expected.

Overlay::Icon (srs.overlay.Icon.*) — 24 glyphs:

fish, sword, skull, axe, tree, pickaxe, footprints, mask, paw, pot, flame, heart, gem, coins, backpack, clock, timer, target, trending, bolt, arrow, bank, vial, Default

Mixed-case Icon keys

The Lua Icon table keys are lowercase for the glyphs (srs.overlay.Icon.fish) but capitalized for Default (srs.overlay.Icon.Default). Default means "use the accent skill's default icon". C++ enumerators are all capitalized (Icon::Fish, …, Icon::Default).

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Overlay::XpBlock (C++; Lua passes a plain table to xp_row):

struct XpBlock {
    Skill skill = Skill::Custom;
    const char* name = nullptr;  // nullptr = use the skill's name
    long long gained = 0;
    long long rate = 0;          // per-hour
    int levelFrom = 0;
    int levelTo = 0;
    float pct = 0.0f;            // progress to next level [0,1]
};

The Lua table keys differ for two fields: level_from / level_to (snake_case), plus skill, name, gained, rate, pct.

docs.title: Example
Player
docs.text:
srs::api::Player / srs.player

Local-player state. Thin wrappers over GameData getters. Each helper returns a sensible fallback (empty string / -1 / 0) instead of optional so Lua callers don't have to deal with a multi-return shape.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method C++ Lua World-tile position Player::position(ctx) → WorldTile srs.player.position() → WorldTile Template-space position Player::templatePosition(ctx) → WorldTile srs.player.templatePosition() → WorldTile Display name Player::displayName(ctx) → string srs.player.displayName() → string Active animation id Player::animation(ctx) → int32 srs.player.animation() → int Carried weight (kg) Player::weight(ctx) → int32 srs.player.weight() → int Run energy Player::runEnergy(ctx) → int32 srs.player.runEnergy() → int Toggle run Player::toggleRunEnergy(ctx, on) → bool srs.player.toggleRunEnergy(on) → bool Idle ticks counter Player::idleTicks(ctx) → int32 srs.player.idleTicks() → int Boosted skill level Player::skillLevel(ctx, Skill) → int32 srs.player.skillLevel(Skill) → int Base skill level Player::skillBase(ctx, Skill) → int32 srs.player.skillBase(Skill) → int Skill XP Player::skillXp(ctx, Skill) → int32 srs.player.skillXp(Skill) → int Current hitpoints Player::hitpoints(ctx) → int32 srs.player.hitpoints() → int Max hitpoints Player::maxHitpoints(ctx) → int32 srs.player.maxHitpoints() → int Current prayer points Player::prayer(ctx) → int32 srs.player.prayer() → int Prayer level (base) Player::maxPrayer(ctx) → int32 srs.player.maxPrayer() → int Overhead prayer headicon Player::overheadPrayer(ctx) → OverheadPrayer srs.player.overheadPrayer() → OverheadPrayer Quest completion state Player::questState(ctx, Quest) → QuestState srs.player.questState(Quest) → QuestState Quest raw progress Player::questProgress(ctx, Quest) → int32 srs.player.questProgress(Quest) → int

docs.title: Detail
docs.text:
• position — returns {0, 0, 0} when GS or the player struct isn't resolved (pre-login). Callers that care about the difference should check World::getId(ctx) >= 0 first. Inside an instance this is the raw instance-local tile.
  • templatePosition — same as position outside an instance; inside an instance it maps the raw instance-local tile back through the engine's chunk layout to the template world tile (the wiki / RuneLite / Microbot coordinate), falling back to position when the conversion can't be made. Pairs with srs.area.isInInstance() to decide raw-vs-template coordinates in instanced content.
  • displayName — empty string pre-login. Resolved via WI-map (GS+0xCA40 → WorldInstance → PlayerSubMap.find(LocalPlayerIndex)) in patch 238+.
  • animation — current animation id from the active AnimSlot. -1 = idle.
  • weight — reads VarPlayer 169.
  • runEnergy — in 0..10000 range (raw network units; divide by 100 for the displayed percentage). -1 if GS isn't resolved.
  • idleTicks — number of consecutive game ticks the player's active animation has been -1. Reset to 0 the moment any non-idle animation plays. Maintained by GameData::onTick.
  • skillLevel / skillBase / skillXp — read the boosted level, base level, or total XP for any skill. Returns 0 when GS isn't resolved.
  • hitpoints / maxHitpoints — shorthand for skillLevel(Skill::Hitpoints) / skillBase(Skill::Hitpoints).
  • prayer / maxPrayer — current prayer points (live, drains with use) + base prayer level. Mirrors srs::api::Prayer::points / Prayer::level.
  • overheadPrayer — the local player's active Protect-from headicon. OverheadPrayer.None when no overhead prayer is active or pre-login. See Prayer for the OverheadPrayer enum (a Lua global enum — same values for players and NPCs; NPCs read it via Npc::overheadPrayer).
  • questState — completion bucket for a quest (NotStarted / InProgress / Finished). Backed by the engine's QUEST_STATUS_GET clientscript (CS2 4029) — the same source RuneLite/Microbot use — so it is correct for every quest with no hand-maintained thresholds. The script must run on the engine thread while scripts run on the render thread, so the value is cached and refreshed asynchronously on the engine thread (EngineDispatch's non-click work lane, drained on every outbound packet): the first lookup of a given quest returns QuestState::Unknown and kicks off a refresh that lands within a tick or two on its own — no click needed, then stays live. Poll until != Unknown, or just read it each tick. Subsequent reads are instant.
  • questProgress — the raw varbit/varp that increments as a quest advances (RuneLite QuestVarbits / QuestVarPlayer) — i.e. the step number a questing script wants. Thread-safe and instant (a plain var read, no clientscript). 0 before the quest is started; quest-specific value as it advances; -1 for the handful of quests with no single tracked progress var, or when VarpSystem isn't ready. Use questState for completion; use this for "which step am I on".

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
WorldTile (read-only):

Field Type x int32 y int32 plane int32

No Lua constructor

WorldTile is a read-only usertype with no Lua constructor — scripts obtain one from srs.player.position() (or another API that returns tiles). Every Lua API that takes a tile also offers (x, y[, plane]) overloads (e.g. srs.camera.rotateToTile(x, y)), so you never need to build one.

Skill enum — values match the engine's skill table:

Attack, Defence, Strength, Hitpoints, Ranged, Prayer, Magic, Cooking, Woodcutting, Fletching, Fishing, Firemaking, Crafting, Smithing, Mining, Herblore, Agility, Thieving, Slayer, Farming, Runecraft, Hunter, Construction, Sailing.

In Lua: Skill.Hitpoints, etc. (registered at Lua global scope, same as CameraMode).

Quest enum — every quest the engine tracks (209 generated enumerators, identical in C++ and Lua), value = stable index. Names + the underlying quest-config struct ids are ported from RuneLite's Quest enum (via Microbot's bundled Quest Helper). Examples: Quest.CooksAssistant, Quest.DragonSlayerI, Quest.MonkeyMadnessIi, Quest.RecipeForDisaster, Quest.DesertTreasureIiTheFallenEmpire. Registered at Lua global scope (same as Skill). Regenerate after a game update with tools/gen_quest_sources.py (sourced from tools/quest_table.txt).

QuestState enum:

Value Meaning Unknown Not cached yet — questState hasn't primed for this quest. Sentinel; never returned by the engine NotStarted Quest not begun InProgress Quest started, not finished Finished Quest complete

In Lua: QuestState.Finished, etc. (registered at Lua global scope).

docs.title: Example
Prayer
docs.text:
srs::api::Prayer / srs.prayer

Toggle prayers and read state. Backed by the prayer book widget (group 541) for clicks and per-prayer activation varbits for reads.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Remaining prayer points Prayer::points(ctx) → int32 srs.prayer.points() → int Base prayer level Prayer::level(ctx) → int32 srs.prayer.level() → int Per-prayer active state Prayer::isActive(ctx, kind) → bool srs.prayer.isActive(kind) → bool Toggle prayer Prayer::toggle(ctx, kind) → bool srs.prayer.toggle(kind) → bool Ensure desired state Prayer::setActive(ctx, kind, on) → bool srs.prayer.setActive(kind, on) → bool
  • points and level pass through to existing GameData accessors so plugins don't need to import GameData.
  • isActive returns false for prayers whose varbit isn't yet mapped or when VarpSystem is unavailable.
  • toggle clicks the prayer button to flip its state. Caller's responsibility to have the prayer tab open and sufficient prayer points — the API doesn't gate.
  • setActive clicks only if currently mismatched.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
PrayerKind constants (PrayerKind / srs.prayer.*):

Lua const Prayer PROTECT_MAGIC Protect from Magic PROTECT_MISSILE Protect from Missiles PROTECT_MELEE Protect from Melee PROTECT_ITEM Protect Item RETRIBUTION Retribution REDEMPTION Redemption SMITE Smite

Subset of full prayer book

Only prayers with confirmed RuneLite varbit IDs are exposed by name. The other ~25 prayers exist server-side and are tracked by the bitfield mirror at varbit 4101 (not decoded here). Add named entries as per-prayer varbits get verified.

docs.title: Overhead prayers (headicons)
docs.text:
srs::api::OverheadPrayer / Lua global OverheadPrayer

The overhead protection-prayer headicon shown above an actor. In C++ this is a pure enum header (OverheadPrayer.h — no class, no export):

enum class OverheadPrayer : int32_t {
    None = -1, Melee = 0, Missiles = 1, Magic = 2,
    Retribution = 3, Smite = 4, Redemption = 5
};

In Lua the enum is registered at global scope — write OverheadPrayer.Missiles, not srs.prayer.OverheadPrayer (no such path exists).

Value Name Meaning -1 None No headicon 0 Melee Protect from Melee 1 Missiles Protect from Missiles 2 Magic Protect from Magic 3 Retribution Retribution 4 Smite Smite 5 Redemption Redemption

The numeric values are the engine's headicon prayer index, and they're identical for players and NPCs.

Readers that return this enum:

  • Local player: Player::overheadPrayer(ctx) / srs.player.overheadPrayer() — see Player
  • NPCs: Npc::overheadPrayer(ctx, target) / srs.npc.overheadPrayer(target) — see NPC
  • Entity handle: target:overheadPrayer() on ActionTarget — see Entity

Note these read the headicon, not the client's prayer-book state — isActive above is the local prayer-book read, overheadPrayer is what's actually displayed over a head (yours or an NPC's).

docs.title: Example
Projectiles
docs.text:
srs::api::Projectiles / srs.projectiles

Read-only enumeration of in-flight projectiles. The common case is "what's about to hit me and when" — use incoming() for that.

Cache ids

id is this client's spotanim/graphic cache id (cache group 0xD in the OSRS-OS3303-BWXF build). It does not directly equal RuneLite's ProjectileID enum — different cache revisions diverge by varying amounts. If you need RuneLite-style labels, build a per-build mapping table.

Time units

ticksUntilLanding is in game ticks (600 ms each, rounded up from the underlying ~30-frame-per-tick counter at GS+0x2154).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Any incoming projectile (cheap) Projectiles::isUnderFire(ctx) → bool srs.projectiles.isUnderFire() → bool Incoming list Projectiles::incoming(ctx) → vector<ProjectileEntry> srs.projectiles.incoming() → table Next-to-land Projectiles::next(ctx) → optional<ProjectileEntry> srs.projectiles.next() → table \| nil Ticks until next Projectiles::ticksUntilNext(ctx) → int32 srs.projectiles.ticksUntilNext() → int All projectiles scene-wide (heavier) Projectiles::all(ctx) → vector<ProjectileEntry> srs.projectiles.all() → table
  • isUnderFire is allocation-free — preferred for tight check-loops.
  • next is the lowest absoluteEndCycle.
  • ticksUntilNext returns -1 when nothing is in flight (single int compare instead of optional unwrap, for ranged-prayer flick logic).
  • all is heavier than incoming — walks the WI hashmap.

docs.title: Spawn events
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Subscribe to projectile spawns Projectiles::onSpawned(cb) → uint64 srs.projectiles.onSpawned(fn) → token Unsubscribe Projectiles::offSpawned(token) srs.projectiles.offSpawned(token) → bool

onSpawned fires the instant the engine constructs a projectile — for every projectile in the scene, not just ones aimed at you.

C++: process-wide, takes no ScriptContext; returns a token (0 if the hook isn't installed) to pass to offSpawned. The callback (ProjectileSpawnedCallback = std::function<void(const ProjectileSpawnedEvent&)>) runs on the game thread, synchronously — keep it cheap and thread-safe.

Lua: fn receives a table {id, cycle, pos0, pos1, pos2, wallClock}. onSpawned returns a numeric token; pass it to offSpawned to unsubscribe.

Unsubscribing

srs.projectiles.offSpawned(token) removes the callback registered under that token. It is safe to call from inside the callback itself (one-shot listeners). Returns false for an unknown or already-removed token. A full script reload still clears all subscriptions automatically, so a register-once-at-load callback needs no explicit cleanup.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
ProjectileEntry (read-only):

Field Type Notes id int32 This client's spotanim cache id animationId int32 anim_id resolved from the proj def framesUntilLanding int32 Negative if already landed ticksUntilLanding int32 ceil(framesUntilLanding / 30) absoluteEndCycle int32 Raw absEnd (compare with engine frameStamp) packedBytes uint32 Opaque trajectory metadata (slope/dist)

ProjectileSpawnedEvent (C++; Lua receives the equivalent table):

struct ProjectileSpawnedEvent {
    int32_t id = 0;
    int32_t cycle = 0;
    int32_t pos0 = 0, pos1 = 0, pos2 = 0;
    int32_t field280 = 0, field288 = 0, field290 = 0;
    int64_t wallClock_ms = 0;
};

Fields beyond id are still being mapped — treat them as provisional.

docs.title: Example
RunePouch
docs.text:
srs::api::RunePouch / srs.runepouch

Read the rune pouch contents via VarClient varbits. All slots (regular + divine) are exposed; slots that don't exist on the player's pouch return rune id 0.

Each slot is two varbits: TYPE (rune item id) and QUANTITY (1..16k). IDs lifted from RuneLite gameval/VarbitID.java.

Read-only

Modifying the pouch goes through the rune-pouch widget UI (group 190) — that's a separate facade if/when needed.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:

hasPouch checks 4 item ids against the inventory + worn (cheap).

contents returns up to 6 entries (4 standard + 2 divine) — empty slots are omitted, so .size() equals the number of active runes.

docs.title: Example
Script lifecycle
docs.text:
script.* / log.* / srs.wait (Lua — global tables)

Everything a Lua script uses to hook into the engine: lifecycle callbacks, script metadata + settings, logging, tick suspension, and the sandboxed module loader. There is no srs::api facade for this surface — C++ plugins implement the IScript virtuals (onLoad / onTick / pulse / onDraw) directly instead.

docs.title: Lifecycle callbacks
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Per-frame callback (~60 Hz) script.pulse(fn) Runs every render frame Per-game-tick callback (~600 ms) script.onTick(fn) Runs once per server tick One-shot next-tick callback script.nextTick(fn) Fires once on the next tick rollover Overlay draw callback script.draw(fn) Per-frame, inside a live ImGui frame — srs.draw / srs.overlay are only valid here

pulse and onTick are both optional — register whichever cadence fits. Use onTick for game logic (actions, state machines) and pulse only when you genuinely need frame-rate polling.

docs.title: Metadata and settings
docs.text: Method Lua Notes Declare settings schema script.declareSettings(schemaTable) Top-level only — silently no-ops outside script load Declare script info script.declareInfo({name=, author=, version=, description=}) Top-level only Read current settings script.settings() → table Empty table if the calling script can't be attributed Settings-changed callback script.onSettingsChanged(fn(settingsTable)) Fires when the user edits settings in the client UI

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Info line log.info(msg) Appends [INFO] msg to the engine output buffer Warning line log.warn(msg) [WARN] prefix Error line log.error(msg) [ERROR] prefix Print print(...) Overridden: tab-concatenated tostring() of each arg, to the engine output buffer — not stdout

The only logging APIs

log.info/warn/error and the overridden print are the whole surface. There is no srs.log.* and no osrs.print — code using those names errors at call time.

docs.title: Waits (tick suspension)
docs.text:
Method Lua Notes Wait N ticks srs.wait([ticks=1]) Mutes this script for N ticks Wait for condition srs.waitUntil(predicateFn[, timeoutTicks=0]) timeoutTicks=0 = no timeout

wait is a suspension gate, not a coroutine sleep

srs.wait(n) mutes this script's pulse / onTick / nextTick callbacks for n ticks — draw keeps firing. It does not interrupt the currently running callback: code after the call still executes. The idiom is srs.wait(n); return. Both wait and waitUntil are silent no-ops outside a firing callback.

  • srs.waitUntil(fn) releases when the predicate returns truthy; if the predicate throws, the wait releases (fail-open) rather than hanging the script.
  • There is no global sleep or scriptSleep.

docs.title: Module loading (require)
docs.text:
require(mod) is replaced with a sandboxed bundle loader:

  • require("a.b") resolves a/b.lua, then a/b/init.lua, from the current bundle's in-memory files only — no filesystem access, no loadlib.
  • Results are cached per bundle; requiring the same module twice returns the cached value.
  • Calling require outside a bundle context (e.g. from a single-file script) or for a missing module throws an error.

docs.title: Available Lua stdlib
docs.text: Open libraries: base, string, math, table, os. Not available: io, package (require is replaced — see above).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
script.declareInfo{ name = "Miner", author = "me", version = "1.0",
                    description = "Powermines iron" }

script.onTick(function()
    if srs.inventory.isFull() then
        srs.inventory.dropAll("Iron ore")
        srs.wait(2)  -- mute onTick for 2 ticks; code below still runs
        return
    end
    log.info("Ticking, slots free: " .. srs.inventory.emptySlots())
end)

script.draw(function()
    -- srs.draw / srs.overlay calls are valid only here
end)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
srs::api::Settings / srs.settings

Read game settings via varbits / varps / varc. The toggle (write) side requires a widget-id table per setting; this module currently exposes only the read half plus a few named convenience helpers.

docs.title: Raw reads
docs.text:
Each reader has a "soft" variant (0 / -1 on miss) and a "present?-aware" variant (returns optional / nil).

Method C++ Lua Raw varbit (0 on miss) Settings::varbit(ctx, id) → int32 srs.settings.varbit(id) → int Varbit, present?-aware Settings::tryVarbit(ctx, id) → optional<int32> srs.settings.tryVarbit(id) → int \| nil Raw varp Settings::varp(ctx, id) → int32 srs.settings.varp(id) → int Varp, present?-aware Settings::tryVarp(ctx, id) → optional<int32> srs.settings.tryVarp(id) → int \| nil Raw varc int (-1 on miss) Settings::varcInt(ctx, id) → int32 srs.settings.varcInt(id) → int Varc, present?-aware Settings::tryVarcInt(ctx, id) → optional<int32> srs.settings.tryVarcInt(id) → int \| nil

The varc getter already returns -1 as its "missing or wrong type" sentinel, so the raw variant gives -1 for both "not wired" and "unset".

docs.text:
Populated as widget/varbit IDs are confirmed against RuneLite. Conservative defaults (false / 0) when unresolved.

Value Spellbook 0 Standard 1 Ancient 2 Lunar 3 Arceuus

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
C++Lua 
using namespace srs::api;
if (!Settings::isRunEnabled(ctx) && Player::runEnergy(ctx) > 4000) {
    Player::toggleRunEnergy(ctx, true);
}
int32_t book = Settings::spellbook(ctx);   // 0 = Standard

if not srs.settings.isRunEnabled() and srs.player.runEnergy() > 4000 then
    srs.player.toggleRunEnergy(true)
end
-- raw varbit read with a present?-aware variant
local v = srs.settings.tryVarbit(4070)
if v ~= nil then
    log.info("spellbook varbit = " .. v)
end

docs.title: Shop
docs.text:
srs::api::Shop / srs.shop

Read shop stock and click buy/sell quantity selectors. Stock lives in container id 300 (matches the widget group). Quantity selectors are shared between buy and sell — pick a quantity, then click an item in the shop (buy) or in the player inventory (sell).

Per-item buy/sell deferred

Per-item buy / sell clicks have the same dynamic-children rect issue as Bank slots. The quantity selectors and bulk-state queries are here; per-item invokes can come later via menu-action recipe.

Spells
docs.text:
srs::api::Spells / srs.spells

Static metadata for OSRS spells. Pure data; casting logic lives in Magic.

The current table is a representative seed — common combat spells, alchemy, and a handful of teleports. Extend as needed; we deliberately don't mirror RuneLite's full Spell enum on day one.

docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Spell metadata Spells::info(s) → SpellInfo srs.spells.info(s) → SpellInfo Lookup by name Spells::byName(name) → optional<SpellInfo> srs.spells.byName(name) → SpellInfo \| nil Enum lookup by name Spells::idByName(name) → optional<Spell> srs.spells.idByName(name) → int \| nil All spells in a book Spells::inBook(book) → vector<SpellInfo> srs.spells.inBook(book) → table

docs.title: Tab
docs.text:
srs::api::Tab / srs.tab

Authoritative source for "which sidebar tab is open right now", mirroring Microbot's Rs2Tab.

Tab state lives in VarClient at index TOPLEVEL_PANEL (171). Reading it is stricter than the open-iface map (which only says the inventory IfType is loaded, not that it's the active tab).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method C++ Lua Current tab enum Tab::current(ctx) → InterfaceTab srs.tab.current() → int Is given tab open Tab::isOpen(ctx, tab) → bool srs.tab.isOpen(tab) → bool Switch to tab Tab::switchTo(ctx, tab) → bool srs.tab.switchTo(tab) → bool Raw varc value Tab::rawIndex(ctx) → int32 srs.tab.rawIndex() → int AWT VK code for tab hotkey Tab::hotkeyVk(ctx, tab) → int srs.tab.hotkeyVk(tab) → int

docs.title: switchTo contract
docs.text:
1. If current(ctx) == tab → return true immediately (no-op).
  2. Read the AWT VK code from the player's STONE_*_KEY varbit for this tab. If bound, inject it as a press+release via the keyboard ring — closest to real player behavior.
  3. If no hotkey is bound (varbit unset / snapshot not warmed) or the keypress can't be delivered (pre-login, GS unresolved), fall back to a spoofed click on the chrome tab widget. The chrome (group, child) pair is resolved from the live display mode (Fixed=548 / ResizableClassic=161 / ResizableModern=164).

hotkeyVk returns 0 if unbound (or if the varbit snapshot hasn't refreshed yet). Useful for "Inventory tab bound to: F4" UI or gating switchTo.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
InterfaceTab (InterfaceTab / srs.tab.*):

Lua const Value Tab UNKNOWN -1 VarClient not ready / pre-login NOTHING_SELECTED 0 No tab (fullscreen interface up) COMBAT 1 Combat SKILLS 2 Skills QUESTS 3 Quests INVENTORY 4 Inventory EQUIPMENT 5 Equipment PRAYER 6 Prayer MAGIC 7 Magic CHAT_CHANNEL 8 Chat channel FRIENDS 9 Friends ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT 10 Account management LOGOUT 11 Logout SETTINGS 12 Settings EMOTES 13 Emotes MUSIC 14 Music

Raw varc values don't match enum

The underlying varc value is 0-based and DOES NOT match this enum's ordinal — see Tab.cpp::current() for the conversion. The raw values mirror Microbot's InterfaceTab.varcIntIndex (e.g. Combat=0, Inventory=3, AccMan=8, Friends=9, Logout=10). The value -1 means "no tab selected" (fullscreen interface up, or pre-login).

docs.title: Example
Tile
docs.text:
srs::api::Tile / srs.tile

Collision queries against the active scene CollisionMap. Coordinates are world tile coords. Plane defaults to 0 (ground).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Walkable Tile::isWalkable(ctx, x, y, plane=0) → bool srs.tile.isWalkable(x, y, plane?) → bool In loaded scene Tile::isInScene(ctx, x, y) → bool srs.tile.isInScene(x, y) → bool Can step between tiles Tile::canTraverse(ctx, fx, fy, tx, ty, plane=0) → bool srs.tile.canTraverse(fx, fy, tx, ty, plane?) → bool Reachable on foot Tile::isReachable(ctx, x, y, plane=0) → bool srs.tile.isReachable(x, y, plane?) → bool Tile render height Tile::height(ctx, x, y, plane=0) → optional<int> srs.tile.height(x, y, plane?) → int \| nil Raw flag bits Tile::flags(ctx, x, y, plane=0) → uint32 srs.tile.flags(x, y, plane?) → int

flags returns the raw collision bitfield. Decode against CollisionMap flag constants for blocked-N/E/S/W and similar.

docs.title: isReachable — same-floor / can-I-path-there test
docs.text:
Breadth-first flood-fill from the player's current tile over the live collision map (canTraverse edges); the tile is reachable iff the fill reaches it. The fill is cached per (player tile, scene), so many queries in one tick share one computation.

This is the correct test where plane can't help. The classic case is the Motherlode Mine: its upper level is plane 0 exactly like the ground floor, but the two are only joined by a ladder — so an upper-floor ore vein / hopper is not walk-reachable from the lower floor and isReachable returns false for it. This mirrors RuneLite/Microbot nearestReachable(); filter object candidates through it instead of trusting plane.

Returns false pre-scene, off-scene, or when plane differs from the player's current plane (a different plane needs a transport, not a walk).

-- Only mine veins we can actually path to (skips the floor above us).
local reachable = {}
for _, v in ipairs(srs.gameobject.byId(26661)) do
    if srs.tile.isReachable(v.tileX, v.tileY, v.plane) then
        reachable[#reachable + 1] = v
    end
end

docs.title: height — render height for floor detection
docs.text:
Engine render height at the tile's SW corner (RuneLite getTileHeights[plane][x][y]), in world units. Where plane is ambiguous (MLM again — both floors are plane 0), the height differs by hundreds of units, so comparing the player's tile height against a threshold tells the floors apart (Microbot's isUpperFloor() uses exactly this with a -490 cutoff). nil pre-scene / off-scene.

For higher-level pathing (multi-tile A*, transports, stall recovery) use Walk instead — Tile is for spot collision checks.

docs.title: Walk
docs.text:
srs::api::Walk / srs.walk + legacy game.* walkers

Navigation API covering full pathfinding, single-tile clicks, and safe-tile selection. Two Lua namespaces exist side by side:

  • srs.walk — wraps the srs::api::Walk facade (to / cancel / isMoving / hasArrived / state / arrivalDistance).
  • game.* — legacy walkers (moveTo, walkTo, minimapWalkTo, walkFastCanvas, walkSmart, findSafeTile, isWalkable) bound directly against PathExecutor / collision internals. They drive the same executor but are not routed through the Walk facade.

All calls are safe no-ops (returning false / true depending on intent) when the executor isn't wired (pre-init host).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method C++ Lua Path-routed walk (hybrid) Walk::to(ctx, x, y, useTransports=true) → bool srs.walk.to(x, y[, useTransports]) → boolgame.moveTo(x, y[, useTransports]) → bool Path-routed walk, cross-plane Walk::to(ctx, x, y, useTransports, plane) → bool srs.walk.to(x, y[, useTransports], plane) → bool Path-routed canvas walk — game.walkTo(x, y[, useTransports]) → bool Path-routed minimap walk — game.minimapWalkTo(x, y[, useTransports]) → bool Single-click canvas walk Walk::fastCanvas(ctx, x, y, plane=-1) → bool game.walkFastCanvas(x, y[, plane]) → bool Smart auto-dispatch Walk::walkSmart(ctx, x, y, plane=-1) → bool game.walkSmart(x, y[, plane]) → bool Find a safe walkable tile Walk::findSafeTile(ctx, originX, originY, danger, searchRadius, plane=-1) → SafeTile game.findSafeTile(originX, originY, danger[, radius[, plane]]) → table \| nil (adapter over the facade — see below) Stop walking Walk::cancel(ctx) srs.walk.cancel() / game.cancelMove() Currently walking Walk::isMoving(ctx) → bool srs.walk.isMoving() / game.isMoving() → bool At goal Walk::hasArrived(ctx) → bool srs.walk.hasArrived() / game.hasArrived() → bool Walk lifecycle state Walk::state(ctx) → Walk::State srs.walk.state() → string Distance at arrival Walk::arrivalDistance(ctx) → int32 srs.walk.arrivalDistance() → int Tile walkable? — game.isWalkable(x, y) → bool

docs.title: srs.walk.to overloads (Lua)
docs.text:
Lua exposes four overloads — the type of the third argument (bool vs int) disambiguates:

srs.walk.to(x, y)                        -- current floor, transports on
srs.walk.to(x, y, useTransports)         -- bool arg 3
srs.walk.to(x, y, plane)                 -- int arg 3: cross-plane
srs.walk.to(x, y, useTransports, plane)  -- full form

plane 0..3 routes via stairs/ladders to the target floor; -1 means the current floor.

docs.title: state / arrivalDistance
docs.text:
state reports the walk lifecycle. Lua maps the enum to a string: "idle", "waitingForPath", "walking", "arrived", "unreachable". Unreachable means the walk terminated without arriving — pick a different goal; don't retry the same one in a loop.

arrivalDistance is the Chebyshev distance to the goal at the moment the most recent walk arrived: 0 = exact tile, > 0 = settled nearby, -1 = no walk has arrived yet.

docs.title: Which dispatch should I use?
docs.text: Scenario Use Long-distance navigation, may need transports/multi-leg srs.walk.to / game.moveTo Force minimap clicks (long-haul behavior even close-up) game.minimapWalkTo Force canvas clicks throughout the path game.walkTo Short, time-critical dodge (1–2 ticks, single tile) game.walkFastCanvas "Just get me there, I don't care how" game.walkSmart Pick the closest safe tile, then walk there game.findSafeTile + game.walkSmart

docs.title: walkFastCanvas — single-click, no client pathfinding
docs.text:
Fires one canvas "Walk here" click at the destination tile and returns immediately. The OSRS server resolves the route, the client does no A*.

Use this for short, time-critical movements where you need a single click to fire on the current tick (dodging a falling-rocks tile, side-stepping a tick-attack hitbox).

Behavior:

  • Returns false if the tile is off-viewport (the engine can't click what it can't see). Camera angle matters — tiles behind the player or above the screen edge don't project.
  • No path validation. If a wall sits between you and the target, the server walks around it (or refuses); the client has no opinion.
  • No arrival polling. It's fire-and-forget. Re-check srs.player.position() next tick if you need to confirm.
  • plane defaults to the player's current plane.
-- Side-step east by one tile, immediately.
local p = srs.player.position()
game.walkFastCanvas(p.x + 1, p.y, p.plane)

docs.title: walkSmart — automatic dispatch
docs.text:
Picks walkFastCanvas if the target tile projects onto the canvas, otherwise falls back to the hybrid path executor (Walk::to).

-- Caller doesn't need to know whether the tile is visible.
game.walkSmart(targetX, targetY)

Returns true if a walk was dispatched. Useful when you have a target tile from some computation (findSafeTile, a script's own planning, etc.) and don't care which dispatch path is used.

docs.title: findSafeTile — pick the closest walkable tile not in danger
docs.text:
One shared implementation

Walk::findSafeTile (C++, returns a SafeTile struct) and the Lua game.findSafeTile (returns a table or nil) now share a single ring-search implementation — the Lua binding is a thin adapter over the Walk facade, so the two cannot diverge. The Lua contract is unchanged: {x, y, plane, onCanvas, walkable} or nil where C++ reports valid = false, and danger entries without a plane key default to the search plane. The Lua form is documented on the legacy game.* table page; the description below is the shared contract.

Searches outward by Chebyshev distance from (originX, originY) for the closest tile that satisfies all of:

  1. Not in the dangerTiles list (plane-aware match).
  2. Walkable according to the live collision map.
  3. Preferably on the current canvas (one-click reachable).

The origin tile itself is skipped — call this when the origin is the problem. If multiple candidates tie on distance, on-canvas tiles win (so the result can usually be reached via walkFastCanvas). If the search exhausts without finding any on-canvas safe tile, the closest off-canvas safe tile is returned (so walkSmart can fall back to the path executor for the multi-tick approach).

Arguments:

Arg Default Notes originX, originY — Where to search around (usually the player's current tile). dangerTiles — List of {x=, y=, plane=} tables. plane defaults to the search plane if omitted. radius 5 Search radius in tiles (Chebyshev). Capped at 32. plane -1 Search plane. -1 uses the player's current plane.

Returns — C++ gets a SafeTile struct:

struct SafeTile {
    bool valid = false;      // false = no candidate met the constraints
    int32_t x = 0, y = 0, plane = 0;
    bool onCanvas = false;   // projects onto the current canvas
    bool walkable = false;
};

Check valid before using the coordinates. Lua (game.findSafeTile) returns the equivalent table — but returns nil instead of a valid=false record:

{ x=…, y=…, plane=…, onCanvas=true|false, walkable=true }

local p = srs.player.position()
local danger = { {x=p.x, y=p.y, plane=p.plane} }  -- I'm standing on it
local safe = game.findSafeTile(p.x, p.y, danger, 3)
if safe then
    game.walkSmart(safe.x, safe.y, safe.plane)
end

docs.title: to — full pathfinder
docs.text:
The original navigation API. Runs the local A* (or StaticPathfinder across regions) and executes the path with hybrid minimap/canvas clicks across multiple ticks. Handles transports automatically.

  • useTransports = true (default): doors, agility shortcuts, fairy rings, manholes, ladders, etc. are invoked as the path crosses them. Set false to force a walk-only path (free accounts, missing quest reqs).
  • Without a plane argument the walk targets the player's current floor. Pass the cross-plane overload (plane 0..3) to route via stairs/ladders to another floor; -1 = current floor.
  • hasArrived() returns true when no walk has been issued yet, or the executor reached PathExecutor::CLOSE_ENOUGH of the goal. It stays false after an Unreachable termination — poll srs.walk.state() to tell "arrived" from "gave up", and srs.walk.arrivalDistance() for how close the arrival actually got.
srs.walk.to(3210, 3210)
-- … later ticks …
if srs.walk.hasArrived() then
    doStuffAtDestination()
end

docs.title: Transports (full pathfinder only)
docs.text:
When useTransports = true, the executor handles:

  • Live object-tile resolution. The transport-table origin column is the player STAND tile, not the LocType's actual tile (the object often sits 1 tile off). The walker queries the live scene by object id at fire time so OPLOC1 packets aren't silently rejected.
  • Multi-step transport chains. Manholes (Open → Climb-down), levers-then-doors, and similar two-row entries with the same origin+destination are emitted as a chain. The walker advances through them when it detects the live object's id has flipped to the next step.
  • Recalculation on completion. After any transport (success or timeout), the executor re-plans from the player's actual landing tile.

If your character genuinely can't use a transport on the shortest route (missing agility level, no Lunar spellbook, etc.) and the pathfinder still tries to route through it, pass useTransports = false to force a walk-only path.

walkFastCanvas does not invoke transports — it's a one-shot canvas click, so anything more elaborate than "click this tile" needs the full pathfinder.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Walk::State (C++ enum; Lua srs.walk.state() returns the string):

C++ Lua string Meaning Idle "idle" No walk issued WaitingForPath "waitingForPath" Path request in flight Walking "walking" Executing the path Arrived "arrived" Reached the goal (or as close as possible) Unreachable "unreachable" Terminated without arriving — pick a different goal

SafeTile — see findSafeTile above for the struct definition and the Lua table shape.

docs.title: Widget
docs.text:
srs::api::Widget / srs.widget

Read-only inspection of the OSRS interface tree, plus a generic click. Widgets are identified by (groupId, childId) — matches RuneLite's WidgetID encoding.

docs.title: State / lookup
docs.text: Method C++ Lua IfTypeManager warmed up Widget::isReady(ctx) → bool srs.widget.isReady() → bool Find by (group, child) Widget::find(ctx, g, c) → optional<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.find(g, c) → WidgetSnapshot \| nil All in group Widget::group(ctx, g) → vector<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.group(g) → table Dynamic children Widget::dynamicChildren(ctx, g, c) → vector<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.dynamicChildren(g, c) → table RuneLite-style label Widget::label(g, c) → string srs.widget.label(g, c) → string

docs.title: Dynamic children
docs.text:
dynamicChildren enumerates the runtime-allocated IfTypes held in the parent's vector at IfType+0xB58. This is where inventory slots, bank items, dialogue options, etc. live; they don't appear in group() (which only walks the static Components array).

Each entry's dynIndex carries its array slot, parentGroupId/parentChildId point to (g, c), and text typically holds the option label or item-derived caption.

docs.title: label
docs.text:
Returns the most informative form available, in priority order:

  1. "Inventory.ITEMS" — exact InterfaceID nested constant
  2. "INVENTORY[0]" — group name + child index
  3. "149.0" — numeric fallback

docs.title: Visibility
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Interface rendering Widget::isOpen(ctx, g) → bool srs.widget.isOpen(g) → bool Drawn last frame Widget::isVisible(ctx, g, c) → bool srs.widget.isVisible(g, c) → bool Hidden (or ancestor hidden) Widget::isHidden(ctx, g, c) → bool srs.widget.isHidden(g, c) → bool Wait until rendered (poll) Widget::waitVisible(ctx, g, c, timeoutMs) → bool srs.widget.waitVisible(g, c, timeoutMs) → bool

isVisible returns true iff the engine actually drew the widget last frame (hook-snapshot path). The renderer skips any widget whose own or any ancestor's Hidden flag is set, so this matches RuneLite's recursive Widget.isHidden() semantics for free.

Defaults on lookup-miss mirror the Java helpers exactly:

  • isVisible(g, c) → false when widget can't be found
  • isHidden(g, c) → true when widget can't be found

waitVisible polls until (g, c) is actually rendered or timeoutMs elapses, returning the final visibility. Use it to gate keyboard entry on a prompt being open — typing into an unrendered box is silently dropped.

docs.title: Hit-test
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Hit-test screen point Widget::atPoint(ctx, sx, sy) → optional<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.atPoint(sx, sy) → WidgetSnapshot \| nil Currently hovered Widget::hovered(ctx) → optional<WidgetSnapshot> srs.widget.hovered() → WidgetSnapshot \| nil

Rect fields are absolute screen coords for these two methods.

docs.title: Scrolling
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Read scroll position Widget::scrollY(ctx, g, c) → optional<int32> srs.widget.scrollY(g, c) → int \| nil Write scroll position Widget::setScrollY(ctx, g, c, y) → bool srs.widget.setScrollY(g, c, y) → bool

scrollY reads a scrollable widget's vertical scroll offset (nil if it isn't resolved / allocated yet). setScrollY writes it — the engine picks it up on the next render frame — clamped to [0, max(0, scrollHeight − height)]. The visible scrollbar thumb is painted by a separate CS2 script we don't invoke, so the thumb may look stale until the mouse moves, but items inside the viewport reflect the new offset immediately. Backs Bank::scrollToSlot.

docs.title: Click
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Click action Widget::click(ctx, g, c, action) → bool srs.widget.click(g, c, action) → bool Click a specific op (X-aware) Widget::clickOp(ctx, g, c, op, actionIndex, action, itemId = -1) → bool srs.widget.clickOp(g, c, op, actionIndex, action[, itemId=-1]) → bool Native CS2-button click (by position) Widget::clickFire(ctx, g, c) → bool — Real-input click (whole widget) Widget::clickReal(ctx, g, c) → bool srs.widget.clickReal(g, c) → bool Real-input click (dynamic child) Widget::clickRealDynChild(ctx, g, c, dynIndex) → bool srs.widget.clickRealDynChild(g, c, dynIndex) → bool Real-input click (sub-rect) Widget::clickRealAt(ctx, g, c, dx, dy, w, h) → bool srs.widget.clickRealAt(g, c, dx, dy, w, h) → bool

click resolves the widget's absolute screen rect via the live IfRender capture, picks a random point in the rect, and routes through Interact (always-on spoof + DoAction). For inventory slots prefer Inventory::interact — same mechanism, narrower API.

clickOp is the X-aware sibling of click: it exposes the two DoAction fields click hard-codes — op (the menu sub-op selector; -1 = none) and actionIndex (the spawn index; 1 for almost all widget actions, 2 for GE coin-collect). itemId carries the item context (-1 for plain buttons). Always dispatched as a CC_OP (menu slot 57); the action string is used only for the entity text + the ~600 ms dedupe key (keyed on (slot, group, child, op, action)), so space repeated identical sub-op clicks ≥ 1 tick apart.

Clicking Grand Exchange buttons

Some CS2 buttons — every Grand Exchange offer / stepper / confirm / collect button — need the engine to build their hover context itself, so a synthesized DoAction no-ops on them. Use clickFire (native click dispatcher; op resolved by position, so the widget's rect must land on the intended button) or the clickReal* family (drives the real WndProc input pipeline — a curved WM_MOUSEMOVE then WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP to a random point in the rect; focus-independent and background / multi-client safe). The clickReal* calls block until the move + click finishes and return false if the widget isn't rendered this frame. clickRealDynChild targets a parent-relative dynamic child (search-result rows, side-inventory cells, steppers); clickRealAt targets a widget-relative sub-rect (icons that aren't separately hit-testable, e.g. an empty GE box's Buy icon). These mostly back the Grand Exchange facade — prefer that surface.

docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Raw IfType pointer — (raw WidgetQuery::resolveIfType) srs.widget.address(g, c) → int \| nil

Diagnostic only — patch-unstable

srs.widget.address returns the raw IfType* for a widget so probe scripts can inspect engine memory. It has no C++ facade counterpart, the layout behind the pointer changes across game patches, and it exists to feed the deprecated mem.* probe workflow. Never use it in production scripts.

World
docs.text:
srs::api::World / srs.world

Current world / server number.

The world int (e.g. 302, 398) is stored in the GS struct at GameSDK::Offsets::GlobalState::WorldId (= 0x321C). This API just wraps GameData::worldId() so plugins / Lua can read it without touching memory directly.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method C++ Lua Current world id World::getId(ctx) → int32 srs.world.getId() → int Seamless world hop World::hopTo(ctx, world) → bool srs.world.hopTo(world) → bool

getId returns -1 if GS isn't resolved or the value is the pre-login sentinel.

hopTo performs a seamless in-game world switch (the native world-switcher — no logout). It is scheduled onto the engine main thread, so it returns as soon as the hop is accepted, not when the new world finishes loading — poll getId() / Game::state() for completion. Returns false (nothing scheduled) when not logged in, when world is the current world, when world isn't a known world, or when the engine isn't resolved. Must be logged in; for a members world the account must be a member (the engine silently rejects ineligible targets).
